title: fix(ci): repair the mobile showcase screenshots workflow
body:
## Summary

The Mobile Showcase Screenshots workflow has been failing since #4802 ([failed run](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30589747280)). Fixing it surfaced one CI bug and two latent startup races in the showcase harness (previously masked by slower runners):

1. **Workflow install filter missed the server package.** #4802 switched to `pnpm install --filter=@t3tools/mobile... --filter=@t3tools/scripts...`, but `scripts/mobile-showcase.ts` boots the T3 server from `apps/server/src/bin.ts`, whose package is named `t3` and is in neither filter graph. The server crashed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: @effect/platform-node` and both jobs timed out waiting for the server port. Fixed by adding `--filter=t3...` to both jobs.

2. **environment-id read raced server startup.** The server begins listening before its `ServerEnvironment` layer persists `userdata/environment-id`; the script read the file once right after `waitForPort` and died with ENOENT on the fast macOS runner. Now polls for non-empty content with the same timeout discipline as `waitForPort`.

3. **Database seeding raced server migrations.** `seedDatabase` deletes from and reseeds projection tables as soon as the port opens, but migrations weren't done yet — `no such table: projection_pending_approvals`. Now polls `sqlite_master` for all seeded tables before touching the database.

## Verification

Workflow runs dispatched on this branch:
- [Run 1](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30590570253) (after fix 1): Android fully green; iOS exposed race 2.
- [Run 2](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30591618971) (after fix 2): Android green again; iOS exposed race 3.
- [Run 3](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30592613967) (after fix 3, iOS only): ✅ green.
- [Run 4](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30593265494) (all platforms): iOS ✅; Android hit an emulator flake (first capture's 'thread' scene never rendered; app bundled but got no data — same commit passed before and after).
- [Run 5](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30594069517) (Android only, same commit): ✅ green — confirms run 4 was a flake.
- [Run 6](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30594882520) (all platforms, both appearances): ✅ **fully green**, both artifact sets uploaded (app-store-connect-screenshots 9.7 MB, google-play-screenshots 6.5 MB).

Also passing locally: `pnpm --filter @t3tools/scripts typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @t3tools/scripts test` (197 tests).

title: fix(ci): capture iPad App Store screenshots in landscape
body:
## Summary

- capture the iPad 13-inch App Store showcase in landscape at 2752×2064
- rotate Simulator after the app launches, then restore portrait during cleanup
- leave the existing M5 simulator target, iPhone captures, and app configuration unchanged

## Why

The screenshot workflow currently captures the iPad App Store target in portrait. Simulator keeps the raw screenshot framebuffer at its portrait dimensions even while the app is running in landscape, so the harness now rotates the live simulator for capture and normalizes the resulting PNG before validating it.

## Verification

- `vp test run scripts/mobile-showcase.test.ts` (19 tests)
- `vp run --filter @t3tools/scripts typecheck`
- targeted formatting and `git diff --check`
- clean local iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) build and showcase capture
- visually verified the generated screenshot is upright landscape at 2752×2064
- verified cleanup restores the reused simulator to portrait at 2064×2752

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] No mobile app or simulator configuration changes
- [x] No generated screenshots committed

Model: GPT-5.6 Sol | Harness: Codex in T3 Code


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes only affect local/CI screenshot automation on macOS and add AppleScript/UI coupling to Simulator, but do not touch the mobile app or production server paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> The mobile showcase harness now supports **per-device iOS orientation** so the iPad 13-inch App Store slot can be captured in **landscape at 2752×2064** instead of portrait.
> 
> **Config and docs:** `ShowcaseIosDevice` gains an optional `orientation` (default portrait). The `ipad-13` device is set to landscape with swapped upload dimensions. Operations docs and config comments reflect the landscape iPad slot.
> 
> **Capture flow:** After launching the showcase app on a landscape device, the runner drives Simulator via **AppleScript** (`setIosSimulatorOrientation`) to pick Portrait or Landscape Right. Raw `simctl io` screenshots are **rotated 90° with `sips`** so PNGs match App Store orientation. Cleanup restores portrait on reused simulators when landscape was used.
> 
> **Tests:** Default device matrix expectations now include iOS orientation and the updated iPad dimensions.

title: fix(ci): rotate iPad showcase captures without Simulator UI scripting
body:
## Summary

The Mobile Showcase Screenshots workflow's iOS job fails on main ([run](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30615503912)): #5065 rotates the iPad simulator by AppleScript-clicking Simulator's menus, and the CI runner denies osascript the required macOS Accessibility permission:

```
execution error: System Events got an error: osascript is not allowed assistive access. (-1719)
```

`simctl` has no orientation command (checked through Xcode 26.5), so this replaces UI scripting with in-app rotation. Getting there surfaced a chain of iPadOS constraints; the fix has four pieces:

1. **In-app rotation.** `t3-native-controls` gains `getShowcaseOrientation` (reads a `--showcaseOrientation` launch arg the harness now passes), `applyShowcaseOrientation` (`UIWindowScene.requestGeometryUpdate`), and `getInterfaceOrientation` so `ShowcaseCaptureCoordinator` can verify the rotation took effect and retry. Scene readiness is gated on the orientation having settled, and the orientation getter reports from **screen bounds** (which mirror the captured framebuffer) — a failed rotation now times out loudly instead of shipping wrong-size screenshots.
2. **iPadOS ignores programmatic orientation for multitasking-capable apps**, so the capture build sets `requireFullScreen` in `app.config.ts`, gated on `T3_SHOWCASE_CAPTURE_BUILD=1` which only the showcase harness sets — production builds are unchanged. (The Expo config key really is `requireFullScreen` in config-plugins 56; the `requiresFullScreen` spelling is silently ignored.)
3. **iPadOS 26 windowing** runs a requires-full-screen app in a fixed portrait compatibility window, so before landscape captures the harness switches the simulator to Full Screen Apps mode via `simctl spawn defaults` — writing all **three** SpringBoard keys the Settings toggle writes (`SBChamoisWindowingEnabled`, `SBMedusaMultitaskingEnabled`, `SBFlexibleWindowingPreviouslyEnabledAutomaticStageCreation`; the first alone is ignored on a freshly created device), then reboots the device and verifies the mode stuck.
4. **Headless displays don't rotate.** With Simulator.app attached the display rotates with the app and screenshots come out natively 2752×2064; a headless CI simulator keeps its display portrait with the app rendered sideways inside it. The harness detects which case it got from the PNG dimensions and post-rotates 270° only when needed.

The osascript helper and the unconditional `sips --rotate 90` are gone.

## Verification

- [iOS CI run on this branch](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30624337401): ✅ green — all 6 captures × 5 scenes; iPad artifacts confirmed upright landscape 2752×2064 by inspection.
- [Full both-platform run](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/30625175356): final verification.
- Locally verified end-to-end against a freshly created simulator (the CI-equivalent path), plus `@t3tools/scripts`/`@t3tools/mobile` typechecks and the 197 scripts tests.

title: fix(server): self-update no longer rolls itself back on restart
body: ## Problem Remote server updates on boot-service (systemd) machines fail at the resume step: download and install succeed, then the client reports "The server did not resume on t3@" and the server comes back on the **old** version. The updater runs `systemctl --user restart` from inside the service being restarted. systemd's default `KillMode=control-group` SIGTERMs the entire cgroup — including that `systemctl` child — so the blocking restart call dies mid-flight. The updater interprets the dead child as a failed restart and its rollback handler rewrites the unit back to the previous version while the old server process is still in its multi-second graceful shutdown. systemd then starts the unit pointing at the old install. The freshly installed target version is left on disk, unused, and every retry hits the same race. Observed on bb-1 (two consecutive failures, `0.0.32-nightly.20260730.956 → 0.0.32-nightly.20260731.963`): the boot log shows "Server self-update installed; restarting boot service" followed ~2s later by "Server self-update could not restart the boot service", and the unit file's mtime matches the rollback write. ## Fix Queue the restart with `systemctl --user restart --no-block`. It enqueues the job and exits before the stop signal reaches the cgroup, so its exit code only reflects whether systemd accepted the job. The existing rollback path is unchanged and now fires only for genuine rejections (bad unit, unreachable manager) — the case it was written for — instead of for the updater's own death. Updated the two test assertions on the restart argv; the rollback-on-failure and retry tests pass unchanged. --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Claude Fable 5) --- --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes critical remote self-update handoff on systemd hosts (unit rewrite + restart timing and concurrency lock), though scope is limited to the boot-service path and rollback behavior is intentionally preserved for real failures. > > **Overview** > Fixes boot-service self-updates that **rolled back to the old version** after install succeeded. The updater ran a **blocking** `systemctl --user restart` from inside the unit being restarted; systemd SIGTERM’d the shared cgroup and killed that `systemctl` child, which was treated as restart failure and restored the previous unit file. > > **Restart** now uses `systemctl --user restart --no-block` so the job is queued and the command exits before the stop signal. Rollback on non-zero exit still applies only when systemd genuinely rejects the job. > > The **in-flight update lock** is no longer cleared on every restart fiber completion (`Effect.ensuring` removed). It is released only when restart fails after rollback, because `--no-block` returns while this process is still shutting down—holding the lock blocks a second update from rewriting the unit mid-teardown. Tests assert `--no-block` on restart argv and that a concurrent update is rejected after a successful queued restart. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 001b2c4adde95d98b96b53d42f397290d4089332. The boot-service path now releases the lock only on the failure path after rollback completes, so a queued-but-outstanding restart keeps the lock held until systemd replaces the process. title: feat(web): configurable fonts and sizes under Settings → Appearance
body:
## What changed

Settings → Appearance gains a **Fonts** section: four surfaces, each with a family picker and a size slider, a live preview rendered in the resolved family and size, and a per-row reset.

| Setting | Covers | Size range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Interface font** | everything outside code blocks and the terminal | 12–20px |
| **Prompt font** | the composer textarea and its placeholder only | 12–20px |
| **Code font** | code blocks, diffs, and file previews | 10–18px |
| **Terminal font** | terminal output | 8–20px |

The family pickers are grouped by category (Sans serif / Monospace) and filtered to faces that are actually installed, probed with canvas metrics — `document.fonts.check()` reports `true` for absent families, so it cannot filter anything. "Custom…" accepts any name: it edits a local draft that commits 400ms after typing pauses (or on Enter/blur) and only once the name resolves, so the applied font holds while a partial name is typed.

**Cell-grid surfaces stay monospace.** The terminal draws on a fixed cell lattice, so a proportional face renders its text narrower than its own cells and strands the cursor to the right. The Code and Terminal pickers offer monospace faces only, and the renderer independently measures the requested family and falls back to the default when it is not monospace, so a previously stored value cannot leave the terminal in that state.

**The terminal size adapts to its canvas.** The preference is a ceiling: narrow panes (splits, the side panel) slide the rendered size down until a classic 80-column grid fits, down to an 8px legibility floor, and widening slides it back up. The measurement lives in `fit()`, so drags, splits, and window resizes all pass through it.

**The composer context strip degrades instead of colliding.** Its controls truncate, and once even truncated labels cannot fit they animate shut to icons (measured from laid-out content, with hysteresis, restoring as space returns).

Under the hood:

- eight client settings in the contracts schema (four families, four sizes), persisted client-side like the other appearance preferences, all covered by Restore defaults
- the `--font-sans` / `--font-mono` theme tokens move out of `@theme inline` so Tailwind utilities reference the variables; `body`, `pre`/`code`, and the `@pierre/diffs` shadow-root hooks route through them
- the interface size drives the root font size (and with it every rem-based dimension); prompt and code sizes stay in absolute pixels so they do not scale twice
- custom names are normalized and quoted before reaching CSS or the canvas font shorthand, where an unquoted non-ident name silently voids the whole declaration
- font application survives async settings hydration, including terminals created while settings were still loading

🟡 **Medium** `src/appearanceFonts.ts:121`

`isFontFamilyAvailable` returns `true` for fonts that are not installed, so `availableFontOptions` keeps them in the dropdown. `document.fonts.check()` resolves against the configured font fallback list, so a family like `Fira Code` that is absent on the user's machine still reports as available — it will silently render the fallback font instead. Selecting such an option then produces a different font than the one shown, defeating the availability filter. If the user changes the terminal font while `GhosttyTerminalSurface.create` is pending, the new font is written to `terminalFontFamilyRef` but never applied to the live terminal — it keeps the old font until another font change or remount. The font-change effect runs while `terminalRef.current` is still `null`, so its `setFont` call is skipped, and after the async `create` completes using the old snapshot no effect reapplies the newer value. Consider re-reading `terminalFontFamilyRef.current` after `create` resolves and calling `setFont` if it differs from what was passed at construction.

🟡 **Medium** `hooks/useLocalStorage.ts:152` Functional updates passed to `setValue` are evaluated immediately against the render-captured `storedValue` rather than against the latest pending value. When `setValue(v => ...)` is called twice before React re-renders (e.g., two updates in the same event handler), both callbacks receive the same stale value and the second write overwrites the first — two boolean toggles leave the value toggled instead of cancelling, and the first increment/append update is silently lost. The `setValue` callback closes over `storedValue` from the current render, so it never reflects values queued by prior `setValue` calls within the same batch. Consider keeping a mutable ref that tracks the latest pending value so each functional update is applied to the result of the previous one before writing to localStorage.

title: fix(server): follow branch drift in dedicated worktrees so PRs link to their thread
body:
## Problem

When an agent (or the user) runs a plain \`git checkout -b\` inside a thread's dedicated worktree and files a PR from the new branch, the PR never links to the thread. The thread's recorded \`branch\` only updates through T3 commands (creation, first-turn auto-rename), so it goes stale — and since #4460 the client only attributes PR state to a thread when the checked-out branch exactly equals the recorded one. Stale metadata silently orphans the PR, and (via #5151) also re-enables inactivity auto-settle for threads that actually have an open PR.

This happened in the wild: a thread recorded \`t3code/ios-background-websocket-reconnect\`, the agent branched off to \`t3code/mobile-reconnect-hardening\` mid-thread and filed #5154 from it, and the link never formed.

## Solution

Keep #4460's strict matching and fix the stale data instead: after each turn completes, the CheckpointReactor already refreshes local git status for the session cwd. Use that fresh status to detect drift — if the checked-out branch differs from the thread's recorded branch **and the worktree belongs to exactly that thread**, dispatch a \`thread.meta.update\` adopting the checked-out branch. The command's existing \`expectedBranch\` compare-and-swap drops the update if the recorded branch moved concurrently.

Guards: shared cwds are never touched (that's where #4460's protection matters), detached HEAD and temporary \`t3code/<hex>\` placeholder checkouts are ignored, and threads with no recorded branch are left alone.

No schema changes, no client changes, no new polling — one server-side hook on an existing refresh path.

## Tests

Three focused cases in \`CheckpointReactor.test.ts\`: adopts drift on a dedicated worktree, refuses when the worktree is shared, refuses temporary placeholder checkouts.

---
Diagnosed and implemented by Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5, 1m context) running in Claude Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes thread metadata on an existing turn-completion path with compare-and-swap guards; wrong adoption could mis-link PRs, but shared-worktree and temporary-branch guards limit blast radius.
> 
> **Overview**
> When an agent or user checks out a different branch inside a thread’s **dedicated** worktree (outside T3’s branch commands), the thread’s stored `branch` can stay stale. That breaks PR↔thread linking and related behavior that only matches when checkout equals recorded branch.
> 
> **CheckpointReactor** now uses the local git status already refreshed on `turn.completed`. If the checked-out ref differs from the thread’s recorded branch, it dispatches `thread.meta.update` with `expectedBranch` so concurrent renames are ignored. Adoption only runs when the session cwd is that thread’s sole worktree; shared worktrees, detached HEAD, and temporary `t3code/<hex>` placeholder branches are skipped.
> 
> Tests extend the harness and add three cases: adopt on dedicated worktree, no adopt when worktree is shared, no adopt for temporary placeholder checkouts.
>

title: fix(orchestration-v2): restore generated thread titles
body:
## Summary

Restores automatic title generation for new threads under orchestration V2.

A provisional title appears immediately from the first message or attachment, then a durable background effect replaces it with a generated title. Web, desktop, and mobile now use the same workflow.

## Problem

During the V2 migration, the client assigned a useful provisional title before launch, while the server inferred title-generation intent from whether the title was still `"New thread"`.

As a result, assigning the provisional title caused the server to skip generation, leaving some threads permanently titled from the first line of their first message.

Title regeneration also depended on a live event listener, so interrupted work could be lost during server shutdown or restart.

## Solution

- Pass explicit title-generation intent with the first message or thread launch.
- Persist the provisional title, regeneration marker, first message, and durable outbox effect together.
- Run automatic and manual title generation through the same replay-safe worker.
- Correlate generation requests so stale results cannot overwrite a manual rename or newer request.
- Derive provisional titles consistently across web and mobile, including image-only messages.
- Avoid changing reused-thread titles until their initial message has been accepted.

## Compatibility

Automatic title generation requires a server containing the new V2 title-generation workflow.

New clients connected to older servers can still create threads and send messages, but those threads retain the older server’s title behavior. This is intentional graceful degradation; the client does not maintain a second, non-atomic title-generation fallback.

The existing version-drift UI directs users to update the connected server when they want the latest behavior.

## User-facing behavior

Before: a new thread could remain permanently titled from the first line of its first message.

After: the provisional title appears immediately and is asynchronously replaced by a generated title.

There are no layout or styling changes.

## Verification

- 107-test orchestration, contracts, client-runtime, and mobile title suite passed.
- Final review fixes were revalidated with 49 focused and adjacent tests.
- Server, contracts, client-runtime, web, and mobile typechecks passed.
- Isolated Playwright testing verified image-only provisional titles and the transition to a generated title with no browser console errors.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Built with OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.6) in T3 Code.

> [!NOTE]
> ### Restore durable thread title generation in orchestration-v2
> - Introduces a `thread-title.generate` effect type and `ThreadTitleRegenerationService` to handle initial and regenerate title generation as durable, effect-driven work rather than opportunistic background calls.
> - Adds a shared `deriveThreadTitleSeed` utility in `@t3tools/client-runtime/operations` that normalizes text, falls back to attachment names and context labels, and is now used consistently across mobile and web clients.
> - On first message dispatch, a provisional title is set immediately from the seed and a durable title generation effect is enqueued; completion is signaled via a new `thread.title.regeneration.complete` command that clears the regeneration marker.
> - Title-generation effects run in a separate lane from provider lifecycle effects on the same thread, allowing parallelism while keeping each lane serialized.
> - Behavioral Change: the web client no longer calls `updateThreadMetadata`

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not serialize first-turn startup behind title generation**

For every newly launched thread, `ThreadLaunchService` dispatches the initial message with `defer_start`, so this becomes the only pending effect and is claimed before workspace preparation later enqueues `provider-turn.start`. The outbox permits only one running effect per thread, which means the agent cannot start until the title model call finishes or times out; a slow title provider therefore turns optional asynchronous metadata generation into first-turn latency for web, desktop, and mobile. Schedule title generation so it does not occupy the per-thread lane ahead of the released run.

title: fix(server): make remote updates rollback-safe
body:
Remote server updates had accumulated multiple version owners and handoff paths, so a failed candidate could leave the service pinned to a broken version.

This replaces that implementation with one stable systemd launcher that owns version selection and durable update state. Candidates are staged and checked against the exact migration manifest, complete all fallible startup before reporting prepared, then activate only after the launcher commits. Clients correlate reconnects with the launcher-generated update ID, while foreground servers keep the explicit manual-update path.

## Verification

- 281 focused tests across 16 files
- Server, client-runtime, and contracts typechecks
- Targeted lint and formatting
- Production server bundle
- Standalone launcher dependency check
- Missing-database preflight check

Built with GPT-5.6-sol in the Codex harness via T3 Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core boot/update infrastructure: systemd units, version pinning, DB migration gating, and process handoff—failures can brick startup or leave the service on a bad runtime until rollback.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces remote self-update paths that pointed systemd at a **versioned** `bin.mjs` (and foreground respawn) with a **stable `service-launcher`** under `~/.t3/runtime`, durable `service-state.json`, and IPC between the running server and the launcher.
> 
> **Boot service** now installs the launcher artifact, writes initial state, and sets `ExecStart` to `node …/service-launcher.mjs` (with `KillMode=control-group`). **Pinned runtimes** are npm-installed into a **staging** tree, validated (including `__service-preflight` against the live DB migration manifest), then atomically published; blocked preflights surface the local `npx t3@… service update` path instead of mutating the DB remotely.
> 
> **Remote update RPC** stages the target version, runs preflight on the staged entry, then **`requestUpdate`** on the launcher and returns a launcher-generated **`updateId`** for client correlation—no direct unit rewrite or detached respawn from the server process.
> 
> **Startup ordering** adds **`ServerActivation`** / **`forkParked`** so background reactors and side effects (runtime state, Tailscale, cloud link reconcile) wait until activation; HTTP ingress is **parked** behind **`awaitCommandReady`**. Launcher **trial** children skip WAL and migrations so preflight stays read-only.
> 
> Servers without an installed launcher-managed service can no longer self-update remotely; the error directs users to **`t3 service install`**.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ff26b5a2202bbdb58d2842f2d8e368f09621ceb1. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

🟠 **High** `cloud/pinnedRuntime.ts:100`

Two concurrent callers can delete each other's published runtime. With the process-wide lock removed, both callers can observe an incomplete `versionDir`. Caller A removes it and atomically publishes a valid staged runtime via `fs.rename`. Caller B — which already passed the `versionDirExists && !alreadyPinned` check — then executes its delayed `fs.remove(paths.versionDir)`, deleting A's freshly published runtime. If B's own install subsequently fails, no valid runtime remains. The `fs.remove` at line 101 runs unconditionally based on a stale observation, with no check that the directory is still the same incomplete one that was inspected. The removal must be serialized or made conditional on the directory not having changed between the check and the delete.

title: feat: fold legacy models into separate menus
body:
Older provider models crowd the model picker and make the current families harder to scan.

This marks legacy models in provider snapshots so every client receives the same classification. Web and desktop now place them in an inline collapsed section, while mobile places a provider-scoped legacy submenu immediately after each provider. Search, favorites, existing selections, and custom models remain directly usable.

### Before

### After, collapsed

### After, expanded

![Expanded legacy models section](https://files.tslop.org/2026/08/legacy-models-after-expanded-05173170.png)

title: feat: native subagent & workflow observability
body: ## Problem When a thread spawns subagents, runs a workflow, or drives Codex collab agents, the UI showed nothing useful: subagent tool calls and narration interleaved anonymously into the parent chat, progress ticks spammed the work log, background shells masqueraded as agents, the sidebar showed no status once the turn settled, and Stop only killed the parent turn while the fleet kept burning tokens. Spec (final, decisions locked): https://n0hbggyouhn1.postplan.dev ## Solution Surface agents using **only native provider emissions** on the current orchestrator — no dependency on orchestrator v2 (#2829), **zero migrations, zero new tables**. Widened `task.*` activity payloads ride the existing event-sourced activity path; a client-side fold in `client-runtime` derives orchestration-v2-shaped subagent state (field names match #4779, so the v2 merge is a mapper swap). **Server** - Contracts: additive `TaskAgentLinkage` on all task payloads (role, model, workflow name/phases, run handles, output file, owning `agentId`), new `task.updated` event, typed usage, tool attribution (`agentId`/`parentToolUseId`) - ClaudeAdapter: carries previously-dropped fields, handles `task_updated`, resolves `parent_tool_use_id` on tool events, keeps subagent narration out of the parent transcript (leak + Working-timer-reset fix), attributes subagent-internal shells to their owning agent, defensive `workflow_progress` parse, Workflow run handles - Codex: registers multi-agent-v2 children from `thread/started`/`subAgentActivity` (root-thread guard from live probe), intercepts child notifications, synthesizes the same `task.*` lifecycle (idle = resumable, cumulative usage, real names from agentPath) - **Stop-everything**: interrupt stops every live Claude task (`Query.stopTask`) and interrupts every live Codex child turn before the parent turn - **Sidebar liveness**: `ThreadBackgroundLivenessService` (in-memory, no persistence) exposes `backgroundLiveness: working | monitoring` on the thread shell — fleets read Working, watch loops read Monitoring - `orchestration.getWorkflowScript` RPC with TOCTOU-safe containment (open-then-verify inode, realpath under `~/.claude/projects`, .js-only, size cap) **Web** - **Agents right-panel surface** (the only roster): live workflows as bordered sections with a **phase rail** (per-phase segments with member status dots) and **collapsible phase sections** (live open, done collapsed); flat agent rows (no unfold); settled runs collapse to one line under "Earlier"; `{} script` opens a read-only script view - **Spawn CTA row** in chat: one anchored row per workflow run / direct-spawn batch, exempt from turn folds and overflow, membership pinned at first row (parallel-batch fix), coordinator status authoritative for workflows - **Quiet timeline**: agent-attributed tool rows re-homed to the panel, `timelineBypass` rows fold into the CTA, background shells stay ordinary work-log rows - All in-flight states present as **Working** (monitoring-pill rule); idle presents as settled **Mobile**: same quiet-timeline fold; `task.completed` kept as terminal signal. ## Verification - client-runtime: 30 fold tests (identity/activations, usage merges, bounds, cascade, nested agents); web: 1772 incl. quiet-timeline fixtures built from real persisted threads; server: adapter/ingestion/liveness/script-containment suites incl. a symlink-escape test and a stop-everything test - Live-tested over multiple rounds: Claude direct spawns + workflows (incl. 10-parallel), Codex collab fleets (10 agents), rerun workflows, monitoring threads — each round's findings fixed against exported wire/DB data ## Remaining gaps - Codex fixtures should be generated from the captured wire logs (three schema-vs-wire divergences were found live) - Settled Codex rows show "assistant message" filler instead of a result summa

findings.body: These two conditions are domain checks with a known outcome (the opened handle is not a regular file; the inode/device changed between `realpath` and `open`), but they are signalled by manufacturing a generic `Error` purely so the surrounding `catch` can fold them into `reason: "read-failed"` with that `Error` as `cause`. The caller-visible result is "Script read failed." for what is actually a containment/type failure, and the structural distinction only survives as free-text inside `cause`. Suggest failing with the tagged error directly for these cases — e.g. add `not-a-file` and `changed-during-read` to the `reason` literal union in `OrchestrationGetWorkflowScriptError` and construct the error at each check (stat the handle in its own `Effect.tryPromise`, then `Effect.fail(new OrchestrationGetWorkflowScriptError({ reason, scriptPath: resolved }))`), leaving `reason: "read-failed"` for genuine I/O failures whose `cause` is a real platform error. Posted via Macroscope — Effect Service Conventions

**Pinned spawn rows break the chronological order of the work group.**

`visibleEntries` places every spawn entry before the retained tail entries, and `renderedEntries` places `hiddenEntries` before `visibleEntries`. A spawn row created in the middle of the group therefore renders above earlier tool rows, and expanding the group moves it again. Rows in this list are otherwise ordered by time.

Preserve group order and select the retained entries by index instead of concatenating two filtered lists.

<details>
<summary>♻️ Proposed order-preserving selection</summary>

```diff
-          const overflowCandidates = visibleGroupedEntries.filter(
-            (entry) => entry.agentSpawn === undefined,
-          );
-          const pinnedSpawnEntries = visibleGroupedEntries.filter(
-            (entry) => entry.agentSpawn !== undefined,
-          );
-          const hiddenEntries = overflowCandidates.slice(0, -MAX_VISIBLE_WORK_LOG_ENTRIES);
-          const visibleEntries = [
-            ...pinnedSpawnEntries,
-            ...overflowCandidates.slice(-MAX_VISIBLE_WORK_LOG_ENTRIES),
-          ];
+          const overflowCandidates = visibleGroupedEntries.filter(
+            (entry) => entry.agentSpawn === undefined,
+          );
+          const hiddenIds = new Set(
+            overflowCandidates.slice(0, -MAX_VISIBLE_WORK_LOG_ENTRIES).map((entry) => entry.id),
+          );
+          const hiddenEntries = visibleGroupedEntries.filter((entry) => hiddenIds.has(entry.id));
+          const visibleEntries = visibleGroupedEntries.filter((entry) => !hiddenIds.has(entry.id));
```

With this shape, `renderedEntries` for the expanded case becomes `visibleGroupedEntries`:

```diff
-          const renderedEntries = expanded ? [...hiddenEntries, ...visibleEntries] : visibleEntries;
+          const renderedEntries = expanded ? visibleGroupedEntries : visibleEntries;
```
</details>

findings.body:
🔴 **Critical** `orchestration/workflowScriptQuery.ts:59`

The containment check runs on `resolved` (a resolved pathname), but the file is then opened with `NodeFS.open(resolved, "r")` using that same pathname string. A process that can modify `~/.claude/projects` can replace the validated file or an ancestor directory with a symlink between the `realpath` call and the `open` call, causing this authenticated RPC to return up to 256 KiB from an arbitrary file readable by the server. The containment check must be tied to the opened descriptor rather than performed on a mutable pathname beforehand. Consider opening the path relative to the root directory and verifying containment via `fstat`/`openat` on the descriptor, or otherwise re-resolving after `open` using the file handle.

No longer relevant as of 25de5b7b25b5ad3cdc6afe29b6ca7ab0946b3fb0

thread.body:
[claude-fable-5] RESPONDING ON BEHALF OF THEO
-----

Real and good catch — fixed in 8d20b6843. The read path now opens first and verifies the opened file via the handle: `handle.stat()` inode+dev must match a fresh `lstat` of the resolved path, so a swap between resolution and open is detected rather than followed. Short reads honored via `bytesRead` in the same change.

The inode comparison is a good improvement, but I believe there's still a gap: **containment is checked on the path before opening, but never re-verified for the opened file descriptor**.

An attacker with write access to `~/.claude/projects` could:
1. Let `realpath` and containment check pass on a legitimate file inside the root (inode A)
2. Replace the file with a hardlink to `/etc/passwd` (inode B) before `open`
3. The inode check at line 76 passes because `lstat(resolved)` and `handle.stat()` both return inode B
4. The opened inode was never verified to be contained within the root

To fully close the TOCTOU, the code should re-verify containment using the opened descriptor—either by:
- Using `openat` relative to an opened handle for `scriptsRoot()`
- Re-running `realpath` on the descriptor (e.g., via `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` on Linux) and re-checking containment
- Or re-doing `realpath(resolved)` after `open` and verifying it's unchanged and still contained

[claude-fable-5] RESPONDING ON BEHALF OF THEO
-----

Dismissing this one, for two reasons.

1. The proposed mitigations do not detect the hardlink vector either. A hardlink inside `~/.claude/projects` pointing at another inode IS a contained path: `realpath` on it (or on `/proc/self/fd/<fd>`) resolves to the in-root path, so re-checking containment after open passes identically. Actually closing that vector would require `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS)` or ownership/`st_nlink` heuristics.

2. The threat model does not warrant it. This endpoint serves read-only script text to the local paired client, running as the same user who owns `~/.claude/projects`. An attacker with write access there is already executing as that user and can read any file directly; the server grants nothing they lack. Also note `fs.protected_hardlinks` blocks hardlinking files the caller cannot write on default Linux configs. The inode/dev check exists to close the symlink-swap race from the earlier finding (a swapped path between realpath and open), which it does.

Happy to revisit if this endpoint ever serves a trust boundary beyond the owning user.

🟡 **Medium** `state/subagentRuntime.ts:523`

In `task.updated`, the `endedAt` timestamp from the payload is never applied to `agent.completedAt`. When `applyStatus` transitions the agent to a terminal state, it already sets `agent.completedAt` to the activity's `at` time. The subsequent `if (endedAt && isTerminalSubagentStatus(agent.status) && agent.completedAt === null)` check then always fails because `completedAt` is no longer `null`, so the provider's authoritative `endedAt` is silently dropped. Terminal timestamps reflect ingestion time instead of the provider's end time, producing incorrect durations and ordering. Consider applying `endedAt` before calling `applyStatus`, or using it to overwrite `completedAt` when the agent is terminal.

✅ Resolved in 4b6d2761c600e2efb05c5eeb22bbbb436551eda7

🟡 **Medium** `src/session-logic.ts:872`

When later `task.progress`/`task.completed` rows merge into an existing spawn CTA, `mergeDerivedWorkLogEntries(existing, entry)` overwrites the CTA row's `createdAt` and `id` with the latest lifecycle event's values. `deriveTimelineEntries` sorts by `createdAt`, so a "Kicked off N subagents" CTA moves from spawn time to completion time and can appear after messages and events that occurred while the agents were running. 🟡 **Medium** `chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:1975`

When a subagent transitions to `idle` (a resumable, still-active state in the panel model), the CTA incorrectly freezes to past tense. Because `live` is computed as `running + waiting > 0`, any agent that completes into `idle` is excluded, so the row switches from `Kicked off … subagents` to `Ran … subagents` and shows `✓ completed` even though the workflow has not settled. Include `idle` agents in the `live` computation and render an appropriate idle/resumable status instead of marking the row completed.

No longer relevant as of 4622c3ab354f9db2f6879c5e0824df014420887c

🟡 **Medium** `chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:1975`

`AgentSpawnCtaRow` renders a workflow coordinator as `Ran 0 subagents · ✓ completed` (green dot) when the coordinator is actively running but no phase member has started yet. The status counts (`running`, `waiting`, `failed`, `live`) are computed only from `agents` (phase and unphased members), ignoring `workflowGroup.workflow.status`. A coordinator-level failure also renders green/completed when none of its members failed. Consider incorporating the workflow coordinator's own `status` into the derived `running`/`waiting`/`failed`/`live` values so the CTA reflects the workflow's true lifecycle state.

A later `task.started` still hits `activationCount === 0` and forces `status` back to `running`, reopening interrupted/failed agents and wiping the terminal state the fold claims to protect.

findings.body:
🟡 **Medium** `Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1079`

Children tracked only via `collabReceiverTurns` (from a prior `collabAgentToolCall`) never emit the synthetic `collabAgent/*` lifecycle events this change introduces, so their task state stays missing or stuck. `handleRawNotification` returns early when `shouldSuppressChildConversationNotification` is true — which covers `thread/started`, `turn/started`, `turn/completed`, status changes, token usage, and `thread/closed` — before `interceptCollabChildNotification` runs at line 1079. Those children are never registered through `thread/started`, and even `subAgentActivity`-registered children never emit `collabAgent/turnStarted`, `collabAgent/turnCompleted`, `collabAgent/statusChanged`, `collabAgent/tokenUsage`, or `collabAgent/closed` because the suppression check intercepts those methods first. Consider moving `interceptCollabChildNotification` ahead of the `childParentTurnId` suppression check, or making the suppression skip notifications addressed to registered child threads.

✅ Resolved in 178eaf794b70d78caceb0b455046ebadffaaffb3

🟡 **Medium** `state/subagentRuntime.ts:692`

Workflow members whose `phaseIndex` is non-null but absent from `workflow.phases` disappear from the UI entirely — they match no phase and are excluded from `unphasedMembers` because it filters on `phaseIndex === null`. This loses the agent from both the phase list and `workflowCardMembers`. Consider treating members whose phase index is not in `knownPhases` as unphased as well.

✅ Resolved in 4b6d2761c600e2efb05c5eeb22bbbb436551eda7

🟡 **Medium** `Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:681`

The `collabAgent/item` case always emits a `task.progress` event regardless of whether the source notification is `item/started` or `item/completed`, so a single child item that fires both lifecycle notifications produces two progress rows for the same task. These duplicate rows occupy the agent activity ring unnecessarily, and since the ring is capped they evict distinct recent activity prematurely. Consider emitting only on `item/started` (or otherwise suppressing `item/completed`), so each item contributes at most one progress entry.

No longer relevant as of 23f75edad177bdfc74a46cccbed3c14d888d6b85

🟡 **Medium** `state/subagentRuntime.ts:519`

A duplicate `task.completed` event overwrites the first terminal `result` or `error` and advances `updatedAt`, even though `applyStatus` treats the status itself as idempotent. This means a late duplicate completion replaces the settled agent's original outcome and makes it appear freshly updated, contradicting the intended first-write-wins semantics for terminal events.

`applyStatus` returns early for duplicate terminal statuses but `task.completed` continues afterward and unconditionally runs `agent.result = bounded(summary)` (or `agent.error = ...`) and `agent.updatedAt = at`. Guard those assignments behind a check that the agent wasn't already terminal.

✅ Resolved in 4b6d2761c600e2efb05c5eeb22bbbb436551eda7

🟡 **Medium** `chat/WorkflowRunCard.tsx:64`

`totalTokens` double-counts tokens for workflows whose coordinator already carries aggregate member usage. The `reduce` starts from `group.workflow.usage?.totalTokens ?? 0` and then adds each member's `totalTokens` on top, so providers that report aggregate member usage on the coordinator (which `deriveAgentPanelModel` accounts for by excluding coordinator usage when members exist) produce an inflated total. Use coordinator usage only when there are no members; otherwise sum member usage alone.

No longer relevant as of 9be170a88333cafd34b39c1b9e2a168f79745008

🟡 **Medium** `state/subagentRuntime.ts:319`

When a workflow slot retries from a failed attempt to a new running attempt, `activationCount` is incremented twice for the same event — once in `fillMetadata` (because `attempt` increases) and again in `applyStatus` (because the previous status was terminal and the new status is `running`). A single transition from failed attempt 1 to running attempt 2 reports 3 activations instead of 2, inflating the retry/run counts shown to users.

The reactivation logic in `fillMetadata` and `applyStatus` both fire for the same event. Consider having only one of them bump `activationCount` for a given transition — for example, skip the increment in `fillMetadata` when the same event will also trigger a reactivation in `applyStatus`, or remove the duplicate increment from `fillMetadata` entirely if `applyStatus` already handles reactivation.

✅ Resolved in 4b6d2761c600e2efb05c5eeb22bbbb436551eda7

🟡 **Medium** `state/subagentRuntime.ts:666`

A workflow phase containing only `idle` members gets `state: "pending"` instead of `"running"`, misreporting an unfinished, resumable phase as not-yet-started. `activeCount` is computed via `isActiveSubagentStatus`, which returns `false` for `idle`, so `activeCount` is 0 even though the inline comment states idle members should keep the phase live. This causes the phase-liveness branch to fall through to `"pending"` when no members are active by that definition.

No longer relevant as of 4b6d2761c600e2efb05c5eeb22bbbb436551eda7

🟡 **Medium** `components/AgentsPanel.tsx:91`

`AgentElapsed` renders idle agents using `agent.completedAt`, but `completedAt` is not set for idle (non-terminal) agents, so `elapsedBetween` falls back to `Date.now()`. An idle agent loaded from history displays the entire elapsed time since `startedAt` — potentially hours or days — instead of its last activation duration. Consider using `updatedAt` (or a dedicated activation-end timestamp) for the idle case.

title: feat(web): add modular theme library
body: ## Summary Adds a token-based theme system to the web client and desktop app: 57 semantic color roles, applied before React mounts so there is no flash of the wrong theme. - **Color scheme first** — the Appearance section leads with three wide tiles (System, Light, Dark), each a miniature of the app painted in the currently picked palettes; the System tile splits to show both halves. - **Mix light and dark from different themes** — every theme card shows its light and dark balls; clicking one assigns that theme to that half of the mix (marked with a ring and a sun/moon badge), and System flips between the two picks with the OS. Picks persist, apply live, and resolve in the boot splash — parity between the inline boot script and the runtime is CI-enforced by tests that derive from the real palette definitions. - **Six built-in themes** — T3 Code (default), T3 Chat (anchored to the official t3.chat palette), Grove, Ocean, Ember, and Iris. Each maintainer theme pairs its accent with a companion action color that drives every solid control, while the accent handles surfaces, selection, and focus. - **Personal themes** — guided creation from two colors (an OKLCH generator derives a readable palette from the exact seeds), an advanced editor for every role, and JSON import/export. The editor opens as a draggable panel above the router that applies its draft to the running app, and starts from the theme you already use. - **VS Code themes convert on import** — the drop box takes T3 Code and VS Code theme files (several at once), maps the workbench colors it finds onto a contrast-solved palette, flattens alpha overlays and wide-gamut `color()` values, and pairs a family's light and dark files into one dual-mode theme. Re-importing an installed theme asks whether to update it or keep both. - **Full-surface coverage** — sidebar, composer, chat timeline (including code blocks in replies), diffs and their gutters, terminals, file previews, the typography previews from #5103, toolbars, status colors, and the browser chrome color. Closes #418 Closes #233 Closes #4302 Supersedes #5258 ## Screenshots | Light half active | Dark half active | | --- | --- | | | | *Both shots show the same mix — T3 Chat in light, Grove in dark — from either side of the System toggle.* | Theme editor | Importing themes | | --- | --- | | | | *The editor floats above the app and paints its draft on the live interface, so a color is judged by browsing the app rather than a miniature; it drags anywhere and survives navigation. Advanced mode lists one role per row behind a filter.* | Themed typography previews | | --- | | | Built with GPT-5.6-Luna and Claude Fable 5 in T3 Code. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Large UI and boot-time localStorage theming surface with many touchpoints; failures generally degrade to fallbacks rather than affecting auth or data, but bad stored theme shapes or boot/runtime drift could cause flash or inconsi

findings.body:
🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1615`

When editing a single-mode theme, switching to "Light + dark" and finishing on the newly added appearance silently flips the theme's base `appearance`. The condition `editingTheme && getThemeModes(editingTheme).length > 1` only preserves `editingTheme.appearance` for themes that already have both modes, so a dark-only theme that gains a light variant can end up with `appearance: "light"` (and vice versa). Since theme cards and plain-ID selection rely on `theme.appearance`, the theme's default mode unexpectedly changes. Consider preserving `editingTheme.appearance` whenever `editingTheme` is non-null, falling back to `activeAppearance` only for new themes.

✅ Resolved in 89d70e928a34e94f719059d8d9c2d430063229e5

### Guided save regens both modes **High Severity** The theme editor's "guided colors" logic can inadvertently discard custom color settings. When saving, if not in advanced mode, the system applies managed colors to both light and dark modes whenever simple colors are marked as dirty or a new theme is being created. This can overwrite per-role customizations in the unedited mode and lead to unexpected palettes for new themes.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e4cf49aaec9c6bc383ed8c7e4cb46826863d72e7. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1608`

When editing an existing dual-mode theme in guided mode, changing the light (or dark) background/accent silently overwrites all custom colors in the untouched dark (or light) variant on save. The single `simpleColorsDirty` flag is shared across both appearances, so `handleSubmit` runs `getManagedEditorColors` on both `colorsByAppearance.light` and `colorsByAppearance.dark` even when only one was edited, replacing every color in the untouched variant with generated defaults. Track dirty state per appearance, or only regenerate the appearance that was actually modified.

✅ Resolved in cd5063912d54efd9bf4a3a125aff7e8f51b7035d

### One mode drops wrong palette **Medium Severity** When editing a dual-mode personal theme and saving with **One mode**, `baseAppearance` follows the active Light/Dark tab (`activeAppearance`), not the theme’s original base. Saving while the variant tab is selected rewrites `appearance` to that mode and drops the other palette from storage without warning.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 82f9299733c707583bd65dc21474c0c13e1d5c92. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Inactive edit toast claims active **Medium Severity** After saving a personal theme from the editor, the success toast always says the changes are “now active,” even when that theme is not the current app theme. In that case only the library entry updates; `setTheme` and `refreshTheme` are skipped, so the running palette stays unchanged while the message implies it switched.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 82f9299733c707583bd65dc21474c0c13e1d5c92. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1923`

`handleConfirmRemoveTheme` resets the theme to `"system"` when the removed theme is active, regardless of whether Follow system is off. With `followSystem` disabled, `"system"` causes the desktop to follow OS appearance while the Follow system switch shows off, and web falls back to light. Use the current appearance as the fallback, like `handleFollowSystemChange` does.

✅ Resolved in 6a0acb144bb63d9bf07000fdfafc605481e9dad0

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1119`

When `value` is a valid 3-, 4-, or 8-digit hex (e.g. `#fff` or `#ff000080`), the color picker `<input type="color">` shows black instead of the current color. `pickerValue` only accepts 6-digit hex and substitutes `#000000` for every other valid format, so opening the picker resets the starting point to black and any alpha value is discarded when the user picks a new color. Consider normalizing `value` to a 6-digit `#rrggbb` (expanding shorthand and stripping alpha) for the picker so it reflects the current color, while keeping the original `value` as the text input.

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1742`

The card div has `role="button"`, and personal-theme cards render nested `<Button>` controls (Export, Remove) inside it. Per the WAI-ARIA spec, descendants of a `button` are not exposed to assistive technology with their own semantics, so screen readers cannot perceive or operate the inner action buttons. Consider restructuring so the action buttons are siblings of (not descendants of) the button-role element — e.g., make the preview/label region a single button control and render the action buttons as adjacent siblings.

### Basic mode saves hidden colors **Medium Severity** Turning off Advanced in Create theme only shows Background and Accent, but `handleSubmit` still passes the full `colorsByAppearance` palette (and full variant objects) into `parseThemeFile`. Edits made while Advanced was on—or invalid hex in roles that are now hidden—still affect the saved theme or trigger validation errors with no matching field on screen.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/components/settings/SettingsPanels.tsx#L1316-L1387`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/f8ef5fa04258390ee192e2f23af6ae444e1dcc86/apps/web/src/components/settings/SettingsPanels.tsx#L1316-L1387)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f8ef5fa04258390ee192e2f23af6ae444e1dcc86. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Boot sets theme id early **Medium Severity** The boot script sets `html[data-theme-id]` for T3 Chat and custom themes before the bundle runs, but inline `--app-theme-*` variables are only applied later by `applyThemePalette`. New CSS maps semantic tokens through those variables whenever `data-theme-id` is present, so the splash window can render with invalid or empty theme colors until JavaScript loads.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/index.css#L1055-L1062`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b/apps/web/src/index.css#L1055-L1062)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Boot follow-system stale theme mismatch **Medium Severity** When `t3code:theme` holds an id that runtime no longer recognizes (for example a removed custom theme), `readThemePreference` falls back to `"system"` and treats Follow system as on if the follow key is unset. The boot script still reads the raw stored id for follow defaults, so Follow system stays off and `isDark` can stay light while the app later applies system dark mode on a dark OS.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

findings.body:
### Boot splash dark for T3 Chat **Medium Severity** When using the T3 Chat theme with "Follow system" enabled on a dark OS, the boot script correctly applies a dark theme. However, the application's runtime theme logic then incorrectly forces T3 Chat to its light palette, causing a visible flash of incorrect theme. This also impacts legacy `t3-chat-dark` settings.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `src/index.css:1071`

The `--app-theme-text-muted` CSS variable is never consumed by the themed token mapping, so a theme's `textMuted` role has no visual effect. The mapping block sets `--muted-foreground: var(--app-theme-muted-foreground)` but never reads `--app-theme-text-muted`, even though `applyThemePalette` sets that variable and `textMuted` is an exposed theme role. Consider mapping `--muted-foreground` to `--app-theme-text-muted` (or whichever role is intended to drive muted text), or document which role controls it.

✅ Resolved in ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b

🟡 **Medium** `src/themePalette.ts:532`

`parseThemeFile` accepts a `variants` entry whose key equals the theme's base `appearance` (e.g. `appearance: "light"` with `variants.light`) and installs it successfully, but every color in that variant is silently ignored. `getThemeColorsForMode` returns `theme.colors` directly whenever `mode === theme.appearance`, so the same-appearance variant colors are never read. Consider rejecting a variant key that matches the base `appearance` so the import fails instead of silently dropping the colors.

✅ Resolved in ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b

🟡 **Medium** `src/themePalette.ts:211`

`handleStorage` ignores storage events whose `key` is `null`, so when another tab calls `localStorage.clear()` this tab does not invalidate `customThemesSnapshot`. Removed custom themes remain displayed and applied until a reload or another theme mutation, because `getCustomThemes` keeps serving the stale snapshot. Browsers set `key` to `null` for `clear()` calls, so treat that case as affecting `CUSTOM_THEMES_STORAGE_KEY`.

✅ Resolved in ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1922`

Selecting the "Theme" item in settings search navigates to `#theme` but no element with `id="theme"` exists on the appearance page, so the scroll/focus target is missing. The old `SettingsRow` received its anchor id from `searchableSetting("theme")`, but the replacement `SettingsSection` and `ThemeLibrary` are rendered without any `id` prop. Consider propagating `{...searchableSetting("theme")}` onto the `SettingsSection` (or a wrapping `SettingsRow`) so the search target anchor is restored.

✅ Resolved in ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1758`

Removing the currently active custom theme leaves the stale theme ID selected and the old palette applied — the app never falls back to the default theme. `handleRemoveTheme` calls `removeCustomTheme(customTheme.id)` first, which synchronously drops the theme from the cache, so the subsequent `getThemeDefinition(theme)` returns `null` for the removed theme and the `setTheme("system")` branch never executes. The `if` check must run before removal.

✅ Resolved in ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b

findings.body:
🟡 **Medium** `hooks/useTheme.ts:406`

`setFollowSystem` does not reset `themeStorageReadFailure` after a successful write, so `getStored()` on line 408 keeps returning the default `"system"` theme for the rest of the session if a prior transient `localStorage` read failure set that flag. Toggling Follow system then applies and reports the wrong theme. `writeThemePreference` already clears this flag on line 133; `setFollowSystem` should do the same before calling `getStored()`.

✅ Resolved in ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b

🟡 **Medium** `hooks/useTheme.ts:339`

When the currently selected custom theme is edited in another tab, this tab keeps the stale CSS colors and never reapplies the updated palette. The `CUSTOM_THEMES_STORAGE_KEY` branch calls `invalidateCustomThemes()` followed by `applyTheme(getStored(), true)`, but `applyTheme` returns early when the theme id, system appearance, and follow-system flag are unchanged, so the invalidated palette is never re-applied. Consider forcing re-application (e.g., resetting `lastAppliedTheme`) before calling `applyTheme` when custom theme definitions change.

✅ Resolved in ebcf87491ef964d0be25120cfdd62e94c3aaf26b

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1419`

The `useEffect` reset on dialog open clears the form, but a `file.text()` call started during the previous session can still resolve after the dialog reopens. When it does, `setJson` and `setFileName` run with the stale file data, repopulating the new session with the previously selected theme. Consider tracking the read with an abortable primitive (e.g. an `AbortController` or a stale-session flag) so late resolutions from a prior open are ignored.

✅ Resolved in 607dd6b28048fbfcbdddb3951bf87a1215b218b5

🟡 **Medium** `chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:1369`

`UserMessagePreviewAnnotationCard` uses `text-message-foreground` for the comment and target summary, but the card's own background is `bg-background/70`. Because `messageForeground` is paired with `messageSurface` while `background` maps to the `canvas` palette, a theme with a dark `canvas` and dark `messageForeground` renders this text the same color as the nested card background, making it unreadable. Content placed on `bg-background` should use the standard foreground token (e.g. `text-foreground`) instead.

✅ Resolved in 607dd6b28048fbfcbdddb3951bf87a1215b218b5

🟡 **Medium** `hooks/useTheme.ts:412`

When a user disables Follow system and then restores default settings, the `followSystem` preference stays `false` because the restore defaults path only calls `setTheme("system")` and never clears `THEME_FOLLOW_SYSTEM_STORAGE_KEY`. As a result, the restored `system` theme resolves to a fixed light appearance instead of following the OS preference, and the restore dialog does not list this retained setting. The restore defaults flow should also reset the follow-system preference (e.g. by calling `setFollowSystem(true)` or removing the storage key), or the key should be documented as intentionally excluded from restores.

No longer relevant as of 415a64685419708e48b5acba0e3fdeb9d55e49f1

🟡 **Medium** `src/themePalette.ts:598`

`applyThemePalette` applies the wrong palette when Follow system is enabled. If the stored theme preference is mode-specific (e.g. `aurora:dark`) but Follow system resolves to light, `resolveThemeAppearance` correctly returns `"light"`, but `applyThemePalette` ignores that and calls `explicitThemeMode(theme)`, which returns `"dark"`. The dark palette is applied even though the `dark` class is absent, so palette variables and the document appearance disagree. The `appearance` argument should take precedence over the stored mode suffix so Follow system actually switches the palette.

✅ Resolved in 607dd6b28048fbfcbdddb3951bf87a1215b218b5

🟡 **Medium** `settings/SettingsPanels.tsx:1137`

The reset `useEffect` in `CreateThemeDialog` runs whenever `initialAppearance` changes while the dialog is open, discarding the user's in-progress draft — including `name`, all edited colors, mode selection, and errors. Because `initialAppearance` comes from the resolved system appearance, an OS light/dark switch during editing wipes out the unsaved theme. The reset should fire only on the closed-to-open transition, not on every appearance update.

title: fix(web): polish interface spacing
body: ## Summary - align composer, sidebar, and top-bar control insets - size the context-window ring consistently with the send control - use the shared bordered glass treatment for context-window details ## Why Several nearby controls used slightly different hardcoded insets and the context-window popover overrode the shared floating-surface styling. This made edges look uneven and the context control feel inconsistent with the rest of the interface. ## Validation - `vp fmt --check` on the eight changed web files - `vp run --filter @t3tools/web typecheck` Created with GPT-5.6 Sol via the Codex harness. > [!NOTE] > ### Polish interface spacing across web UI components > Makes minor padding and spacing adjustments across several components for visual consistency. Changes affect `BranchToolbar`, `ChatComposer`, `GitActionsControl`, `OpenInPicker`, `SidebarV2`, `SettingsSidebarNav`, and `ContextWindowMeter`. The `ContextWindowMeter` popover also gains stroke color transition animation on the SVG circle alongside the existing dash offset animation. > > > > Macroscope summarized 4a87482. > > --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > CSS-only spacing and popover styling tweaks with no logic, auth, or data-path changes. > > **Overview** > Aligns **horizontal insets** across the composer strip, sidebar rows, header icon buttons, and workspace titlebar so neighboring controls share the same visual edge. > > **Composer & branch context** — `BranchToolbar` uses asymmetric `ps-1 pe-2` instead of uniform horizontal padding. `ChatComposer` bumps footer padding one step (`px-3/pb-3`, `sm:px-4/sm:pb-4`) and nudges the model picker trigger (`-ms-px ps-0`). > > **Sidebar & settings** — `SidebarV2` offsets the project filter trigger and thread list group with shared inset tokens (`--sidebar-row-content-inset`, `--sidebar-content-inset`). `SettingsSidebarNav` adds a 1px start padding on the menu list. > > **Header actions** — `GitActionsControl` and `OpenInPicker` apply `ps-[8.5px]` on xs outline buttons so icon-leading controls line up with peers. `ChatView` adds `mr-px` on workspace titlebar controls. > > **Context window meter** — Simplifies ring `strokeDashoffset` math, extends the SVG transition to include `stroke`, and switches the details popover to shared floating-surface styling (`viewportClassName="p-0"`, `p-[var(--floating-content-inset)]`) instead of custom glass overrides. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4a87482e5c3f1b5e6ec0068507fc178cdf1244bb. title: fix(web): better right panel (new diffs styling)
body: ## Problem The right-panel tabs and diff chrome had inconsistent sizing and spacing, with the close affordance reserving extra trailing space. Diff rows, controls, separators, and loading skeletons also no longer matched the darker panel treatment. Expanding a file could shift the list upward because the virtualizer's bottom padding disagreed with its sticky-item measurements. ## Solution - compact the panel tabs and replace each leading icon with the close control on hover - use consistent 8px outer insets and align the diff toolbar with the title-bar controls - flatten diff backgrounds and borders, and render unmodified-line counts as inline dividers - remove the virtualizer padding mismatch and keep selected-file reveal scrolling stable - findings.body:
🟡 **Medium** `components/DiffPanel.tsx:545`

The completed-turn refresh effect writes the new `{ threadKey, turnId }` to `lastCompletedTurnRefreshRef.current` *before* the early return, so when `canRefreshGitDiff` is false (e.g. the panel is showing a turn diff), the completed turn is recorded as "already seen" without triggering a refresh. When the user later switches to Working tree or Branch changes, the effect sees the same `turnId` and skips the refresh, leaving the git diff stale until a manual refresh or window-focus event. Move the ref update to after the refresh call (or guard it so it only records the value when a refresh is actually performed).

✅ Resolved in 13c8279932519c0ae8585bc0b1967931e163137e

🟡 **Medium** `state/review.ts:27`

The `singleFlight` concurrency key omits `input.changeType`, so two in-flight requests for the same environment, refs, and paths but different change types are deduplicated onto the same promise. The later request receives the result of the earlier one, returning file contents for the wrong change type (e.g. `new` returns empty `oldContents` instead of `deleted` returning empty `newContents`). Add `input.changeType` to the `JSON.stringify` array in the key.

### Draft state survives scope remount **Medium Severity** The `AnnotatableCodeView` component's `draft`, `draftText`, and `selectedLines` state persists when the inner `CodeView` remounts due to a `codeViewKey` change. If a draft comment is open when the context changes (e.g., switching git scope or thread), `hasOpenComment` remains true, disabling gutter/line selection and leaving an undismissable draft.

`vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2286`

`reviewDiffFileError` pins `operation: "GitVcsDriver.getReviewDiffFileContents"` and `command: "git"` for every failure in this pipeline, including the purely filesystem-based ones (`realPath`, `stat`, size limit, `readFile`, binary detection in `readWorkingTreeReviewFile`). Those failures then surface as `Git command failed in GitVcsDriver.getReviewDiffFileContents (...)` even though no git command ran, and the stage that actually failed is only recoverable from the free-form `detail`. Elsewhere in this module the stage is part of the structural context (`GitVcsDriver.getReviewDiffPreview.hash`, `...getReviewDiffFileContents.revision`, `...repositoryRoot`, `...mergeBase`).

Consider threading a stage into the helper and using a non-git `command` label for filesystem stages, e.g. `reviewDiffFileError(input, { stage: "readFile", command: "fs.readFile" }, detail, cause)`, so the error's operation/command fields identify the failing step instead of claiming a git invocation.

title: feat(desktop): remember recently used sites in the Browser panel
body: Closes #4746 ## What Changed Adds a **Recently used** group to the Browser panel splash, above the existing Local servers list. URLs opened in the panel are remembered per project and persist across restarts. History is recorded after successful URL-bar navigation, local-server opens, terminal links, and chat preview links. Each row shows the page title when available, the URL, relative visit time, and a remove action. Local servers is unchanged. ## Why The splash only knew about listening localhost ports, so it surfaced things that are not web servers while missing custom domains such as `app.test` and `main.app.local`. Reopening a site after a restart also meant typing the URL again. Recording sites that were actually opened handles custom domains without broadening port discovery and keeps the list relevant to each project. History is stored in localStorage with the existing Zustand persistence pattern. There is no server involvement and no new dependency. ## UI Changes | Before | After | |---|---| | | | ## Roadmap I've reduced the scope of this PR down so it is no longer XXL. If merged, I have a further (smaller) submission which is to add favicons to the "Recently used" section and browser tabs. I would also like to do more work here. The Local servers section displaying servers that do not serve web content doesn't make a lot of sense. It currently displays things for me such as `localhost:1025` which is a MailHog SMTP server and `localhost:3306` which is a MySQL server. ## Checklist - [x] This PR is small and focused - [x] I explained what changed and why - [x] I included before/after screenshots for the UI change - [x] ~I included a video for animation/interaction changes~ Built with Claude and GPT-5.6 through T3 Code. --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Client-only localStorage UI state with no auth or server changes; broad test coverage limits regression risk in preview and chat link flows. > > **Overview** > Adds **per-project browser history** persisted in localStorage via a new Zustand store, keyed to the same **logical project grouping** as the sidebar (not just the active physical project row). > > The Browser panel **empty state** gains a **Recently used** section above Local servers: each row shows title (when known), URL, relative visit time, and remove. Visits are recorded only after **successful** navigation from the URL bar, discovered local servers (storing the pre-resolution `requestedUrl`), terminal links, chat preview links, and discovered-port opens. Page titles are applied **update-only** to existing history entries after load. > > History **normalizes and sanitizes** URLs (scheme, credentials, length), **deduplicates** localhost / environment-host aliases, and caps entries per project and projects overall. Persisted state is **migrated and re-sanitized on every rehydrate**; visits/titles before thread registration are **queued** and drained on project registration. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 487681deb19d99fa1dd5245e25a7ba489afcf006. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

findings.body:
### History key registered before settings hydrate **Medium Severity** `registerThreadProject` runs from `useClientSettings` before client settings have hydrated, so it can overwrite a persisted thread-to-project mapping with a key derived from defaults. `Recently used` then briefly resolves against the wrong project bucket, and any visits recorded in that window stay under the temporary key when registration later corrects without migrating entries.

### Grouping change orphans site history **Medium Severity** Thread history is registered under `deriveLogicalProjectKeyFromSettings`, and changing sidebar grouping mode recomputes that key without moving existing `byProjectKey` entries. After a grouping toggle, `Recently used` can look empty even though the visits are still persisted under the previous logical key.

findings.body:
### Title updates thrash persisted state **Medium Severity** `setTitleForUrl` always writes a new `byProjectKey` entry even when the matched row already has the same title. The PreviewView title effect depends on `threadRef`, whose identity is recreated whenever `activeThread` changes, so routine chat/thread updates can re-fire the effect and force repeated Zustand persist writes of the full history blob while a page is open.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/components/preview/PreviewView.tsx#L149-L154`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/d9787f2afabec74a490c5a32111e368fb87e6e9d/apps/web/src/components/preview/PreviewView.tsx#L149-L154)

### Titles can miss recorded visits **Medium Severity** `setTitleForThreadUrl` only updates an existing history row, while `PreviewView` records the visit only after `navigateToResolvedUrl` resolves. If `navStatus` reaches Success with a title before that visit is written, the title effect no-ops and does not run again unless `navUrl` or `navTitle` changes, so the Recently used row can stay title-less.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L208-L227`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/6e04fd5f13c061bf252b48bdf2cb28f3e8405209/apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L208-L227)

thread.body: Fixed in `204ecf353`. The title effect now also depends on the current most-recent history URL and remains gated on history being non-empty. Recording a successful new visit changes that URL and reruns the update-only title enrichment; an existing most-recent row was already available to the first effect run. Agent-driven navigation still cannot create a history row.

findings.body:
### Trailing slashes create duplicate history **Low Severity** `visitLookupKey` keeps trailing-slash path variants distinct while `titleLookupKey` collapses them. Opening the same path with and without a trailing slash therefore creates two Recently used rows, even though title updates already treat those URLs as the same page.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L37-L43`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/e6b7a3fb82928dda14a6452613e469f7b57c9d49/apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L37-L43)

thread.body: This distinction is intentional. `/path` and `/path/` are different URL paths and can serve different resources, so visit history preserves the exact navigation (as it does for query and hash variants). `titleLookupKey` is deliberately more permissive only so a document title can attach after the webview settles through a trailing-slash redirect; collapsing visit identity with that key could make a recent row reopen the wrong route. The separate-history and most-recent-title behavior is covered by focused tests.

findings.reception_evidence: This distinction is intentional. /path and /path/ are different URL paths.

findings.body:
### Hash omitted from history labels **Medium Severity** Recent history labels are built from host, path, and search only, so the hash is dropped even though `normalizeHistoryUrl` keeps hash routes as distinct stored entries. Hash-router apps can show identical rows for different pages, and the subtitle URL stays ambiguous when a title is present.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e53afc10eab9d0598a7c0944c09791e759d7eda1. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### History stores volatile env hosts **High Severity** `visitLookupKey` treats loopback and the environment host as the same site, but `upsertHistoryEntry` always keeps the latest raw URL. After a local-server open stores a stable loopback URL, a normal URL-bar submit records the webview’s resolved host and overwrites history with that volatile address. On remote/WSL environments that host can change after restart, so Recently used entries stop opening.
Additional Locations (2) - [`apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L44-L51`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/b96fc725a47d4d21775f3fd47d27a295187f320c/apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L44-L51) - [`apps/web/src/components/preview/PreviewView.tsx#L167-L174`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/b96fc725a47d4d21775f3fd47d27a295187f320c/apps/web/src/components/preview/PreviewView.tsx#L167-L174)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b96fc725a47d4d21775f3fd47d27a295187f320c. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Local URL aliases create duplicate history **Medium Severity** `titleLookupKey` treats loopback hosts, `0.0.0.0`, and the environment host as the same site for titles, but `upsertHistoryEntry` dedupes visits by exact URL only. Opens from local servers, terminal links, and chat can therefore store `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and the resolved env IP as separate Recently used rows for one server.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L36-L46`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/0fc57bffdc6320fd877882be1300e01d837d353d/apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L36-L46)
