### Recents hidden until project registration **Medium Severity** `useThreadRecentHistory` only reads history after `projectKeyByThreadKey` is set, but that mapping is ephemeral (not persisted) and is filled in a `ChatView` `useEffect` that also waits on `activeProject`. After reload or while the project atom is still null, persisted `byProjectKey` data is ignored, so the Browser empty state can show `No preview yet` or omit Recently used even when history exists.

🟡 **Medium** `src/browserFaviconStore.ts:64`

`resolveFaviconKey` stores favicons keyed by the literal environment hostname (e.g. `192.168.64.2`) when `readPreparedConnection` returns `null`. Later, `useFaviconForThreadUrl` canonicalizes that same host to `local` once the prepared connection is available, so the stored favicon is never found and the lookup returns `null`. This causes permanent favicon misses when a favicon arrives before the prepared connection is ready, because the write key and the read key don't match. Consider deferring `resolveFaviconKey` until the prepared connection is available, or applying the same canonicalization at write time regardless of connection readiness.

✅ Resolved in a3d1463cd1f3ea54d90befc34700bc959c725381

🟠 **High** `src/browserHistoryStore.ts:33`

`normalizeHistoryUrl` unconditionally strips the URL fragment, so hash-routed SPAs lose their route in history. Visiting `http://localhost:3000/#/settings` stores `http://localhost:3000/`, and reopening it lands on the wrong page. For hash routers the fragment is the navigation state. Consider preserving `parsed.hash` instead of clearing it.

✅ Resolved in f8b7ccb53626ff0553f34ceda4f1a05cca4b47f2

### Navigate drops captured favicon state **Medium Severity** `navigate` rebuilds `PreviewTabState` without `favicon` / `faviconOrigin`, so every navigation clears a captured icon from tab state. `capturedFaviconsRef` still dedupes that origin, so same-origin revisits and URL-bar reloads skip re-capture and the icon never returns on the tab until a different origin is captured first. That also blocks favicon recency updates in the renderer store.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/desktop/src/preview/Manager.ts#L1353-L1354`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/10e48726a332c70903820f90e3569797a6a839c5/apps/desktop/src/preview/Manager.ts#L1353-L1354)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 10e48726a332c70903820f90e3569797a6a839c5. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Stale favicon capture race **Medium Severity** `captureFavicon` only reads `capturedFaviconsRef` before the async `session.fetch` and writes the dedupe key after `update` succeeds. Two in-flight captures for the same webview/origin can both pass the check; the slower one can overwrite a newer favicon, or a stale revisit capture can clobber a fresher one after an A→B→A navigation.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 60385e0a1423af199661397be47449a0c7516dda. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `preview/usePreviewBridge.ts:83`

When a thread is remapped from one project to another (`projectKey` changes), the favicon is never recorded under the new project. `lastRecordedFaviconKey.current` still matches the current favicon, so `faviconRecordForDesktopState` returns `null` for subsequent state updates and the pending-favicon effect skips recording because `pendingFavicon.current` is also `null`. The favicon that was already stored under the old project key is silently missing from the new project.\n\nThis happens because the dedupe refs (`lastRecordedFaviconKey`, `pendingFavicon`) are only reset when the bridge subscription re-subscribes, not when `projectKey` changes. Consider resetting `lastRecordedFaviconKey.current` to `null` inside the `[projectKey, threadRef]` effect so the favicon is re-evaluated and stored under the new project key.

✅ Resolved in a3d1463cd1f3ea54d90befc34700bc959c725381

🟠 **High** `src/browserHistoryStore.ts:33`

`normalizeHistoryUrl` returns the full `URL.href`, including `parsed.username` and `parsed.password`. Visiting a URL like `https://user:secret@example.com/` therefore persists the embedded credentials in `byProjectKey` and writes them to `localStorage`, where they survive restarts and are exposed in recent-history displays or to any same-origin script. Stripping `parsed.username` and `parsed.password` before returning `parsed.href` prevents credentials from being stored.

✅ Resolved in 60385e0a1423af199661397be47449a0c7516dda

### Pending titles drop host remapping **Medium Severity** When a title is queued before the thread has a project key, `environmentHostname` is discarded. On drain, `setTitleForUrl` runs without it, so `titleLookupKey` cannot match a remapped page URL to a localhost history entry and the title never sticks on WSL/remote environments.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L255-L257`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/a6ae4d709363885cba1f25e30b0e4cb6ec375803/apps/web/src/browserHistoryStore.ts#L255-L257)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a6ae4d709363885cba1f25e30b0e4cb6ec375803. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `src/browserHistoryStore.ts:129`

`registerThreadProject` drains queued titles by calling `setTitleForUrl` without `environmentHostname`, so pending titles are never matched to their history entries. `setTitleForUrl` resolves the title by comparing `titleLookupKey` values, which map loopback and environment hosts to `local` — but only when `environmentHostname` is passed. When it is omitted (as in the drain loop), the loopback/environment host normalization is skipped, so the lookup key for the pending title never matches the key of the existing entry, and the title is silently dropped. Store `environmentHostname` on `PendingTitle` and pass it through when draining.

✅ Resolved in e4f00ba018ed75ffd1114b0f0bb29181f8201815

### ICO favicons often fail capture **Medium Severity** The `image/x-icon` / `image/vnd.microsoft.icon` branch returns null when the body is not a classic ICO header or when the verbatim data URL exceeds the cap, and never falls through to the `nativeImage` resize path used for PNG/JPEG. Mislabelled PNG favicons and ordinary multi-size `.ico` files above roughly 6KB are dropped, so local sites keep falling back to the globe.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 84e85153b4dee4321b68437dc8abc1190e8bcb87. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Favicon lookup already collapses those hosts; title matching does not.

When `recordFaviconForThread` returns `false` (because `resolveFaviconKey` returns `null` while thread registration is still pending), the favicon from the current state is silently dropped. The code sets `lastRecordedFaviconKey.current = faviconRecord.key` only on the success branch but leaves `faviconNavigationPending.current = false` via the `else if`, so a later state event with the same favicon and `navigationPending === false` will be skipped by the `key === lastRecordedKey` dedup in `faviconRecordForDesktopState` — yet `lastRecordedKey` was never actually recorded. The oversized PNG/JPEG path correctly rejects undecodable buffers and leaves dedupe untouched.

title: feat(chat): refine V2 conversation UI
body:
## Summary

This is a stacked follow-up to #2829 and targets `t3code/codex-turn-mapping` directly.

- add an Appearance preference for keeping branch and worktree context below the composer after a thread starts
- collapse the draft-only context strip with the same timing and easing as the composer docking transition
- move right-panel layout controls into the right-panel header
- reuse the existing dropdown glass surface for thread details and align branch/action selectors with the shared panel row styles
- redesign imported project actions as a full-width split row and use the wrench-based Actions control in compact headers
- simplify queued and steering intent markers and tighten collapsed-turn spacing
- make provider errors expandable while retaining Markdown details, provenance, and inspector controls
- clarify context-handoff presentation with a bidirectional icon and cleaner endpoint layout
- hide synthetic workspace-preparation activity and transient interruption-request rows across web and mobile

## Impact

The V2 conversation and thread-details surfaces are quieter and more consistent, while preserving diagnostic information behind disclosure controls. Existing users retain draft-only composer context by default and can opt into keeping it visible for active threads.

## Deliberately excluded

- message-details visibility preference
- grouped delegated-task/subagent rows
- internal agent-wake filtering
- optimistic queued-message removal
- automatic thread-title generation
- provider-derived handoff color mapping
- local `.t3orc` runtime data

## Validation

- 163 focused timeline, settings, composer, mobile, contracts, and client-runtime tests passed
- focused project-actions panel rendering test passed
- typechecks passed for web, contracts, client-runtime, mobile, and desktop
- `git diff --check` passed

## Notes

- The full `ProjectScriptsControl.test.tsx` file still has two compact-control assertion failures that reproduce on the #2829 base; the stacked change does not modify those code paths.
- No browser pass or visual assets were captured for this draft.

Model: GPT-5.6 Sol (xhigh) via Codex in T3 Code.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Mostly UI, settings defaults, and timeline filtering with tests; no auth or data-path changes beyond a new client setting defaulting to prior draft-only behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **Appearance** preference (`persistComposerContextStrip`, default off) so branch/worktree controls can stay below the composer in active threads, not only on new-thread drafts. The strip **animates** in/out with the same timing as composer docking, and right-panel **layout controls** move into the right-panel header.
> 
> **Thread details & panels:** Thread details use **dropdown glass** instead of removed `panel-glass`; branch and project-action selectors align with shared panel row styles. Imported project actions render as a full-width split **Actions** row with wrench icon in compact headers.
> 
> **Timeline & feed:** User intent markers (queued/steer) are simplified (icon + label above the bubble). Collapsed turn folds lose extra border/padding. Provider **errors** use expandable `<details>` with markdown and inspector. Context handoffs use a bidirectional icon and cleaner endpoint layout without a middle dot separator.
> 
> **Noise reduction (web + mobile):** Synthetic workspace-preparation commands and transient `run_interrupt_request` rows are filtered from timelines/feeds; only the terminal interrupt result remains visible. Shared helper `turnItemIsWorkspacePreparation` lives in client-runtime.
> 
> Docs link **Appearance** preferences; README and settings search include composer context.
>

title: fix(server): restore worktree branch naming in the v2 orchestrator
body:
Stacked on #2829. Complements #5176, which restored title generation — this PR covers the other half of the regression: worktree branch naming.

## Problem

On the v2 orchestrator, threads stay on their temporary `t3code/<hash>` branch forever. `ThreadLaunchService` only generated a branch name when `workspaceStrategy.branch === undefined`, but the web client always passed a temporary `t3code/<hash>` name — so generation never fired, and unlike v1 there was no later rename pass.

## Fix

The server now owns worktree naming:

- Without an explicit branch, the worktree is provisioned **immediately** under a server-invented temporary `t3code/<8hex>` name (`randomUuidV4` + shared `buildTemporaryWorktreeBranchName`).
- After the workspace metadata dispatch, a background fork generates the real name, renames via `git branch -m`, and dispatches a `:branch-rename` metadata update. Name generation never sits on the critical path in front of worktree creation, the setup script, or the provider turn (matching v1's concurrency, where the rename raced the turn). This also removes the previous awaited-generation path, so branchless launches (scheduled tasks, MCP-driven) no longer block provisioning on an LLM call.
- If generation or the rename fails, the temporary name sticks with a logged warning.
- The web client stops inventing temporary branch names. `branch` stays optional in the contract: explicit user-chosen branch names are respected verbatim, and temporary names from clients that still send them (mobile's offline outbox) are renamed server-side the same way.

## Notes

- Generated branch names follow the existing v2 `feature/<slug>` convention rather than v1's `t3code/<slug>` wrapper; happy to align to v1 if the namespace matters downstream.
- Minor UX: the sidebar shows no branch for a beat longer on brand-new threads (until the workspace metadata event lands) since the client no longer has a name to show optimistically; the "Preparing worktree" run phase covers that window.

## Testing

- 5 new `ThreadLaunchService` tests: server-invented temp names, off-critical-path rename (run reaches `starting` while generation is gated behind a deferred), explicit-branch passthrough, generation-failure fallback, existing-worktree rename.
- Full orchestration-v2 suite: 558 passed, 54 files (on top of the merged #5176).
- Typecheck clean for `t3` and `@t3tools/web`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes thread launch provisioning and git branch lifecycle on the critical path for new worktrees; failures degrade to temp branch names rather than blocking launch.
> 
> **Overview**
> Restores v2 thread launch behavior where worktrees stayed on client-supplied **`t3code/<hash>`** branches and never got LLM-generated names, because **`ThreadLaunchService`** used that name verbatim and did not run a rename pass like v1.
> 
> **Branch naming** — When no explicit branch is sent, the server provisions immediately under a temporary **`t3code/<8hex>`** name (via **`buildTemporaryWorktreeBranchName`** / **`randomUuidV4`**), instead of awaiting **`generateBranchName`** or using the removed **`thread-<id>`** fallback. After workspace metadata is written, a background fork generates a real branch name, **`git.renameBranch`**, and a **`thread.metadata.update`** with command id **`branch-rename`**; failures are logged and the temp name remains. Explicit user branches are unchanged; client-supplied temp names (legacy/mobile) still get renamed the same way, including **`existing_worktree`** launches.

title: fix(orchestrator): Prevent redundant delegated completion turns
body:
## Summary

- [Decision brief](https://xudl9al0nyl8.postplan.dev): evidence, product
  tradeoffs, and the final durable-delivery design.
- Coalesce app-owned delegated child terminals into one durable, queued
  completion delivery per parent-run cohort, with at most one successor for
  results that arrive after the first delivery starts.
- Let a parent acknowledge a terminal result through `task_status` or an
  untruncated direct-child read, then cancel its unstarted stale delivery
  without deleting the result.
- Hide automatic completion deliveries from web and mobile queue controls while
  preserving their scheduler priority and allowing their prompt to appear if
  the delivery enters the conversation.
- Add durable Stop, task-cancel, Queue Remove, archive, delete, and recovery
  barriers around server-owned completion delivery.

## Problem and Fix

| Problem and Why it Happened | Fix |
| --------------------------- | --- |
| #4499 delegated-task-parent-wake deliberately created one real queued parent continuation for every async child terminal. Sibling completions therefore fanned out into repeated parent turns and timeline output. | A parent-run cohort reserves one delivery that terminal siblings join before it starts. A late result gets at most one bounded successor instead of recursively re-arming the parent. |
| A parent could read a result through `task_status` or its direct child timeline, but the scheduler had no durable observation signal, so its queued completion still ran later. | Terminal `task_status` reads and untruncated direct-child terminal-result reads durably acknowledge the task and remove it from the queued delivery. Status-only waits, prompt-only reads, and truncated results do not acknowledge. When no owned task remains, the queued run is cancelled. |
| Stop, Queue Remove, archive, and delete cancelled transient work but did not own or dispose future completion delivery. | Durable cohort and task-delivery states make these actions replay-safe barriers. Results remain inspectable even when their automatic delivery is disposed. |
| Server-created completion messages looked like normal queue entries and exposed Edit, Reorder, and Steer controls. In particular, a Grok wake could be converted into interrupt-and-restart steering. | Server commands reject those mutations, while web and mobile omit automatic completion entries from visible queue controls. The scheduler still gives every surviving hidden delivery priority over ordinary queued messages, and the prompt remains visible once it enters the conversation. |

## Defensive Fixes

| Problem and Why it Happened | Fix |
| --------------------------- | --- |
| Provider lifecycle updates can persist a full run or subagent row captured before a later acknowledgement or Stop barrier. | Projection storage preserves newer delivery state when a stale provider row omits it, and run finalization intentionally excludes its old cohort snapshot. |
| A continuation offer can survive in memory while a cohort is acknowledged, disposed, archived, deleted, or replaced by a later generation. | The worker rereads durable projection ownership immediately before dispatch and drops an offer that is no longer current. |

## Validation

- Focused MCP, continuation-worker, projection, Claude allowlist,
  scheduler-priority, and hidden queue presentation tests pass.
- Direct-child read coverage proves that only the complete terminal result,
  rather than `t3_thread_wait`, a prompt-only page, or a truncated result,
  acknowledges delivery.
- Isolated real-provider verification proved one durable delivery for one child,
  coalescing for two async Grok children, acknowledgement persistence, and
  durable acknowledgement and retraction before a queued delivery starts.
- `vp check` passes with no warnings or lint errors, all 15 typecheck tasks pass,
  and the desktop production build succeeds.
- The current source tip was integrated into the v2.1 trial, where focused
  queue and delega

findings.body:
### Stale cohort overwrites delivery **High Severity** `CheckpointCaptureService` reads a run snapshot, then later commits `run.updated` with that full `...run`, including `delegatedCompletion`. Unlike `RunExecutionService`, it does not strip cohort state, and projection preservation only helps when the field is omitted. A child can reserve or update delivery after the read and before the commit; the completed event then writes the older cohort back and drops the newer reservation, so the parent wake never dispatches.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProjectionStore.ts#L141-L149`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/d137da8ffefc05ef419a4cda99aeec34a6b19853/apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProjectionStore.ts#L141-L149)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d137da8ffefc05ef419a4cda99aeec34a6b19853. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Concurrent acknowledges fail reads **Medium Severity** Completion-delivery acknowledge is rejected when ownership is already `acknowledged`, while `readTask` only skips that dispatch from a pre-lock snapshot. Concurrent `task_status` and `t3_thread_read` use different `commandId`s, so the loser can hit that reject and fail the whole MCP read even though the result payload was already in hand.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/server/src/mcp/OrchestratorMcpService.ts#L884-L915`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/d137da8ffefc05ef419a4cda99aeec34a6b19853/apps/server/src/mcp/OrchestratorMcpService.ts#L884-L915)

### Delivered tasks can re-arm wakes **High Severity** `planDelegatedCompletionDelivery` treats only `acknowledged` and `disposed` as terminal ownership states, so a `delivered` task still falls through into a new reservation when wake-policy is upgraded while the parent is live. That re-arms another automatic parent completion after the result was already delivered, which is the redundant-turn failure this change is meant to prevent.

title: feat(sidebar-v2): bring back thread pinning
body:
Sidebar v2 shipped without a way to keep an important thread from drifting: active cards hold creation order, and the settle/snooze lifecycle eventually parks everything on a shelf. There was no way to say "this one stays on top."

Pinning brings that back. Pinned threads render as full cards above the inbox behind a thin divider (no header text — the pin glyphs carry the meaning). A pin overrides the lifecycle: while pinned, a thread can neither auto-settle out of sight nor be hidden by snooze state, and its settle/snooze affordances yield to a single Unpin. Unpinning returns the thread to wherever it would otherwise classify.

Pin state is server-backed and syncs across devices, following the snooze template layer for layer:

- Contracts: optional `pinnedAt` on thread + shell (pre-pin servers still decode), `thread.pin`/`thread.unpin` commands and events, and a `threadPinning` capability so clients hide the affordance under version skew.
- Server: decider cases (idempotent by re-emission, archived threads rejected; no other invariants — a pin only ever promotes visibility), projector, projection pipeline, `pinned_at` column via migration 036, and snapshot/persistence plumbing.
- Web: pinned partition ahead of snooze/settle, pin glyph on cards, Unpin hover action, Pin/Unpin in the context menu.
- Mobile: same partition in thread list v2, Unpin as the swipe primary on pinned rows, Pin in card long-press menus.

Covered by focused tests at each layer: decider pin/unpin invariants, projector lifecycle, persistence round-trip, client reducer events, and a mobile partition test proving a pinned thread cannot vanish into a shelf.

---

title: fix(web): blink the terminal cursor again
body:
## What

The web terminal's cursor stopped blinking when the renderer moved from xterm.js to libghostty-vt. This restores it.

![Terminal cursor blinking again](https://pub-b182a4071edc4521829926b34990540b.r2.dev/files/547cf389-65f4-4f57-b2b7-de6de9ec0561/t3code-terminal-cursor-blink.gif)

## Why it broke

The old renderer was constructed with `cursorBlink: true`, so every T3 terminal blinked regardless of what the program inside it wanted. libghostty-vt's built-in default is a steady cursor, and the Canvas renderer only toggles the cursor while the terminal reports `cursorBlinking` — that is, when a program turns blinking on through DECSCUSR (`CSI 5/3/1 q`) or DEC mode 12. A plain shell prompt does neither, so the cursor sat still.

## What changed

- `GhosttyTerminalCore` sets `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_DEFAULT_CURSOR_BLINK` when it creates a terminal, so a session starts blinking and returns to blinking on `CSI 0 q`. Programs still own the cursor: a steady DECSCUSR style or `CSI ?12l` turns the blink off, and `CSI ?12h` turns it back on.
- The option is applied again in `resetAndWrite`, because RIS restores Ghostty's built-in steady default. That is the path a reattach to an existing session takes, so without it a reconnected terminal came back steady.
- The blink phase machinery in `GhosttyTerminalSurface` was already in place (500ms half-cycle, reset to the visible phase on write and focus). It now runs through one predicate, `shouldBlinkTerminalCursor`, which also holds the cursor steady when the reader prefers reduced motion, next to the existing unfocused and hidden-cursor cases.

## Tests

- `runtimeAbi.test.ts` exercises the real vendored WASM: the default is steady, option 23 makes it blink, `CSI 2 q` / `CSI ?12l` override it, `CSI 0 q` / `CSI ?12h` restore it, and RIS drops back to steady (the reason for the second apply).
- `renderer.test.ts` covers the off phase repainting the cell without the inverted cursor glyph.
- `surface.test.ts` covers the blink predicate.

Verified in a dev environment — the GIF above is the terminal drawer in that build.

## Note

`apps/mobile`'s Android and iOS terminal views gate on the same `cursorBlinking` flag, so they blink only when a program asks. Matching them to this default is a separate change, not included here.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Terminal UI and embedder default cursor option only; no auth, data, or API surface changes beyond local terminal behavior.
> 
> **Overview**

title: feat(server): server-stamped task data shapes (stacked on #5219)
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Stacked on #5219** — merges into `t3code/native-subagent-observability`, not main.

Follow-up to the subagent observability PR: three write-time data-shape changes that let read-time complexity retire. Still zero migrations — everything rides `payload_json` and the existing `activity_id` upsert.

## Problem

The client fold compensates for append-only lifecycle rows at several points:

- Progress ticks append (2,700+ rows in a live dev DB vs ~400 start/terminal rows), so a large fleet's ticks can evict its own `task.started` rows out of the 500-row retention window — degrading the roster on full reload.
- Agent-vs-background classification is derived independently in three places (client fold denylist + legacy-marker heuristics, web session-logic, server liveness registry) that must agree.

## Solution

- **Progress upserts.** `task.progress` / agent-owned `tool.progress` persist under stable ids (`task-progress:<taskId>`), so each tick replaces the last through the existing upsert + replace-by-id apply in the projector and client reducer. One progress row per task; retention pressure from progress disappears.
- **`agentKind` stamp.** Ingestion stamps `"agent" | "background"` into every task linkage payload via `classifyTaskAgentKind` (new in contracts). Clients trust the stamp; the fold's denylist and marker sniffing remain only as a fallback for pre-stamp rows.
- **Canonical task-type sets.** `MONITOR_TASK_TYPES` / `INERT_TASK_TYPES` move to contracts; `ThreadBackgroundLiveness` consumes them instead of keeping its own copies.

Tests: classify unit tests in contracts, stamp-trust fold tests, ingestion suites updated for the stable ids (216 orchestration tests green).

---
Built by Claude Fable 5 via Claude Code.

title: test(server): catch client transfer regressions in CI
body:
Thread history can silently regress by sending an entire conversation or oversized projections back to the client. The test needs enough data pressure to catch that without making every CI run expensive.

This adds a deterministic stress history calibrated from heavy local Codex and Claude threads: 10 turns with five command tools and one retained 900 KB MCP result each, followed by a measured turn with 20 tools and a 1.1 MB retained result. It measures only thread transport: the gzip thread snapshot and the measured turn over the real RPC WebSocket with permessage-deflate. It also verifies that resuming the thread subscription from the HTTP snapshot sequence does not replay another snapshot.

PR and main CI runs upload a strict machine-readable result. A trusted workflow_run publisher, loaded only from the default branch, compares the PR result with the exact-base main result when available and updates one github-actions[bot] comment with baseline, observed impact, ceilings, and ceiling changes. The PR artifact is size-limited, schema-validated, rendered only as known numeric fields, and never executed. Stale workflow runs cannot overwrite a newer result.

The current calibration persists 9 MB of historical MCP results but projects them to a roughly 95 KiB decoded thread snapshot, about 5.5 KiB of snapshot wire traffic, and about 51 KiB decoded / 6 KiB wire for the live turn. Total client-bound wire traffic is about 11.6 KiB, with roughly 30% ceiling headroom. The focused test takes about 15 seconds. Blacksmith also publishes the exact measurements and compression diagnostics in the job summary.

Created by GPT-5.6 using the Codex harness in T3 Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches CI and fork-PR comment publishing with artifact validation, but production server behavior changes are limited to exporting `isThreadDetailEvent` and test-only measurement paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **end-to-end thread transfer budgeting** so CI can catch regressions that ship oversized thread snapshots or live-turn WebSocket traffic to the client.
> 
> A new live integration test seeds a **deterministic heavy history** (10 turns with large retained MCP payloads, then one measured turn) for **Codex and Claude**, measures **gzip HTTP snapshot wire/decoded size** and **WebSocket wire/decoded/message counts** (with **permessage-deflate**), checks that resuming a subscription from the snapshot sequence does **not** replay another snapshot, and **fails** if configured ceilings are exceeded. Optional env paths write a markdown job report and a strict **JSON artifact** consumed by automation.
> 
> **CI** uploads `thread-transfer-results` and appends the budget report to the job summary. A separate **`workflow_run`** workflow loads only **trusted default-branch** publisher code, validates artifacts (size + fixed schema, never executed), resolves the PR run and a **`main` baseline**, and **upserts one bot comment** with baseline vs PR impact, ceilings, and stale-head guards. Supporting harness tweaks use **deterministic test event IDs** and **drain** hooks after quiescence; `isThreadDetailEvent` is exported for the test.
>

### Corrupt baseline blocks PR report **Medium Severity** `publish` treats a missing baseline as optional, but `readResult` throws on an invalid or schema-mismatched baseline file. A bad `main` artifact then aborts the whole publish step, so a valid PR result never updates the comment.
Additional Locations (1) - [`.github/scripts/thread-transfer-report.cjs#L87-L97`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/344bc61d56c93e1a9cb94f6e7d5895953c93f981/.github/scripts/thread-transfer-report.cjs#L87-L97)

### Null head repo breaks filter **Medium Severity** The fallback PR filter requires `pull.head.repo.full_name` to equal `workflow_run.head_repository.full_name`. With `GITHUB_TOKEN`, associated pull requests from forks often have a null `head.repo` while the workflow payload still includes `head_repository.full_name`, so the sole matching PR is dropped and publishing is skipped even though the previous logic would have resolved it.

### Missing artifact clears PR comment **Medium Severity** When the latest CI run for the current PR head has no `thread-transfer-result.json`, `publish` still upserts a warning comment. That replaces an earlier successful thread-transfer report for the same commit after a cancelled run, failed job, or any completion where the artifact was not uploaded.
Additional Locations (1) - [`.github/scripts/thread-transfer-report.cjs#L285-L288`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/c13ff82cc9b3d9c3366bd406461d5222a92001ee/.github/scripts/thread-transfer-report.cjs#L285-L288)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c13ff82cc9b3d9c3366bd406461d5222a92001ee. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `scripts/thread-transfer-report.cjs:240`

When `workflow_run.pull_requests` is empty, the fallback lookup at line 246 picks the first open PR whose head matches `source.head_sha` and publishes the report there. A single commit can be the head of multiple open PRs (the same branch targeting different base branches), so this publishes the artifact and baseline comparison to an arbitrary PR among them — not necessarily the PR that triggered the run. The fallback should use the source run's ref or PR metadata to disambiguate instead of relying on `listPullRequestsAssociatedWithCommit` result order.

✅ Resolved in a3372d7db744e5b6ba0df54d70d4da652ef7ffd4

### Quiesced receipt precedes stream tail **Medium Severity** The live transfer test treats `turn.processing.quiesced` as turn completion, then reads `latestSequence` and stops the WebSocket queue when any streamed event reaches that sequence. In `CheckpointReactor`, the quiesced receipt is published before `thread.activity.append` is dispatched, so the captured sequence can lag the real projection head and `collectQueueUntil` can finish before the last client-bound events are counted in the wire delta.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/server/integration/TransferBudgetScenario.integration.ts#L42-L50`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/57de417534d9fe5ce659566571ee1d7553d5d437/apps/server/integration/TransferBudgetScenario.integration.ts#L42-L50)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 57de417534d9fe5ce659566571ee1d7553d5d437. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Global head stalls stream wait **Medium Severity** After the measured turn, the test waits for a `subscribeThread` item whose `event.sequence` is at least `harness.engine.latestSequence`, but `latestSequence` is the global orchestration log head while the subscription only forwards a whitelist of thread detail events (see `isThreadDetailEvent` in `ws.ts`). If the head event is omitted from that stream—e.g. `thread.meta-updated` from post-turn git branch drift or other non-detail thread or project events—the queue never satisfies the predicate and the live test times out after 10 seconds.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 57de417534d9fe5ce659566571ee1d7553d5d437. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `scripts/thread-transfer-report.cjs:320`

`publish` overwrites the PR comment with a stale result when the PR head advances between artifact download and comment upload. The head-sha staleness check happens in `resolve`, but `publish` never re-checks, so an older workflow run can clobber a newer comment after the PR has already been updated by a more recent run. Re-fetch the pull request immediately before `upsertComment` and skip the update when `pull.head.sha` no longer matches `PR_SHA`.

✅ Resolved in c13ff82cc9b3d9c3366bd406461d5222a92001ee

### WebSocket message cap too low **Medium Severity** The measured-turn WebSocket message budget was reduced to `20` while the PR calibration and the file comment describe roughly `24` observed messages and ~30% headroom (~`32`). If the live test still emits about 24 frames per provider, `transferBudgetViolations` fails CI even when transfer size is healthy.

### Total wire cap below sum **Medium Severity** After narrowing budgets to thread snapshot plus measured-turn WebSocket wire, `totalWireBytes` still caps at 2_900_000 while `threadSnapshotWireBytes` is 2_600_000 and `measuredTurnWebSocketWireBytes` is 320_000. title: feat(web): make pairing QR codes actually scannable, with endpoint choice
body: The pairing QR code was hidden behind a 16px hover icon and rendered at 88px, locked to whichever endpoint happened to be the default. Basically unusable: you had to know the icon existed, hover it without moving away, and hope the default endpoint was the one your phone could actually reach. Now each pairing link row has a Share button that expands an inline panel with a 168px QR code, an endpoint picker (LAN / Tailscale IP / Tailscale HTTPS / hosted app), the full pairing URL, and copy actions. The old split "Copy pairing URL for: X" button and its dropdown are folded into the panel, so the row stays compact and there is one place to share a link. Details worth noting: - Loopback endpoints are never offered as QR targets: a phone scanning `127.0.0.1` would dial itself. They remain in the copy flow via URL, where same-machine use is legitimate. - The picker keys endpoints by their unique `AdvertisedEndpoint.id`. The persisted-default key (`endpointDefaultPreferenceKey`) collapses endpoints of the same type (e.g. two Tailscale IPs), so it is only used to match the saved default. - The QR sits on a white card intentionally: inverted codes fail on many camera apps, and the card doubles as the quiet zone. - Endpoint choices show plain-language hints ("Devices on the same network", "Opens the hosted app, no install needed") instead of `title`-attribute-only metadata. - The picker uses radiogroup semantics and the Share button is wired to the panel with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`. - Selection logic is extracted to `ConnectionsSettings.logic.ts` with focused tests (loopback exclusion, unique-id selection, stale-selection fallback). The clipboard-unavailable fallback dialog is unchanged. title: fix(server): keep regenerated titles on topic
body:
Regenerated titles can drift toward the latest assistant finding or operational follow-up, especially after the original request falls out of the recent context window.

This gives regeneration its own subject-selection guidance and keeps the opening user message inside the existing 8,000-character budget alongside the recent tail. Opening image context is retained too.

## Testing

title: fix(mobile): reconnects no longer shift the thread list
body:
When an environment reconnected on mobile, the connection status appeared as a row above the thread list. Every reconnect pushed all the rows down, then popped them back when it resolved. Jarring, and it happens constantly.

Now the header's brand slot doubles as the status surface. While an environment is unavailable, the T3 Code lockup ("Threads" on the iPad sidebar) fades to a spinner plus a status label in the same place, then fades back on reconnect. Nothing is inserted into the list, so its geometry never moves.

An 800ms debounce gates the swap, so the sub-second blips that make up most reconnects now show nothing at all. Offline and error states get a wifi-slash icon instead of the spinner, and tapping the status still opens environment settings the way the old pill did.

Covers every surface the old pill lived on: iPhone Home (both the liquid-glass and pre-glass header paths), Android Home, and the iPad sidebar in both native and custom chrome. The pill component is deleted; its display logic stays in `workspace-connection-status.ts` with tests extended for the new presentation helper.

title: fix(server): allow remote updates with database migrations
body: Remote background-service updates refused every release containing a SQLite migration because rollback could only swap binaries safely. The service launcher now snapshots all SQLite files before a trial and restores them before rollback. Trials can run migrations normally, and a protocol bump makes older launchers fail closed until one local service update installs the new safety boundary. Verification: - 22 focused service launcher and update tests - server typecheck and targeted lint - CLI parsing suite - production server and standalone launcher bundles Generated by GPT-5.6-sol in T3 Code using the Codex harness. --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Changes core self-update, SQLite persistence, and launcher recovery paths; protocol 1 launchers must perform one local service update before remote DB migrations work. > > **Overview** > Remote background-service updates can include SQLite migrations by **snapshotting and restoring** the database (main file plus WAL/SHM) around trial candidates, instead of blocking any release that changes the schema. > > **Launcher protocol 2** adds required `dbPath` on pending updates and `request-update` IPC; the launcher backs up SQLite once per trial, restores on rollback/failure (with a durable restore marker if interrupted), and drops the snapshot after commit. **Preflight** no longer compares migration manifests—it only requires a launcher at the new protocol. **SQLite startup** always runs WAL and migrations (the trial skip path is removed). **Self-update** passes `dbPath` into `requestUpdate`. > > **Boot service install** fails with `BootServiceUpdatePendingError` when service state already has a pending remote update, so local install does not overwrite launcher/state; connect onboarding treats that like other background-setup skips. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 0aaf284faba0e58abd9eb1549175b6e785f0c063. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). > [!NOTE] > ### Add database snapshot and rollback support for remote server updates > - Bumps `SERVICE_LAUNCHER_PROTOCOL` to 2 and adds `dbPath` to pending update state, update requests, and IPC messages so the launcher knows which database to snapshot. > - Before starting a trial run, the launcher snapshots the SQLite database (including WAL and SHM files); if the snapshot fails, the trial is aborted and the previous version is restored. > - On rollback or trial failure, the launcher restores the database from the snapshot before restarting the previous version, with a crash-safe restore marker to handle interrupted restores. > - `install` in [bootService.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5374/files#diff-9ec1426b86c5c9f63a503a0c78a87a5165a6460ca539deb5c365bda9ff0576f0) now aborts with `BootServiceUpdatePendingError` when an existing `service-state.json` indicates a pending remote update, preventing state from being overwritten mid-update. > - The SQLite persistence layer always runs migrations on startup; trial-mode conditional behavior and the `trial` flag are removed from both the persistence layer and the launcher client. > - Risk: Callers of `BootServiceError` must now handle `BootServiceUpdatePendingError`; `requestUpdate` requires `dbPath`; child IPC messages without `dbPath` are rejected. > > > > Macroscope summarized 0aaf284. > >

title: fix(web): keep terminal font settings reliable
body:
## Problem

The typography controls could leave the terminal in two incorrect font states:

- Advanced mode still inherited an unset terminal family from the code-font preference, so changing Code changed active terminals.
- Custom terminal faces were checked before their styles loaded. A proportional face could pass through the monospace fallback, then render against a fixed cell grid after loading, leaving glyphs behind the cursor and link underline.

## Fix

- inherit the code family only in simple typography mode; Advanced uses the terminal preference or terminal default
- load every style the canvas renderer can request before accepting a custom terminal family
- validate regular, bold, italic, and bold-italic advances across representative glyphs, including the space glyph
- repeat fixed-width validation when later font-loading events arrive
- keep terminal previews and default labels aligned with runtime resolution
- cover simple/Advanced preference resolution, fixed advances, and post-load rejection with regression tests

## Validation

- full GitHub Actions test suite
- `vp run --filter @t3tools/web typecheck`
- targeted `vp lint --report-unused-disable-directives` on changed files
- targeted `vp fmt` and `git diff --check`
- direct Node runtime assertion for strict advance validation

Follow-up to #5103.

title: fix: reconnect faster after remote server updates
body:
A remote server update restarts the server for about 15 seconds, but the client shows "Resuming" for up to ~33s. Separately, the relay tunnel becomes reachable ~5s after the new server starts listening.

Measured from `boot-service.log` across recent updates: old server dies at T+2s, new server listens at T+7-9s, relay tunnel reachable at T+13-15s.

## Client: nudge reconnect for the whole restart, not just once

The update flow forked a fiber that waited for the **first** `backoff` state and called `retryNow` once. That nudge lands at ~T+2s while the server is still down for another ~11s, so it is wasted. The supervisor then climbs its normal `1/2/4/8/16s` ladder and attempts land at ~3, 5, 9, 17 and 33s, which is how a ~15s restart becomes a ~33s wait.

Now it nudges on **every** backoff entry, with a one-second sleep before each one, so attempts stay ~1s apart for the whole restart window. The sleep is the pacer: a connection that fails instantly (ECONNREFUSED, or a 502 through the relay) re-enters backoff immediately and would otherwise spin a tight retry loop.

The fiber stays `Effect.forkChild`, so it is interrupted as soon as the update command settles. With that in place the 30s cap is unnecessary and now matches `SERVER_UPDATE_RESUME_TIMEOUT`, covering the realistic restart window instead of cutting off at 30s.

The loop is extracted as `nudgeReconnectDuringUpdateRestart` so it is testable without standing up an `AtomRegistry`; two tests cover the repeated-nudge count and the pacing.

## Server: what the ~5s actually is

Worth stating plainly, since it changes what is fixable here: the ~5s between `Listening on http://127.0.0.1:3773` and `Relay client process started` is **not** local serialization behind activation. Activation opens ~50ms after the listen log, and nothing is logged in the remaining window. The time is spent inside the two relay calls in `reconcileDesiredCloudLinkWith`, dominated by server-side Cloudflare control-plane work on `POST /v1/client/environment-links` — a serial chain of tunnel create, configure, and DNS mutations. Measured locally: secret store I/O is under 1ms total, the ed25519 keypair is genuinely first-run-only, and network transport for both POSTs is ~0.6s.

That chain runs on every boot because `releaseManagedTunnelOnShutdown` deletes the tunnel at shutdown (a deliberate Cloudflare per-tunnel billing tradeoff), so the next startup always pays full tunnel-creation latency instead of reusing an existing tunnel.

So moving the reconcile earlier would not have bought the 5 seconds — the work is remote and already starts promptly. Keeping the reconcile gated on activation is also the safe choice: it preserves the finalizer ownership rule at `server.ts:564` and keeps a rolling-back trial from fighting the previous version for the tunnel. I left that gate alone and removed the one piece of local dead time on the path, the 250ms sleep in front of the first attempt. Routes are already serving when activation opens the gate, and the retry schedule covers what the sleep hedged against.

The real leverage is relay-side (keep the tunnel alive across restarts, or parallelize the independent legs of `provision`), which is out of scope here.

## Validation

- `packages/client-runtime` tests: 524 passed
- `apps/server` tests: 1846 passed, 7 skipped
- typecheck and lint clean

Note: running the server suite on a machine with a live T3 server leaks `T3_SERVICE_LAUNCHER_CONTEXT` into the test process and fails 125 tests on `main` as well. Unsetting it makes the suite pass on both `main` and this branch.

title: fix(server): stop tying codex text-generation temp files to the caller's scope
body:
Stacked on #2829. Follow-up to #5309 — explains and fixes why branch renaming still didn't work in real builds even though #5309's rename path executed.

## Diagnosis (from a live Alpha build containing #5176 + #5309)

Titles generated fine, branches stayed `t3code/<hash>`. Traces showed the rename fork running and failing in 22ms:

```
TextGenerationError: Text generation failed in generateBranchName: Failed to write temp file
  [cause]: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/var/folders/.../T/t3code-codex-schema-10580-Ahg5y9/a30ebec4bc02'
```

`runCodexJson` writes its `--output-schema` / `--output-last-message` temp files with `makeTempFileScoped`, whose `Scope` requirement leaks to the ambient fiber context (swallowed by the generic `S["DecodingServices"]` in the return annotation, so it never typechecked as missing). The branch rename fork inherits its context from the `launchThread` RPC request, whose scope has long since closed by the time the fork runs — and registering a finalizer on a closed scope runs it **immediately**, deleting the temp directory between creation and write. Hence ENOENT on every branch generation, with #5309's deliberate fallback keeping the temp name.

Title generation kept working because #5176 runs it on the durable effect worker, whose ambient scope stays live — which is exactly why the symptom split (titles ✓ / branches ✗).

## Fix

Use unscoped `makeTempFile` and remove the per-file temp directories in `runCodexJson`'s existing explicit `Effect.ensuring(cleanup)` instead. Generation is now self-contained regardless of which fiber calls it, and the temp *directories* (previously left behind by the file-only unlink whenever the scope path wasn't exercised) are cleaned up too.

## Testing

- New regression test: `generateBranchName` succeeds with an explicitly **closed** ambient `Scope` provided — fails with the ENOENT error before the fix, passes after.
- Full `CodexTextGeneration` suite: 18 passed.
- Typecheck clean for `t3`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> 
> **`writeTempFile`** now uses unscoped **`makeTempFile`** with explicit cleanup: **`removeTempFileDir`** on write failure, and **`runCodexJson`**’s existing **`Effect.ensuring`** removes the full temp directories (not single-file unlinks) on success or failure.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel pending anchor scroll on minimap jumps**

When a user jumps via the minimap while a just-sent message is still being positioned, this path no longer tells `ChatView` that manual navigation happened before starting its own `scrollToIndex`. `onTimelineAnchorReady` schedules the anchor positioning over animation frames, so a minimap jump made during that window can still be followed by the pending anchor scroll and pull the viewport back to the sent message; the previous `onManualNavigation()` call on this path cleared those pending anchor refs before the minimap scroll. Add an equivalent cancellation before starting the minimap jump.

### Live follow lost after scroll-back **Medium Severity** The streaming follow effect now returns unless mode is `anchoring-new-turn`, while `maintainScrollAtEnd` stays off whenever `anchoredEndSpace` is present. After a user scrolls away and back to the end during a send, mode becomes `following-end` but the anchor message id is never cleared, so neither T3 nor LegendList follows further stream growth until the scroll-to-end pill clears the anchor.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx#L525-L528`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/221222ccb8ef11e7c54b02a5ba638f280425c990/apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx#L525-L528)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore end-follow while an anchor remains**

When a sent message remains as `anchorMessageId`, `MessagesTimeline` still passes `maintainScrollAtEnd={false}` whenever `anchoredEndSpace` is truthy, so this effect is the only fallback that keeps an at-end timeline pinned during later streaming/final timeline updates. If `onIsAtEndChange` flips `timelineScrollModeRef` back to `following-end` while that anchor is still present, this new guard skips the old `scrollToEnd` path and subsequent rows/size changes can stop following even though the user never manually navigated away.

title: ci: label-gated hosted-web preview deploys
body: Testing client-only web changes today means running the whole stack locally or waiting for a release. Anything visible on app.t3.codes had no per-PR preview. This adds a \`preview:web\` label that, when applied to a same-repo PR, deploys the web app to Vercel on that push and every subsequent push. The deploy is a plain non-prod, non-aliased deployment into the existing hosted-web project, so the \`latest\`/\`nightly\` channel aliases are never touched. A sticky PR comment carries the deployment URL. How it fits the existing architecture: - The hosted app is already a pure static SPA with no backend proxy. \`apps/web/vite.config.ts\` already derives \`VITE_HOSTED_APP_URL\` from \`VERCEL_URL\` on non-production deploys, so a preview self-identifies as the hosted-static app at its own unique URL with zero build-config changes. - Previews omit the T3 Connect cloud config (Clerk/relay), so they boot into manual pairing. The intended flow: spin up a server, run \`t3 pair --tailscale\`, open the pairing URL against the preview origin (or paste host + code in Settings → Connections). Packaged servers already send wildcard CORS, and HTTPS/WSS over Tailscale Serve satisfies mixed-content rules. - Label-gating keeps Vercel build volume sane and restricts secret-bearing deploys to deliberate opt-ins; fork PRs are skipped entirely. title: fix: smooth remote server updates
body:
A remote server update restarts the server in ~9 seconds, but the client stayed disconnected for 90+ seconds, and the progress UI was a three-step rail (Download / Install / Resume) where "Install" is a sub-second launcher handoff and "Resuming" meant nothing to most people.

Two changes:

**Keep the managed tunnel across update restarts.** Shutdown released the Cloudflare tunnel, so every update forced the replacement tunnel's hostname route through 1-2 minutes of edge propagation — measured on a live update: server listening at T+9s, first inbound request at T+96s. An update handoff always brings a server right back (new version, or the old one after rollback), so the tunnel is never orphaned. The release now checks the launcher's durable state file and skips deletion when an update is pending; the next boot respawns the connector from the stored config against the same tunnel and is reachable as soon as it connects (~T+12s). Explicit unlink and non-update shutdowns still release, so the per-tunnel billing hygiene is unchanged.

**Calmer, honest update UI.** The version-skew banner is no longer an amber warning: it reads "Server update available" with the raw versions (unreadable for nightlies) in a tooltip. The in-flight rail becomes a single status row, "Downloading…" then "Restarting…", matching what actually happens; failures keep the row with the rollback reason and a Retry action.

Together with #5404 (merged), an update should now be: ~6s "Downloading…", ~10s "Restarting…", reconnected.

title: perf(server): stop shipping full MCP tool results in thread payloads
body:
MCP tool calls were exempt from activity payload slimming: `projectActivityPayload` early-returns on `itemType === "mcp_tool_call"`, so the full tool result rides along in every snapshot and live event. On MCP-heavy threads this dominates the wire — one imported thread ships 3.2 MB gzipped, with two-thirds of its post-slimming bytes being unslimmed MCP payloads (worst single call: a GitHub `fetch_pr` result at 1 MB).

The exemption existed because both clients render `payload.data.item` in the expanded work-log row. The fix keeps exactly the fields that row renders (`tool`, `server`, `status`, `arguments`, `appContext`, `error`, `durationMs`, plus `toolName`/`input` for the Claude-adapter shape) and summarizes the result to one 84-char line, same as regular tool output. Full payloads stay in SQLite, so an on-demand detail endpoint can be added later without data loss.

Measured against a real db seeded with six representative threads (2,991 MCP activities): **12.2 MB of MCP payload JSON drops to 546 KB (95.6% reduction)**. Both provider payload shapes (Codex `data.item`, Claude/OpenCode `data.result`) verified against real rows.

Note: this trades away in-app access to full historical MCP results (they were previously visible in the expanded row). Per the pagination investigation, that's an accepted temporary loss; the data remains in persistence.

title: fix(server): drop superseded tool updates from snapshots
body:
## Problem

A `tool.updated` row is the in-flight snapshot of a tool call. Once the call finishes, the `tool.completed` row carries the final state and both clients fold every matching update into it — so the updates are pure wire cost. One real database holds 47k such rows; a single thread carries 3,291 of them.

## Fix

Filter superseded `tool.updated` rows out of thread snapshots, mirroring the existing `dropStaleContextWindowActivities` dedup. Snapshots only — live `thread.activity-appended` events are untouched, so updates still stream in real time and the completion supersedes them on the client exactly as before. Full payloads stay in SQLite.

Two guards on which rows are safe to drop:

- **Per turn.** A live `thread.reverted` makes the client discard whole turns. A completion in a different turn could vanish and leave the dropped update unrepresented, so matching is scoped to the turn — same reasoning the context-window function documents.
- **Later completion only.** A later update under the same identity is the *next* call reusing that identity and is still in flight, so it survives.

### On the match key

The spec assumed `data.toolCallId`. I checked a real database first: **zero** of 48.8k `tool.updated` rows carry one, and neither do any `tool.completed` rows — it only appears on ACP-sourced payloads. The clients already handle this in `deriveToolLifecycleCollapseKey` (web `session-logic.ts`, mobile `threadActivity.ts`): they prefer `toolCallId` and fall back to an itemType/title/detail triple. This mirrors that exactly, so retention matches what the clients would have collapsed anyway. Rows with no identity at all pass through, since the clients never collapse those either.

## Verification

Replayed the shipped projection over the 40 largest threads in a real database: `tool.updated` rows 29,312 to 592, total wire size 257MB to 36MB (that figure includes the pre-existing context-window dedup).

Tests mirror the context-window dedup cases: superseded rows dropped, unsuperseded kept, cross-turn completion does not drop, post-completion update kept, `toolCallId` matching when present, identity-less rows kept, live events untouched, and the collapsed work log unchanged versus full history. Full server suite green (1878 passed).

> Changes snapshot projection for thread history (HTTP/WS reads) with intentional divergence from client adjacency-based collapse; low risk to persistence and live streaming, but reviewers should confirm snapshot UX matches expectations on parallel-heavy threads.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Shrinks thread detail snapshots** by stripping `tool.updated` activities that a later `tool.completed` in the same turn already supersedes—redundant in-flight rows clients would fold anyway.
> 
> Adds `toolLifecycleIdentity` (prefers `data.toolCallId`, else itemType/normalized title/detail like web and mobile) and `dropSupersededToolUpdatedActivities`, wired into `projectThreadDetailSnapshot` after existing context-window dedup. Updates with no identity, completions in other turns, or updates after a completion are kept; interleaved parallel calls may drop updates the UI would still show as separate rows (~1.5% of drops). **`thread.activity-appended` is not filtered**—streaming behavior stays the same.
>

title: perf(swift-ios): fix streaming markdown that never rendered and stop per-publish rework
body:
Streaming a turn on the native iOS app burned way more CPU than it needed to, and a few of the hot paths had genuine stability hazards hiding in them. This PR is a sweep of both, built on the swift rebuild branch.

## The headline problems

**Streaming markdown never actually rendered.** The message view debounced renders by 200ms (trailing), but streamed revisions arrive every 80ms, so the timer restarted forever and never fired. Users saw raw `**bold**` and backtick soup for entire turns, then a hard layout swap at the end. Now a 150ms leading-edge throttle keeps messages as live markdown while streaming.

**The markdown cache destroyed itself during streaming.** It was keyed by the full message source, so a single 60-second turn inserted ~750 throwaway intermediate entries and evicted every completed message in the thread (limit is 512). Scrolling back after a turn was all cache misses, each a synchronous main-thread parse. Now keyed by the precomputed content fingerprint, streaming intermediates stay out of the cache entirely, and the final streamed render is promoted into it on completion.

**Every publish redid work that hadn't changed.** During an active turn the client publishes ~4x/second, and each publish did a synchronous disk read + JSON decode of the environment catalog, re-parsed ~10 ISO8601 timestamps per thread through two formatters, and rebuilt the full provider catalog (hundreds of structs). All three are now cached with invalidation on their actual write paths.

**The terminal buffer was unbounded.** Run a verbose build in the terminal tab and the app appended forever, re-laying-out a multi-megabyte string per output chunk. That's a hang/OOM, not a slowdown. Capped at 256KB of tail.

## Stability fixes

- Two `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` calls on server-supplied IDs (model picker, agent awareness) trapped on duplicate keys, which the codebase elsewhere documents as occurring in real snapshots. Both are now first-wins reduces.
- WebSocket RPC: `connected()` iterated `unary.keys` / `subscriptions.keys` across suspension points while reentrant completions mutate those dictionaries (undefined behavior); the connection loop and keepalive held strong `self`, so a released client could never deinit and its 5s heartbeat ran forever; a subscription teardown racing a reconnect could send `Interrupt` for a request ID the server had reassigned to a live subscription; reconnect backoff now jittered so multi-environment setups don't stampede token mints in lockstep.
- QR scanner camera session kept running when the app backgrounded with the scanner open; it now stops on disappear and resumes on return.
- Cold-start deep links whose thread hadn't loaded yet were silently stranded; pending navigation requests now retry as snapshot data lands.

## Smaller wins

- Rendered markdown blocks are `Equatable` (inline runs compare by reference via the existing streaming run cache), so only the changed tail of a streaming message re-renders instead of all blocks.
- Table column widths are computed once on the background render pass instead of measuring every cell's `AttributedString` per body evaluation.
- The home list's permanent 1Hz timer idles to 60s when no thread is working; the thread header's per-second `TimelineView` only runs while working.
- DPoP JWK/thumbprint cached (was a SHA-256 + key derivation on every managed request); shared `JSONEncoder/Decoder.t3` instances (were rebuilt per call); `sortedKeys` dropped from throwaway `JSONValue` bridging encodes; ISO8601 formatter reused in command builders.
- Activity logs sort by raw ISO string instead of parsing dates in the comparator; attachment hydration skips text-only threads; approval/input resolution only touches transcripts containing the request; diff hydration anchors use binary search; local attachment previews decode off-main through the shared thumbnail cache; markdown caches drop on memory warnings.

All 256 tests pass, zero build warnings, verified clea

🟡 **Medium** `Core/WebSocketRPC.swift:449` `WeakOwner.installConnection` promotes `value` to a strong local and keeps it alive across the `await value.connected()` call, which itself awaits each queued `connection.send`. 🟡 **Medium** `Chat/MarkdownMessageView.swift:136`

`drain()` unconditionally clears the shared `renderTask` in its `defer`, so when `cancel()` is called while a render is suspended in `MarkdownRenderCache.document`, a new `submit` starts a replacement task, and the old task then unwinds, the old task's `defer` erases the reference to the replacement task. The replacement is then left running untracked, so a later revision's `submit` sees `renderTask == nil` and starts a second concurrent drain. The two drains can finish out of order and deliver an older rendered document after a newer one, causing the visible markdown to regress. Capture the current task identity and clear `renderTask` in the `defer` only if it still refers to the exiting task.

title: feat: paginate thread loading with user-anchored turn windows
body:
## Problem

Long threads are heavy to open, especially on mobile. The heaviest observed thread (161 turns, 23k activities) ships 8.4MB of JSON on every open, all of which must be parsed, held in client state, and persisted to the mobile cache. On many-turn threads, the most recent 10 turns are only 2-6% of the bytes.

## Solution

Opt-in pagination of the thread detail snapshot, cut on user-anchored turn boundaries:

- **Server**: `GET /api/orchestration/threads/:id` accepts `turnLimit` + `beforeCursor`. The window is everything from the Nth-last turn-with-a-user-pending-message onward, so subagent/fan-out turns ride along and the first page always contains the last N user prompts (verified against real data: fan-out bursts run 35+ consecutive subagent turns). Responses carry `page: { beforeCursor, hasMore, snapshotSequence }` with an opaque exclusive cursor returning disjoint older slices. A 150-raw-turn ceiling bounds pathological fan-out. The WS fallback snapshot honors the same opt-in via the subscription input.
- **Compatibility**: pagination is strictly opt-in and capability-gated (`threadSnapshotPagination` in server config). Old client + new server and new client + old server both keep full-snapshot behavior.
- **Shared client state**: initial loads request the last 10 user turns; `loadOlderTurns` fetches 20 more per call. Consistency rules: a fresh snapshot replaces all loaded history (no stale-revert resurrection), in-flight pages are discarded when a revert/snapshot/deletion rewrites history or when the page was read from a projection behind the loaded state, and merged pages never advance the live-event dedupe sequence. All covered by state-machine tests.
- **UI**: a plain "Load earlier turns" header row on web and mobile; LegendList's `maintainVisibleContentPosition` anchors scroll on prepend.

No schema migration: the migration-029 indexes cover the bounded queries (verified with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN against a 45k-activity fixture; worst-case bounded reads run in single-digit ms).

Measured on the heaviest real thread: initial fetch drops from 8.4MB to 1.0MB wire (~1/8th), and a full page-by-page walk reproduces the exact row set of an unwindowed fetch with zero overlap between pages.

## Testing

- 7 new server tests for window resolution, cursor semantics (foreign/malformed cursor degradation, disjointness/coverage walk), and the turnless-thread edge case
- 7 new client state-machine tests for the race rules
- Full server (1880) and client-runtime (615) suites green; typecheck and lint clean across the workspace
- Live smoke against the seeded worktree db: windowed first page returns exactly the last 10 user messages with hasMore, older pages are disjoint, full walk covers all 815 messages

---

> **Medium Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **opt-in, capability-gated** thread detail pagination so long threads open with a small recent window instead of the full history.
> 
> **Server** exposes `turnLimit` and `beforeCursor` on HTTP thread snapshots and WS subscribe fallbacks. Windowing walks back **user-anchored turns** (subagent turns ride along), returns `page` metadata with an opaque keyset cursor, and uses a new `projection_turns` keyset index. Malformed or foreign cursors degrade to the first page.

> **Client-runtime** loads the last 10 user turns initially and fetches 20 more per “load earlier” via `requestOlderThreadTurns`, with epoch/lock/watermark rules so reverts, fresh snapshots, and stale pages cannot corrupt merged history. Thread cache schema bumps to **v3** so old clients cannot treat a partial window as complete.

thread.body:
[claude-fable-5] RESPONDING ON BEHALF OF THEO
-----

Dismissing — the duplication scenario cannot occur, and the suggested fix would break paging on active threads.

The replay-append hazard requires a replayed event to touch a row that came from the merged page. It cannot: (1) pages contain only turns strictly older than the loaded window (disjoint slices), and `mergeById` keeps the loaded row on any id collision; (2) streaming `thread.message-sent` appends only target the active message, which lives in the newest turn — always in the loaded window, never sourced from a page; (3) non-streaming `message-sent` for an existing id *replaces* text (`threadReducer.ts` case "thread.message-sent"), which is idempotent under replay; (4) replayed turnless activities carry recent `created_at` values outside the older page's time bound, so the page never contained them.

Requiring `snapshotSequence === loadedSequence` would reject nearly every page on an active thread — the projector advances continuously between the client's watermark and the page read — making "load earlier" fail precisely when threads are busiest. Rejecting only regressions (`<`) is the intended bound; not advancing `lastSequence` from a page is deliberate so live events between the watermark and the page's sequence still apply to the loaded window.

thread.body:
[claude-fable-5] RESPONDING ON BEHALF OF THEO
-----

False positive. Per RFC 9449 §4.2, the `htu` claim is "the HTTP target URI ... without query and fragment parts", and this codebase implements that on both ends: `normalizeDpopHtu` (`packages/shared/src/dpopCommon.ts:11`) strips `search` and `hash`, and the verifier (`packages/shared/src/dpop.ts:134`) runs the server-observed request URL through the same normalization before comparing against the proof's `htu`. Query parameters never participate in proof binding on either side, so signing against `requestUrl` without the window params is correct — a paginated fetch over a DPoP relay connection verifies exactly like an unpaginated one. (If proofs were bound to full URLs, every existing GET with query params would already be broken.)

title: fix(web): align composer inline chips with prompt text

## Summary

The Prompt font preview's inline skill pill sat low relative to surrounding text when custom prompt fonts were used. The first pass corrected the outer pill placement; this follow-up corrects the smaller label glyph position inside that pill.

The shared composer inline-token wrapper uses a small em-based negative vertical alignment. The smaller skill label gets a scoped em-based relative offset so its glyph bottom aligns with surrounding prompt text without moving the pill box or changing the editor's line height; shared file and terminal-context labels retain their existing positioning.

title: feat: expand pull request review context and panel tabs
body:
## Dependency

This is an upstream stacked follow-up to #4849. It is based directly on #4849's current head (`08225ba0`) and is not intended to replace that PR.

The temporary upstream base branch `stack/pr-4849-base` points exactly at that commit so this PR's commit list and Files changed view contain only this follow-up:

- `92f8ba5e1 refactor(web): share diff rendering foundations`
- `8b10e5bf0 feat(pull-requests): expand omitted diff context`
- `9393ecc32 feat(web): keep pull requests open as panel tabs`

This PR should merge only after #4849. Once #4849 lands, retarget this PR to `main` and delete the temporary base branch.

## Why

The in-app review flow in #4849 had three connected gaps:

1. Host patches contain only changed hunks. Expanding omitted lines therefore could not work reliably, especially when the local checkout did not have the pull request's exact remote revisions.
2. Diff styling, virtualized geometry, and inline comment composition had drifted across the thread diff, file preview, and pull request review surfaces.
3. A thread treated its pull request panel as a singleton, so opening another review replaced the first instead of preserving both as tabs. The compact panel chrome also did not reflect refreshed pull request state.

## What changed

### Shared diff foundations

- Added `StyledDiffCodeView`, the single web adapter around Pierre's `CodeView`. It keeps app styling and virtualized row measurements together so visual changes cannot silently desynchronize scrolling geometry.
- Replaced the file-only `LocalCommentAnnotation` and pull-request-only composer with `DiffCommentAnnotation`, shared by file previews, thread diffs, and pull request diffs.
- Extracted normalized full-file loaders with comparison-scoped cache keys for local Git comparisons and host-backed pull request comparisons.
- Added a lint restriction that directs new `CodeView` usage through the shared adapter.

### Expand omitted pull request context

- Added the typed `pullRequests.diffFileContents` RPC through contracts, authorization, WebSocket dispatch, client-runtime state, the pull request service, and provider adapters.
- GitHub resolves either the pull request base/head pair or a selected commit's parent/head pair, then reads both revisions through the raw contents API.
- GitLab performs the equivalent lookup with merge-request diff refs or commit parent refs and the repository files API.
- New, deleted, changed, and renamed files are handled explicitly. Invalid commit SHAs, binary files, unsupported hosts, and files above the 1 MB expansion limit produce bounded errors.
- The pull request Code tab supplies Pierre with full-file contents, so readers can reveal omitted context without checking out or fetching the review branch locally. Commit-scoped diffs retain a separate comparison identity.

### Keep reviews in compact panel tabs

- Pull request surfaces are keyed by project, repository, and number instead of one singleton ID. Existing persisted singleton state migrates to the new shape.
- Multiple reviews can coexist as peer tabs beside a thread, and refreshed open/draft/closed/merged state colors the corresponding tab icon.
- Empty-panel actions correctly disable Terminal when there is no project thread, and the pull request page can collapse and restore its detail panel with the standard layout control.
- The detail header now centers repository, pull request number, title, author, branches, changed-file count, and additions/deletions. The head branch can be copied directly, conflicts have a dedicated actionable row, and secondary agent handoffs live in the overflow menu.
- Reviewer display is condensed into accessible avatar stacks, while duplicate title, branch, and state metadata is removed from the Summary tab.
- User documentation calls out opening linked reviews in compact right-panel tabs without leaving the conversation.

## Impact and scope

- GitHub and GitLab reviews can reveal unchanged context directly in the i

🟠 **High** `pullRequest/GitLabPullRequestCli.ts:963`

`readFile` rejects any file whose contents include the Unicode replacement character `U+FFFD` (`\uFFFD`), classifying it as binary. A legitimate UTF-8 text file that intentionally contains that character — for example, a documentation file discussing encoding errors — is therefore reported as `GitLabDiffFileContentsUnavailableError` with reason `"binary"` instead of being returned. The check assumes `U+FFFD` can only appear as a decode artifact, but it is also a valid Unicode scalar that can appear in source text. Consider dropping the `\uFFFD` check and relying on the null-byte and truncation checks alone.

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/GitLabPullRequestCli.ts:513`

When `decodeMergeRequestListJson` drops malformed rows, the cursor's `delivered` count undercounts the raw rows consumed, so the next page request starts too early via `page`/`slice` and returns already-seen rows. The next slice never catches up because every batch with malformed rows repeats the undercount. `decodeMergeRequestListJson` already returns `rawCount` for this purpose; `listPage` should advance the cursor by that raw count rather than by the kept item count.

🟠 **High** `pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts:534`

`matchesUnsortedListing` drops pull requests from the `reviewing` listing when the viewer was requested as a reviewer through a team. The fallback path only checks `item.reviewRequestLogins`, which contains only individual logins, so PRs whose only review request is a team the viewer belongs to are silently excluded.

✅ Resolved in 68638575f810df407c98ec72af8965455ef4ced9

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts:854`

`readFile` only reports `binary` when the decoded stdout contains a NUL byte, so binary files whose bytes happen to contain no NUL are returned as text instead of failing with the `binary` error. The process runner has already decoded stdout to a string, so non-UTF-8 byte sequences arrive as replacement-character-corrupted content in `oldContents`/`newContents`, feeding invalid full-file content into diff expansion. Consider using the raw bytes or a stricter text- validity check (e.g. rejecting undecoded/replacement characters) rather than relying solely on NUL detection.

✅ Resolved in 68638575f810df407c98ec72af8965455ef4ced9
