### GitLab root commit expansion fails **Medium Severity** Commit-scoped diff expansion on GitLab still fails for root commits even when the file is new. `getCommitDiffRefs` rejects an empty parent before `changeType` is considered, so readers cannot expand omitted context for initial-commit files the way GitHub now allows.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/server/src/pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts#L813-L825`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162/apps/server/src/pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts#L813-L825)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Collapsed PR panel cannot reopen **High Severity** Collapsing the pull requests detail panel clears the URL selection and sets `isOpen` false while keeping surfaces, but reopen bails out because `selectActiveRightPanelSurface` returns null whenever the panel is closed. The layout control still looks available via `surfaces.length`, so restore appears broken after collapse.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Panel key omits project **Medium Severity** Pull request surfaces are now keyed by `projectId`, `repository`, and `number`, but the mounted `PullRequestDetailPanel` React key still uses only `repository#number`. Switching between two open tabs that share the same repository and number under different projects can reuse panel state instead of remounting the correct review.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/rightPanelStore.ts#L153-L174`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/9393ecc324fad4ff990384cd4595f01916f7f436/apps/web/src/rightPanelStore.ts#L153-L174)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9393ecc324fad4ff990384cd4595f01916f7f436. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### GitLab expansion never wired **High Severity** `GitLabPullRequestCli` implements `getMergeRequestDiffFileContents`, and the PR claims GitLab can expand omitted context, but `GitLabPullRequestProvider` never exposes `getDiffFileContents`. `PullRequestService.diffFileContents` only calls that optional provider method, so GitLab reviews always fail expansion with “This host cannot expand unchanged pull request lines,” while GitHub is wired correctly.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/server/src/pullRequest/PullRequestService.ts#L902-L925`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/9393ecc324fad4ff990384cd4595f01916f7f436/apps/server/src/pullRequest/PullRequestService.ts#L902-L925)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9393ecc324fad4ff990384cd4595f01916f7f436. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

findings.body:
🟡 **Medium** `routes/_chat.pull-requests.tsx:606`

`toggleRightPanel` reopens the last-selected pull request after a filter change has already cleared the selection. Selecting a PR, collapsing the panel via the toggle, then changing a state/involvement/host/project filter causes the next press of the panel toggle to restore `lastSelected.current` — a PR from the previous filter view — showing the detail panel with no matching row in the filtered list.

`lastSelected` is a ref that is never reset when filters change and `clearedSelection` is applied, so it survives across filter switches. Consider clearing `lastSelected.current` whenever a filter change clears the selection, or validating that `lastSelected` still belongs to the current filter scope before restoring it.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts:744`

`getPullRequestDiffFileContents` fails for a commit-scoped diff against a repository's root commit. The jq expression `[.parents[0].sha, .sha]` produces an empty `baseRef` because a root commit has no parents, and the subsequent `!baseRef` check returns `GitHubPullRequestReadError` even though every file in a root commit is `new` and the old side is never read. Consider producing an empty/sentinel `baseRef` when `.parents` is empty so the validation passes for root-commit diffs.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟠 **High** `pullRequest/PullRequestReviewBar.tsx:58`

Two race conditions let one pull request's review summary leak into another. The `useEffect(() => setBody(""), [reviewKey])` runs *after* the first render on a new PR, so that render still holds the previous PR's `body` — an immediate submit sends PR A's summary text with PR B's review. The comment on line 61–63 says this reset is meant to prevent exactly that, but a passive effect cannot clear stale state before it is read.

Additionally, `setBody("")` on line 87 runs after a successful submission without verifying the component still represents the same `reviewKey`. Since the panel stays mounted across PR switches and the textarea stays editable while `pending`, a user can submit PR A, switch to PR B, type B's summary, and then have A's delayed success callback erase B's text.

Consider keying the summary state by `reviewKey` (e.g. `useState` with a keyed reset or a per-key map) so stale text is never observable, and guard the post-submit reset so it only fires when the submitted key is still current.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟠 **High** `pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts:467`

When `sorted` is `false`, `involvementArgs` drops every search qualifier — `review-requested:<viewer>` for the reviewing tab and `is:unmerged` for the closed tab are both omitted. The fallback read therefore returns unrelated pull requests (anyone's, including merged ones) instead of preserving the requested filters. The comment explains the fallback avoids search because the index returned nothing, but `--author` still applies for authored PRs, so dropping only the `review-requested:` and `is:unmerged` qualifiers (while keeping `--author`) would leave the authored fallback correct while fixing reviewing and closed. Consider preserving the involvement and state filters on the fallback path, or document why the fallback intentionally widens the result set.

No longer relevant as of 68638575f810df407c98ec72af8965455ef4ced9

🟠 **High** `diffs/DiffCommentAnnotation.tsx:96`

When `pending` is `true`, the submit button is disabled but the ⌘/Ctrl+Enter keyboard shortcut still calls `onComment`, so a user can trigger duplicate submissions while one is already in flight. Add `!pending` to the ⌘/Ctrl+Enter condition to match the button's guard.
<details>
<summary>Also found in 1 other location(s)</summary>

`apps/web/src/components/pullRequest/PullRequestReviewAnnotation.tsx:193`

> The textarea's ⌘/Ctrl+Enter handler invokes `send()` even while `pending` is true, unlike the Reply button which is disabled during that state. Pressing the shortcut again before the first reply completes can therefore call `onReply` multiple times and post duplicate replies (and rapid repeated keydowns can start multiple requests before the parent rerenders). Guard `send`/the key handler with the pending state.

</details>

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/bitbucketPullRequestJson.ts:503`

`decodeCommitsJson` discards `decoded.success.next`, so pull requests whose commit list spans multiple pages silently receive an incomplete commit timeline — only the first page of commits is returned. The function reads `next` from the decoded page but never includes it in the result, unlike the other page decoders in this file. Consider including `next` in the return type (or threading pagination through the caller) so remaining pages are fetched.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟠 **High** `pullRequest/PullRequestReviewBar.tsx:86`

When a review submission succeeds, `clear(reviewKey)` deletes **all** pending comments for that pull request — including ones the user added while the request was in flight and that were **not** sent to the server. The `pending` flag only disables the buttons in this bar; it does not prevent inline comment composition elsewhere, so a comment added during the request is silently lost when the older submission resolves. Consider clearing only the comment IDs that were actually submitted, or blocking comment mutations for this review key while `pending` is true.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/AzureDevOpsPullRequestCli.ts:231`

`listPullRequests` can get stuck paging through the same rows forever when a page contains malformed entries. The `truncated` flag is computed from `decoded.success.rawCount`, but `--skip` is advanced by the count of decoded rows the service hands over. When malformed rows are skipped during decoding, the cursor advances by fewer rows than Azure actually returned, so the next request re-skips the same offset and returns the same malformed rows again — a page of all malformed rows loops indefinitely, blocking access to older pull requests. The `--skip` offset must advance by the raw row count consumed, not the decoded count.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/BitbucketPullRequestProvider.ts:62`

`reasonFor` classifies every HTTP 403 as `unauthenticated`, but Bitbucket returns 403 when a validly authenticated account lacks permission for a specific repository or operation. The service then treats this as a credential problem, telling the user to reauthenticate and hiding the real permission failure. Only 401 means the credentials themselves are unusable; 403 should remain `failed` so the request-specific permission error surfaces.

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestProvider.ts:217`

When `cli.listReviewThreadComments` fails, the fallback sets `viewer.didAuthor` to `true`, which causes `gitHubViewerPermissions` to strip the `approve` and `request-changes` verdicts — disabling those controls for every non-author on a transient GraphQL failure. The fallback comment says an unknown permission should keep controls live and let GitHub refuse the write, but `didAuthor: true` does the opposite for verdicts and also incorrectly grants thread resolution to read-only non-authors. Consider using a fallback that does not assert authorship — e.g. `{ canUpdate: true, didAuthor: false }` — so the unknown-permission state leaves controls live without narrowing verdicts or granting resolution.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

findings.body:
🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/PullRequestListFilters.tsx:56`

Clicking an already-selected filter pill clears the open pull-request detail panel even though the filter value does not change. Each pill's `onClick` calls `onChange(option.value)` unconditionally, and every route caller spreads `...clearedSelection` into the update, so re-selecting the active involvement, state, or host pill sends `clearedSelection` and closes the panel.

Guard each `onClick` so `onChange` is only called when the value actually changes. The same applies to the `All` button and each provider button in `PullRequestProviderFilter`.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/bitbucketPullRequestJson.ts:527`

`decodeStatusesJson` silently drops any build statuses beyond the first page. When Bitbucket paginates the statuses response, the function ignores the page's `next` URL and returns only `checks` from the first page, so additional checks never appear in the pull request UI. Unlike the other decoders in this file that return the `next` URL for the caller to follow, this one returns a bare array with no pagination info.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟠 **High** `pullRequest/PullRequestSummaryTab.tsx:370`

The `CommentComposer` holds its draft in local state but is not keyed by pull-request identity, so when the reused `PullRequestSummaryTab` switches from one pull request to another, React preserves the component and its `body` state. A draft typed on PR A remains visible on PR B, and submitting it posts the text to PR B using the wrong `projectId`, `repository`, and `number`. Add a `key` to the `CommentComposer` keyed on the pull-request identity so React remounts it — and resets its draft — when the detail changes.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/GitLabPullRequestCli.ts:433`

`listPage` ignores `input.cursor.delivered` and always requests only `limit + 1` rows. Because `updated_before` is inclusive, when `limit + 1` or more merge requests share the cursor timestamp, every subsequent page returns the same prefix of rows that `PullRequestService` has already seen. The walk reports `truncated: true` but never advances past those rows, so older merge requests at or beyond that timestamp are never reached — pagination stalls, repeatedly returning the same set. The continuation needs to account for `delivered` (skip rows already handed over at the boundary timestamp) so the walk can advance past them.
<details>
<summary>Also found in 1 other location(s)</summary>

`apps/server/src/pullRequest/PullRequestService.ts:264`

> `nextListCursor` cannot advance when at least `limit` change requests share the boundary timestamp. The next inclusive provider query returns the same top `limit` rows; `seenAt` filters all of them locally, but line 264 emits the same timestamp again, so every subsequent page repeats an empty slice forever and remaining rows at that timestamp (and all older rows) are unreachable. The continuation needs a provider-side tie-breaker/offset or another way to fetch beyond already-seen boundary rows.

</details>

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

🟡 **Medium** `pullRequest/PullRequestTimelineTab.tsx:27`

`overflows` and `expanded` are never reset when `body` changes, so if an updated pull request payload replaces a previously long comment with a shorter one (same event ID, reused component), the component still shows a `Show more`/`Show less` control and keeps its expanded state from the old content. This happens because `setOverflows` only transitions to `true` and the `useLayoutEffect` does not clear `overflows` or `expanded` when the effect re-runs for a new `body`. Consider resetting both states on body change — for example, resetting `overflows` and `expanded` to `false` at the start of the effect — so overflow is recomputed fresh for the new content.

✅ Resolved in 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

`pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts:765`

Nothing failed underneath this branch — the refs read succeeded and simply carried no usable shas — so the `new Error(...)` exists only to satisfy `GitHubPullRequestReadError`'s required `cause`, and the reported message becomes "returned an unreadable getPullRequestDiffFileContents response", which is not what happened. The siblings above (`GitHubDiffCursorError`, `GitHubDiffCommitError`, `GitHubViewerLoginUnavailableError`) are the pattern for exactly this: a dedicated tagged error with structural attributes and no cause. Consider adding e.g. `GitHubDiffRevisionsUnavailableError` with `command`, `cwd`, `number` and the optional `commit`, deriving `message` from those fields.

`pullRequest/GitLabPullRequestCli.ts:718`

Same as the GitHub side: the commit decoded fine and just has no parent, so this synthesizes an `Error` purely to fill `GitLabMergeRequestReadError`'s required `cause` and reports the failure as an unreadable response. Consider a dedicated tagged error carrying `command`, `cwd` and the commit sha, with `message` derived from those fields and no invented cause — matching `GitLabDiffCommitError` next to it.

No longer relevant as of 9f095cf893de85d47ee9eada821c00390ea5c162

`pullRequest/GitHubPullRequestCli.ts:799`

Two semantically distinct refusals (over the 1 MB expansion limit, binary blob) are encoded only in the text of a manufactured `Error`, and the file path — the context a caller needs — lives in that string instead of a structural attribute. Neither case has an underlying failure to preserve as `cause`. title: fix(web): plans stop hijacking the UI, fold into chat instead
body: Plans were way too aggressive in the UI: a 340px sidebar that auto-opened on every turn with steps, usually to show process boilerplate ("Verify: typecheck, lint, targeted tests", "Commit and push", "Babysit CI"). Analysis of real usage: 100 of 122 threads with plans ended with a stale all-checked strikethrough list still occupying the panel, and 22% of plan snapshots had only 1-2 generic steps — sometimes a single line commanding the whole column. Before: Now: The useful kernel is one line: which step is Claude on right now. So plans are now two quiet indicators instead of a surface: - **Inline folded chip in the transcript** — one collapsible row per turn that produced plan steps: segment bar, current step, n/m count. Anchored where planning began, expands in place to the full list, mutes when done, scrolls away with history. - **Current step on Working indicators** — sidebar rows show the in-progress step (with n/m) in place of the branch while a thread works, and the in-chat "Working for Xm" line appends it. Backed by a small in-memory `ThreadPlanProgress` registry on the server (same pattern as `ThreadBackgroundLiveness`), exposed as an optional `planProgress` field on the thread shell and cleared on turn settle / session exit — stale state is structurally impossible. Deleted outright: `PlanSidebar`, the `plan` right-panel surface kind (storage v9 migration drops persisted plan tabs), the auto-open effect and per-turn dismissal tracking, the `autoOpenPlanSidebar` setting, and the "Tasks" toggle in the composer. The plan-mode proposed-plan card in the timeline is unchanged. Verified with tsgo across contracts/server/web/desktop/client-runtime, mobile tsc, vp lint, full web (1818 tests) and server (1888 tests) suites, plus new focused tests for `deriveTurnPlans` and `ThreadPlanProgress`. title: fix: prevent reconnect loops during server stalls
body:
Server event-loop stalls could make one delayed pong kill the RPC connection, then immediately reconnect into the same expensive bootstrap work. Users saw repeated disconnects and `Syncing...` even when the underlying network was healthy.

This tolerates short pong delays, uses a safer reconnect ladder, and avoids repeated bootstrap work by caching command and editor discovery and resuming shell state from an authoritative cursor. Failed HTTP snapshot refreshes still request a complete socket snapshot, trace attributes are bounded to preserve useful diagnostics, and sends attempted while disconnected now explain why they were not sent.

Focused tests cover pinger tolerance, wake recovery, shell synchronization, discovery caching, and trace truncation.

🤖 Final review fixes and PR cleanup by GPT-5.6 Codex using the Codex harness in T3 Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core connection supervisor, RPC protocol (patched dependency), and shell subscription resume semantics; mis-tuned wake/backoff or resume cursors could cause extra sync work or delayed reconnects.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens **client–server connection behavior** against event-loop stalls, aggressive reconnect loops, and expensive session bootstrap.
> 
> **Transport & supervisor:** Patches Effect RPC **ping/pong** to allow two missed 5s windows before closing (~15s silence). Raises the first reconnect delay from **1s → 3s** and, when a **foreground wake probe** fails, **skips the first backoff sleep** once (then normal backoff resumes). Supervisor and session tests are updated for the new timing and wake behavior.
> 
> **Connect cost:** Adds a **30s PATH command-resolution cache** in shared shell code and **60s memoized editor discovery** on the server so repeat connects avoid huge filesystem scans. **Trace file sink** now clamps oversized span attributes (including `db.query.text`) without mutating live spans.
> 
> **Shell sync:** On the same live RPC session, **foreground resubscribe** resumes from the in-memory `snapshotSequence` instead of always forcing a full HTTP refresh; failed HTTP refresh falls back to a full socket snapshot. New/rewritten shell-sync tests cover these paths.
> 
> **Web:** Sending while the environment is unavailable shows a **warning toast** (draft preserved) instead of silently attaching an annotation.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c44dad4598b2a28e1501b74b7ed6e02d2034dfe7. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<!-- If you delete either of the start / end markers from your PR's description, Macroscope will append its summary at the bottom of the description. -->
> [!NOTE]
> ### Harden connection resilience by fixing idle disconnects with backoff, pinger tolerance, and shell cursor reuse
> - Changes the `EnvironmentSupervisor` retry ladder first rung from 1s to 3s; a failed foreground wake probe now triggers an immediate reconnect instead of waiting for the first backoff sleep
> - Patches the Effect WebSocket pinger to tolerate two missed pong windows before closing, up from zero tolerance
> - Foreground resubscriptions on the same live session resume from the in-memory shell cursor; new sessions fall back to a full socket snapshot when the HTTP load fails

author: gfsaaser24

findings.body:
### Socket snapshot cannot enable resume **Medium Severity** When the HTTP shell refresh fails, `canResume` stays false for the whole RPC session because only a successful HTTP load sets `lastAuthoritativeSession`. Later resubscribes on that same session still omit `afterSequence` even after the socket already delivered a full snapshot, so every foreground wake repeats a full shell download instead of resuming from the in-memory cursor (thread sync resumes whenever in-memory data exists).
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c7aba013344111c694c8ba8c32399070d7308d0c. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `state/shell.ts:215`

When the HTTP snapshot load fails on a new session and the server delivers a complete snapshot via the cursorless socket subscription, `lastAuthoritativeSession` is never set to that session. Every subsequent foreground resubscription on the same healthy session retries the HTTP load instead of resuming from the now-authoritative in-memory cursor, and if HTTP still fails it downloads another full socket snapshot. `lastAuthoritativeSession` is only assigned inside the `Option.isSome(httpSnapshot)` branch, so any session that becomes authoritative through a socket snapshot is treated as non-authoritative forever. Consider setting `lastAuthoritativeSession` when a complete socket snapshot is applied in `applyItem` (or when `synchronized` arrives on a cursorless subscription), not only when the HTTP snapshot succeeds.

✅ Resolved in c44dad4598b2a28e1501b74b7ed6e02d2034dfe7

### Stale shell resume after HTTP fail **Medium Severity** On a new RPC session, `makeSubscribeInput` tries an authoritative HTTP shell refresh when `lastAuthoritativeSession` does not match. If that load returns `Option.none` (the documented “use the socket snapshot instead” path), the code still subscribes with `afterSequence` from the existing in-memory snapshot left over from cache or the prior session, so resume skips the full socket snapshot the fallback is meant to use.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fb2b8c52de4399083781290ee61648d71542fc9d. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Stale connected phase after wake **Medium Severity** When a foreground wake probe fails, the supervisor clears the RPC session and immediately retries, but it doesn't update the public connection state. This leaves clients believing the connection is still active, bypassing disconnected warnings and allowing sends against a dead session.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4e8e3a17f638bfdc776068bf2f029d4310bca17d. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

`src/shell.ts:510`

The PATH-scan memo is process-global mutable state: its lifetime is unbounded, it is not resettable per test/runtime, and it is shared by every consumer of `@t3tools/shared/shell` regardless of which layer provided `FileSystem`/`Path`. That hides a stateful dependency of `resolveCommandPathForPlatform` in a module global instead of representing it in the Effect environment.

Consider owning the cache in a layer, as the rest of the repo does (for example `Cache.makeWith` inside `make` in `apps/server/src/project/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts`, with `timeToLive` distinguishing hit/miss), and having `resolveCommandPath` acquire it via `yield* CommandResolutionCache` so the requirement shows up in the effect type. The manual TTL/eviction bookkeeping (`cacheCommandResolution`, `COMMAND_RESOLUTION_CACHE_*`) then goes away with it. The same PR already does this correctly one level up with `Effect.cachedWithTTL` in `ExternalLauncher.make`.

No longer relevant as of 6eb16ea5d4d452b203b7fd406d4de6a209c2c692

🟡 **Medium** `src/observability.ts:261`

`truncateTraceAttributes` only inspects top-level string values, so oversized strings nested inside arrays or objects are never clamped. Because `compactTraceAttributes` preserves nested structures (maps, arrays, `Error` objects), a large `error.stack` or any deeply nested string is serialized in full, defeating the 500-character clamp and still exhausting/rotating the trace sink. Consider recursing into nested structures so the length limit applies to strings at every depth.

✅ Resolved in 6eb16ea5d4d452b203b7fd406d4de6a209c2c692

### Trace clamp ignores 500 limit **Medium Severity** The `truncateTraceAttributes` function incorrectly truncates most string attributes to 200 characters, despite their intended `maxLength` of 500. This causes more trace context to be lost than designed for non-`db.query.text` attributes.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 06d6db3eba23278104a5091f8dee1d628cc2e768. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `src/observability.ts:269`

`truncateTraceAttributes` truncates every oversized string attribute to `TRACE_ATTRIBUTE_TRUNCATED_LENGTH` (200 characters) plus the suffix, even when the configured limit for that key is `TRACE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_LENGTH` (500). The function computes `maxLength` per key but ignores it when slicing, so a 450-character attribute is wrongly cut to 200 characters and 300 characters are discarded. Use `maxLength` for the slice instead of the fixed constant.

✅ Resolved in dec616668ba5e46e066c07d5120c66984edc924d

🟡 **Medium** `src/shell.ts:578`

The command resolution cache uses `Clock.currentTimeMillis` for TTL expiry, so a backward wall-clock adjustment keeps expired entries alive far past their 30-second TTL. After the system clock moves back, `cached.expiresAtEpochMs` stays in the future relative to the new `nowEpochMs`, so the cache keeps returning stale resolved paths or stale not-found results for added or removed executables until the wall clock catches up. Consider using a monotonic clock (e.g., `Clock.monotonicTimeNanos`) or a duration-based expiry for TTL comparisons instead of wall-clock time.

✅ Resolved in dec616668ba5e46e066c07d5120c66984edc924d

This is a false positive. In Effect 4, Effect.tryPromise catch maps a rejected promise into the typed error channel; it does not recover it as a success. title: fix(server): one disconnecting client no longer blocks every reconnect
body:
My machine stopped accepting connections and stayed broken. Reloading did nothing. The server was healthy and the relay was fine: the WebSocket authenticated, then the very first RPC died and the socket closed ~100ms later, on every attempt.

Editor discovery is memoized with `Effect.cachedWithTTL`, which stores whatever Exit the first caller produces — including an interrupt. Callers run it on the connection fiber under a timeout, so a client that disconnects mid-scan caches the interrupt. Every later connect then replays it, `server.getConfig` fails, and nothing can reconnect. Worse, each failed connect re-runs discovery and re-poisons the cache, so the 60s TTL keeps refreshing and it never self-heals. Only a restart clears it.

Cache the discovered set only on success. An interrupted scan now leaves the cache untouched and the next connect simply rescans. The memoization that #5561 added is preserved.

Trace from the stuck server, showing where the connection died:

```
EnvironmentAuth.authenticateWebSocketUpgrade  Success
SessionStore.markConnected                    Success
ws.rpc.server.getConfig                       Interrupted
SessionStore.markDisconnected                 Success
```

The regression test reproduces this: it fails on the current code with the same interrupt through the same `isExecutableFile` → `resolveAvailableCommand` stack, and passes with the fix. Verified by reverting the source and re-running. Full server suite: 1,901 passing, typecheck clean.

Introduced by #5561, which is in nightly `.1021`.

Made by Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches connection-time config path (`getConfig` / editor discovery) with custom caching semantics; scope is narrow and covered by a targeted regression test.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Editor discovery memoization no longer caches interrupts**, fixing reconnects that failed on every `server.getConfig` until restart.
> 
> `ExternalLauncher.resolveAvailableEditors` drops `Effect.cachedWithTTL` for a `Ref`-backed cache that **writes only after a successful PATH scan**. If discovery is interrupted (e.g. client disconnect mid-connect on the connection fiber), the cache stays empty and the next connect rescans instead of replaying the interrupt for the full 60s TTL. TTL expiry uses **`Clock.currentTimeNanos`** (monotonic), aligned with shell command-resolution caching.
> 
> A regression test interrupts discovery mid-scan and asserts a later call still returns editors.
>

title: fix(web): reading a thread clears Done; Woke is dismissible
body:
## Problem

Since #5486, opening and reading a finished thread no longer clears the sidebar's "Done" badge. That PR removed the visit-on-open effect in ChatView (to stop mere visits from eating the Woke signal) but didn't replace it for read tracking, so `lastVisitedAt` only updated on woke-acknowledge, settle, or archive. Any thread whose last turn completed after your stored visit showed Done forever.

## Solution

- **Reading clears Done.** ChatView stamps `markThreadVisited` with the open thread's `latestTurn.completedAt` (not `updatedAt`/now). This clears exactly the completion you're looking at while preserving #5486's woke semantics: a timer wake stamped later than the completion still shows its pill, and `markThreadVisited` never moves the timestamp backwards.
- **Woke banner in the open thread.** A woken thread now shows a dismissible info banner in the composer banner stack, so dismissal has a prominent home beyond the small sidebar pill (which stays clickable too). Dismissing uses the same acknowledgment as the pill; sending a message already clears it via the send path, as do settle and archive.
- **Merged/closed PR suppresses Woke.** If the thread's PR merged or closed while it was snoozed, the work is finished — no wake-up call needed. Applied consistently in the sidebar row and the banner.

Also moved the sidebar row's git-status/PR lookup above the status computation so Woke can see the PR state (no behavior change otherwise).

title: feat(web): drag pinned threads into your own order
body:
Pinned threads were stuck in creation order — pinning says "keep this on top" but you couldn't say which one goes first. Now you can drag pinned cards in the v2 sidebar into whatever order you want, and that order holds everywhere: every client, every platform, even with multiple servers connected at once.

## How it syncs

Each pinned thread stores an optional fractional-index `pinOrderKey` (lexorank-style string) on its own server, next to `pinnedAt`. Clients sort the merged pinned list by plain string comparison of keys, so:

- A drag computes one key that sorts between the drop position's neighbors and writes it to **one thread on one server** — neighbors on other servers are never touched.
- Order converges across clients through the existing event/projection stream, the same way `pinnedAt` already does. Concurrent drags of the same thread are last-write-wins; equal keys fall back to a deterministic id tiebreak.
- Version skew degrades cleanly via a new `threadPinReorder` capability: threads on older servers aren't draggable and keep today's creation order below the arranged run.

## Changes

- **contracts**: `thread.pin.reorder` command, `thread.pin-reordered` event, optional `orderKey` on `thread.pin`, `pinOrderKey` on thread shells, capability flag
- **server**: decider case (rejects unpinned threads, idempotent no-op re-emission), projection column + migration 038, key cleared on unpin/settle so re-pinning starts fresh
- **web**: dnd-kit sortable on the pinned block (same pattern as v1 project reordering, 6px activation so clicks still work), optimistic order until the confirming event lands, fresh pins keyed to the top of the arranged run
- **mobile**: read-side sort by the same keys (no drag UI yet), so phones show the order you arranged on web

Threads pinned before this ships stay keyless and get a key materialized on their first drag — no backfill. A pinned thread's key survives snooze, so it wakes back into its exact slot.

Tests: fractional key math (incl. 100-deep insertion churn), reorder planning, pinned sort, decider cases. Full typecheck/lint/test suites green across contracts, client-runtime, server, web, and mobile.

🟡 **Medium** `components/Sidebar.logic.ts:570`

`generateSpreadPinOrderKeys` clamps exhausted slots to `space - 1`, so when `count` exceeds the 675 two-digit capacity, the trailing keys all become `"zz"`. This produces duplicate order keys, causing `sortPinnedThreadsForSidebarV2` to fall back to the `localeCompare` ID tiebreak and silently lose the requested visual order. Consider rejecting `count` values above the available space or generating wider keys so every returned key is unique.

title: fix(dev): agents get --share right on the first try
body:
## Problem

Agents asked to "spin up a dev server with --share" routinely take many turns and sometimes fail outright. An audit of 66 agent session logs found the time from request to a working pairing URL ranged from ~90 seconds to 46 minutes, with three recurring traps:

1. **Inherited `T3_SERVICE_LAUNCHER_CONTEXT`.** Agents working inside a managed t3 install leak the service-launcher env vars into the dev server, which dies with `ServiceLauncherClientError: The service launcher started a different t3 version` — *after* the `shared on tailnet:` line already printed, so the shared URL looks live but is dead. 26 sessions hit this; the `env -u ...` workaround existed only as per-agent folklore.
2. **Contradictory pairing-URL guidance.** AGENTS.md said to send the pairing URL to the user; the `test-t3-app` skill said pairing URLs are secrets that must never appear in responses. Agents that followed the skill withheld the token and got told off.
3. **Stale pairing recovery.** The skill documented a five-flag `auth pairing create` incantation from before `t3 pair` existed, and nothing mentioned that CLI-minted tokens carry weaker scopes than the startup URL (which cost one session 20 extra minutes of lockout debugging).

## Fix

- `createDevRunnerEnv` now deletes `T3_SERVICE_LAUNCHER_CONTEXT` and `T3_BOOT_SERVICE_UNIT` next to the other ambient-env deletions — a dev-runner server is never launcher-managed. One focused test.
- AGENTS.md states the whole flow as three steps (run `vp run dev --share` in the background, wait for `pairingUrl:`, paste the full URL) and names `bin.ts pair` for token recovery with the scope caveat.
- `test-t3-app` skill: when the user asked for a shared environment, the full pairing URL is the deliverable; recovery section rewritten around `pair` (which self-discovers the server) instead of the manual flag list — net 11 lines shorter.

Written by Claude Fable 5 on Claude Code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Dev-runner env sanitization and documentation only; no production auth or data-path changes beyond preventing a false launcher-managed startup in local dev.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes agents spinning up **`vp run dev --share`** when they work inside a managed T3 install: **`createDevRunnerEnv`** now deletes **`T3_SERVICE_LAUNCHER_CONTEXT`** and **`T3_BOOT_SERVICE_UNIT`** so the child server is not treated as launcher-managed and no longer dies with a version-mismatch after tailnet output already looked healthy. A unit test locks in that behavior.
> 
> **`AGENTS.md`** and the **`test-t3-app`** skill are aligned on delivery: run dev with **`--share`**, wait for **`pairingUrl:`**, paste the **full URL including the token** when the user asked for a shared environment (not a bare origin). Pairing recovery is documented as **`node apps/server/src/bin.ts pair`** instead of the old multi-flag **`auth pairing create`** flow, with a note that CLI-minted tokens are standard-scope vs admin scopes on the startup URL for Settings → Connections.
>

findings.diff_hunk:
efect in this repo is a change that works on the path you teste
 - `vp i` installs. Worktrees get this from the t3.json setup script; if module resolution looks broken, it probably did not run.
 - `vp run dev` starts server and web. In a worktree, state defaults to that worktree's gitignored `.t3`, which deliberately outranks an ambient `T3CODE_HOME` so you cannot land on shared state by accident. An explicit `--home-dir` still wins.
 - Ports derive from the worktree path and are stable across restarts, but read the real ones from the `[dev-runner]` line since occupied ports shift.
-- `--share` publishes over the tailnet. Do not open the URL when you use this, just send it to the user with the pairing code included in url
-- The web app requires pairing. Hand over the pairing URL, not the bare origin. A URL without its token is useless to whoever you gave it to.
+- Sharing over the tailnet is three steps: run `vp run dev --share` in the background, wait for the `pairingUrl:` line in its output, paste that full URL (token included) in your reply. Do not use tsdev or raw `tailscale serve` for this, and do not open the URL yourself.
+- The web app requires pairing. Hand over the pairing URL, not the bare origin. A URL without its token is useless to whoever you gave it to. If the token got consumed, mint a fresh one with `node apps/server/src/bin.ts pair` — note it carries standard scopes, while the startup URL carries admin scopes (needed for Settings → Connections management).

title: feat(web): thread actions from the chat header title
body:
Every thread action (pin, settle, snooze, rename, delete, ...) lived only in the sidebar row's right-click menu — a long trip from the thread you're already reading, and unreachable when the sidebar is collapsed or the mobile drawer is closed.

The thread title in the chat header now opens that same menu: click it (a chevron fades in on hover), or right-click anywhere in the breadcrumb area. Rename happens inline in the header, with the same commit rules as the sidebar. Full action parity with the sidebar menu.

Details:
- The menu item list is extracted into a pure `buildThreadActionMenuItems` that both the sidebar and header render, so labels/ordering/capability gating cannot drift.
- Settled/snoozed classification uses the same inputs as ChatView's parked-thread banner, so the menu and banner always agree.
- Settle/snooze from the header do not navigate away — you acted on the thread you're reading, and the banner offers the way back.
- Drafts keep the plain read-only title; the git/scripts controls on the right keep their own right-click behavior.

Written by Claude Fable 5 via Claude Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds delete and metadata mutations from a new entry point and refactors shared menu logic; behavior is covered by unit tests and reuses existing thread action paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Thread actions that were only on sidebar right-click are now available from the **chat header** for server threads: click the title (chevron on hover) or right-click the breadcrumb area. **Drafts** keep a read-only title with no menu; header git/scripts controls still use their own context menus.
> 
> **`buildThreadActionMenuItems`** centralizes menu labels, order, and capability gating; **SidebarV2** and the header both use it so the two menus stay aligned. **`useThreadActionMenu`** wires the native context menu to the same mutations as the sidebar (pin, settle, snooze, delete, etc.); settle/snooze from the header do not navigate away. Settled/snoozed labels use the same PR/auto-settle inputs as ChatView’s parked-thread banner.
> 
> **Inline rename** in the header shares **`resolveRenameCommit`** (trim, reject empty, noop if unchanged) with sidebar behavior and persists via `updateMetadata`. **`ChatView`** passes `isServerThread` and `changeRequestState` into the header. **`readEnvironmentSupportsTitleRegeneration`** gates the regenerate-title item per environment.
>

findings.body:
🟡 **Medium** `hooks/useThreadActionMenu.ts:245`

When the orphaned-worktree cleanup fails after a successful thread deletion, `deleteThread` returns a failure result but has already shown a toast saying *"Thread deleted, but worktree removal failed"*. Passing that same failure into `reportFailure("Failed to delete thread", ...)` then displays a second toast claiming the deletion itself failed, even though the thread was already deleted. Consider checking the result before calling `reportFailure`, so a cleanup failure doesn't produce a misleading "Failed to delete thread" toast.

✅ Resolved in 29e815f09849ecb822077ed4558250ef107b1f97

### Header settle clock drifts from banner **Medium Severity** Header settle classification passes a precise `Date.toISOString()` into `effectiveSettled`, while ChatView's parked-thread banner uses the shared minute-quantized `useNowMinute` clock. Near the auto-settle inactivity boundary or queued-turn grace window, the header can show `Un-settle` while the banner still treats the thread as active, so acting on the menu applies an active override the banner never indicated.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx#L4097-L4104`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/1ec5870ba990c9546985f7bc062c8361ea4e96ae/apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx#L4097-L4104)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1ec5870ba990c9546985f7bc062c8361ea4e96ae. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟠 **High** `chat/ChatHeader.tsx:136`

The `renaming` state is keyed by `threadId` for display (`renamingTitle` is only non-null when `renaming.threadId === activeThreadId`), but the state object itself is never cleared when `activeThreadId` changes. Because `ChatHeader` is rendered without a `key`, starting a rename on thread A, navigating to thread B, then returning to thread A restores the stale draft from the previous rename session. Blurring the input then commits that stale text via `commitRename`, overwriting the thread title even if it was updated while away. Clear `renaming` when `activeThreadId` changes (e.g. via an effect) or key the component by thread so the editor remounts.

✅ Resolved in d2afc48cf486b83c1eac91e57885425ef7bb3903

🟠 **High** `chat/ChatHeader.tsx:148`

`commitRename` calls `updateThreadMetadata` with `reportFailure: false` and discards the returned `AtomCommandResult`, so when the rename mutation fails (e.g. after a connection loss) the input closes and no error is shown — the user is left believing the rename succeeded until the old title persists or reappears. The same pattern affects the snooze toast's Undo handler: it calls `unsnoozeThread(threadRef)` and discards the result, and because that mutation is configured with `reportFailure: false`, a server failure leaves the thread snoozed with no error feedback. In both cases the equivalent sidebar paths handle the `AtomCommandResult` and toast non-interruption failures. Consider awaiting the result and toasting on failure (excluding interrupted commands) so the user is notified when the rename or undo didn't take effect.
<details>
<summary>Also found in 1 other location(s)</summary>

`apps/web/src/hooks/useThreadActionMenu.ts:155`

> The snooze toast's Undo handler calls `unsnoozeThread(threadRef)` and discards its `AtomCommandResult`. Because `useThreadActions` configures `unsnoozeThreadMutation` with `reportFailure: false`, a server failure leaves the thread snoozed with no error feedback, even though the equivalent menu action and sidebar Undo report failures.

</details>

✅ Resolved in 210a1b1e26dc0e0c9a264b2113fded4c4b8579b8

🟡 **Medium** `chat/ChatHeader.tsx:248`

The title button binds both `onClick={openMenuFromTitle}` and `onDoubleClick={startRename}`. Browsers fire two `click` events before `dblclick`, so a double-click to rename first opens the thread action menu (twice), preventing or racing the rename input. The double-click rename gesture is unreliable because the single-click menu action always fires first. Consider deferring the single-click action with a short timer that is cancelled on double-click, or using a non-conflicting gesture for rename.

✅ Resolved in 210a1b1e26dc0e0c9a264b2113fded4c4b8579b8

title: feat(server): record runtime mode per turn and on mode changes
body:
## Problem

We could not answer basic questions about which permission mode people actually use.

Runtime mode (`approval-required` / `auto-accept-edits` / `auto` / `full-access`) was only reported on `provider.session.started`. Two problems with that as a denominator:

- A session restarts whenever runtime mode, cwd, model, or provider instance changes, so users who toggle often are overcounted.
- `provider.turn.sent` carries `interactionMode` (build vs plan) but not runtime mode, so the two could not be crossed.

Mode switches were not reported at all. The reactor computes the transition and logs it, but nothing reached analytics, so "started supervised, gave up, switched to full access" was unanswerable.

## Solution

Two additions, both in `ProviderService.ts` where `analytics` and the persisted binding are already in scope:

- `provider.turn.sent` now carries `runtimeMode`, giving a usage-weighted view that crosses with `interactionMode`. `resolveRoutableSession` already loaded the binding and dropped the mode; it now surfaces it.
- New `provider.runtime_mode.changed` event with `from`/`to`, emitted in `startSession` when the incoming mode differs from the previously persisted binding. Since a mode toggle restarts the session, this is the only place the transition is observable.

No schema, migration, or layer wiring changes. No new PII: both are existing anonymous events with one enum field added.

## Testing

Added one integration test covering both paths, with a recording analytics layer since `layerTest` discards events. Verified it is not vacuous: reverting each production change independently fails the corresponding assertion. `vitest` (496 passed), `typecheck`, and `vp lint` are clean.

## Follow-up not in this PR

Defaults still dominate and are invisible: `full-access` and `default` are the defaults, so nothing distinguishes a deliberate pick from never opening the menu. Separating those needs a client-side signal, which is a larger change. There is also no PostHog in web/mobile/desktop at all, so menu opens and abandoned selections remain dark.

---

Made with Claude Opus 5 (1M context) in T3 Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Telemetry-only additions on existing anonymous events; no auth, persistence schema, or routing behavior changes beyond surfacing binding runtimeMode for analytics.
> 
> **Overview**
> Improves **provider runtime mode** telemetry so analytics can answer how people actually use permission modes and when they switch.
> 
> **`provider.turn.sent`** now includes **`runtimeMode`** (from the persisted binding via `resolveRoutableSession`), giving a turn-weighted view that can be crossed with **`interactionMode`** instead of relying only on session-start counts (which over-weight frequent togglers because mode changes restart sessions).
> 
> **`provider.runtime_mode.changed`** is emitted from **`startSession`** when the new mode differs from the previously persisted binding, with **`from`** / **`to`** and provider— the natural hook because a mode toggle restarts the session.
> 
> Integration coverage adds a **recording analytics** layer, optional analytics on the fixture builder, and a test that asserts per-turn `runtimeMode` and a single transition from `approval-required` to `full-access`.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 05f9921c830c4df2c54569e77c59f5fa1bedbee0. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(web): live background-work banner no longer hides behind the update notice
body: With a server update pending and subagents running, the composer showed the passive "Server update available" notice in front while the live "3 agents working in the background" banner hid behind it until hover. Worse, the collapsed stack cap peeking out behind the front banner is hardcoded warning-yellow, so the neutral subagent banner read as a mystery yellow warning that "transformed" on hover. Two fixes: - Banner ordering is now by urgency: error/warning system banners stay in front, the background-liveness banner comes next (its Stop button is the only stop affordance once a turn settles), and calm notices like the update offer stack behind it. - The collapsed stack cap border now derives from the variant of the banner actually hidden behind the front one, instead of always faking a warning. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) using Claude Fable 5 --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > UI-only banner ordering and styling in the chat composer; no auth, data, or API changes. > > **Overview** > Fixes composer banner stacking so **live** states (background agents, in-flight server update, reconnect) stay in front of passive notices like “Server update available,” and so the collapsed stack peek no longer always looks like a warning. > > **`ChatView`** splits system banners into urgent (error/warning variants or `urgent: true`) vs calm, then builds the stack as: urgent system → background liveness → calm system → woke / branch-mismatch / parked. Reconnect/version-skew and **running** server-update items are flagged `urgent` so they front the stack despite `default` styling. > > **`ComposerBannerStack`** adds optional `urgent` on items (assembler-only) and maps the collapsed cap border to the **first hidden** banner’s variant instead of a fixed warning border. Tests cover neutral vs warning caps behind the front banner. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit aa08190e6146fa020dc7d1b839e63ca6a271720d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). > [!NOTE] > ### Fix live background-work banner being hidden behind the update notice in `ChatViewContent` > - Reorders composer banners in [ChatView.tsx](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5595/files#diff-4b49e092ccd43be0f0de24abe85ba522e09f04288a5d84253b0263e1a389400e) by partitioning system banners into 'urgent' (error/warning variants or items flagged `urgent: true`) and 'calm' sets, placing urgent items before background liveness and calm items after. > - The reconnecting-through-version-skew and in-progress server update banners are now flagged `urgent: true` so they appear first; 'update available' (calm) no longer obscures the liveness banner. > - The collapsed stack cap border in [ComposerBannerStack.tsx](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5595/files#diff-70e682f5637e29152782d8d01713cd41d0ced0860f99ad7cefbdc07da06e364b) now reflects the severity of the first hidden banner instead of always using a warning color. > > > > Macroscope summarized aa08190. > >

title: feat(swift-ios): bring Ghostty to the terminal
body:
The SwiftUI terminal was a plain-text command box, so ANSI output, TUIs, scrollback, keyboard workflows, and multiple shell sessions fell short of the React Native app.

This replaces it with a native Ghostty-backed full-canvas terminal, adds mobile and hardware keyboard controls, accurate resizing and scrollback, stable clear/reconnect behavior, and independent per-thread terminal sessions.

Stacks on #5178.

## Before / after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://files.tslop.org/2026/08/swiftui-terminal-before-2a2e1e4b.jpg) | ![After](https://files.tslop.org/2026/08/swiftui-terminal-after-fb2188e8.jpg) |

## Demo

![Terminal demo](https://files.tslop.org/2026/08/swiftui-terminal-preview-37aa4839.gif)

[Full-quality screen recording](https://files.tslop.org/2026/08/swiftui-terminal-demo-06706a29.mp4)

## Verification

- `T3CodeTests/FeatureToolStateTests`
- `T3CodeTests/NativeMultiEnvironmentTests`
- `T3CodeTests/CoreContractTests`
- 37 tests passed, 0 failed
- iPhone 17 Pro Simulator: ANSI colors, clear/reconnect, Ctrl-C, resize, and session create/switch/stop fallback

This PR was built by GPT-5.6-sol using the Codex harness in T3 Code.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large new native dependency and reworked terminal RPC/stream lifecycle; behavior is user-facing but scoped to the terminal feature with existing T3 RPC contracts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the **plain-text terminal** with a **GhosttyKit**-rendered surface so VT/ANSI output, TUIs, and scrollback work like the RN app. The UI is a full-screen canvas with pinch-to-zoom text size, a session menu (switch, open, stop), and software/hardware keyboard controls (accessory bar, Ctrl/Cmd modifiers, copy/paste/clear).
> 
> **Client and protocol:** Terminal APIs are now keyed by **`terminalID`** per thread instead of one implicit shell. `NativeFeatureClient` drops the shared `terminalEvents` fan-out and uses **`attachTerminal`** per session plus a new **`terminalSessions`** stream from **`terminalMetadataEvents`**. Snapshots keep raw escape sequences (stripping moved to `TerminalText` for copy-only). **`clearTerminal`** is added; buffer cap rises to 512KB.
> 
> **Build:** Xcode links **`GhosttyKit.xcframework`** with Metal/IOSurface/QuartzCore.

title: Automate production mobile EAS releases
body: ## What Changed - Trigger the mobile EAS production workflow automatically for relevant changes merged into `main`. - Serialize production runs to preserve OTA release order. - Automatically create and submit iOS and Android store builds when the app version changes. - Publish OTA updates only when a finished production build matches the current native fingerprint. - Restore package versions from `0.0.32` to `0.0.31`. ## Why This makes mobile production releases follow merges automatically while avoiding duplicate builds and incompatible OTA updates. Store builds are created when the app version changes, and JavaScript updates are published only when an installed native binary can apply them. Manual workflow dispatch remains available for retries and forced releases. ## Checklist - [x] This PR is small and focused - [x] I explained what changed and why - [ ] I included before/after screenshots for any UI changes - [ ] I included a video for animation/interaction changes --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes production release automation (store submits and OTA channel) on every qualifying merge; misconfigured version or fingerprint logic could skip OTAs or trigger duplicate builds, though serialization and gating reduce blast radius. > > **Overview** > **Production mobile releases now run automatically** when relevant paths merge to `main`, while `workflow_dispatch` stays for manual build/OTA retries. > > `mobile-eas-production.yml` adds path-filtered `push` triggers and a **serialized** concurrency group so OTAs stay ordered (bursts collapse to the latest commit). On push it **compares** `app.config.ts` version to the latest EAS production build per platform and starts **auto-submit** store builds when they differ (in-progress builds count, avoiding duplicates). It then **fingerprint-gates** production OTAs: updates publish only if a **finished** build matches the current native fingerprint; otherwise the job summary warns and skips. > > A new **`mobile-fingerprint-check.yml`** runs on PRs, fingerprints merge-result vs base (with `pnpm install` on base for lockfile accuracy), writes an iOS/Android diff to the job summary, and syncs a **📱 Native Change** label on in-repo PRs so native drift is visible before merge. The check is advisory and always passes. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 88c9273e4f7f5095a24cffe2a03763d962069eaa. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). > [!NOTE] > ### Automate production mobile EAS releases and fingerprint checks on push to main > - On pushes to `main` touching mobile paths, [mobile-eas-production.yml](.github/workflows/mobile-eas-production.yml) checks the current app version against the latest production build per platform and triggers a new store build + auto-submit if versions differ. > - OTA updates are published to the production channel only when a finished production build with a matching native fingerprint exists; otherwise a warning is written to the job summary. > - Adds [mobile-fingerprint-check.yml](.github/workflows/mobile-fingerprint-check.yml), which computes and compares native fingerprints for iOS and Android on PRs, writes a diff summary, and adds/removes a `📱 Native Change` label on same-repo PRs. > - Manual `workflow_dispatch` triggers retain the existing build/submit and OTA publish steps unchanged. > > > > Macroscope summarized 88c

title: Allow Android tablets to rotate
body: ## What Changed Added an Expo config plugin that enables Android tablets with a smallest width of at least 600dp to support all orientations while keeping phones locked to portrait. ## Why The app's top-level portrait orientation setting currently locks Android tablets to portrait. This mirrors iPad behavior by allowing tablet rotation while preserving the existing portrait-only behavior on phones. ## Checklist - [x] This PR is small and focused - [x] I explained what changed and why - [x] I included before/after screenshots for any UI changes - [x] I included a video for animation/interaction changes --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Scoped Android native MainActivity orientation logic with idempotent plugin injection; no auth, data, or API changes. > > **Overview** > Adds **`withAndroidTabletOrientation`**, a new Expo config plugin registered in `app.config.ts`, so Android behavior matches iOS: phones stay portrait-only while tablets can rotate. > > At build time the plugin patches **`MainActivity`** to call **`applyTabletOrientation()`** after `onCreate` and again in **`onConfigurationChanged`**. When **`smallestScreenWidthDp >= 600`**, it sets **`requestedOrientation`** to **`SCREEN_ORIENTATION_FULL_USER`** (overriding the manifest portrait lock); otherwise it forces portrait. Fold/unfold on foldables re-applies the same rule without requiring an activity restart. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1f42088bc2975297392f519a2da5b31da12ee40e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). > [!NOTE] > ### Allow Android tablets to rotate freely while keeping phones in portrait > - Adds a new Expo config plugin [`withAndroidTabletOrientation.cjs`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5613/files#diff-5d3b4bf5256c107ada39bb5f39d2cbfbf80a43525d37038481fc167a17179cc0) that patches `MainActivity.kt` at build time to inject orientation logic. > - At runtime, devices with `smallestScreenWidthDp >= 600` (tablets) use `SCREEN_ORIENTATION_FULL_USER`, respecting the system auto-rotate setting; phones stay locked to portrait. > - An `onConfigurationChanged` override re-evaluates orientation on each configuration change, covering foldable devices. > - The plugin is registered in [`app.config.ts`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5613/files#diff-290065ad5da22af2aa0a274a6657359bd050ba8ad4e36b97765dac7c98f90bab) and skips patching if already applied. > > > > Macroscope summarized 1f42088. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Enhancements** * Improved tablet orientation support in the mobile app, allowing users to select available screen orientations on larger Android tablets. * Preserved portrait orientation behavior on Android phones.
author: juliusmarminge

findings.body:
### Orientation ignores foldable size changes **Medium Severity** The tablet orientation override runs only once in `onCreate` and never rechecks `smallestScreenWidthDp`. Expo SDK 56 keeps the activity alive across fold/unfold via `smallestScreenSize` in `configChanges`, so a folded launch stays portrait after unfolding, and an unfolded launch that set `SCREEN_ORIENTATION_FULL_USER` can keep the cover display unlocked after folding.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/mobile/plugins/withAndroidTabletOrientation.cjs#L44-L50`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/1e430ec61ae9d60937384164ee14ecb3a540c3ee/apps/mobile/plugins/withAndroidTabletOrientation.cjs#L44-L50)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1e430ec61ae9d60937384164ee14ecb3a540c3ee. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+const { withMainActivity } = require("expo/config-plugins");
+
+// The top-level `orientation: "portrait"` writes android:screenOrientation="portrait"
+// into the manifest, which locks every Android device — including tablets — to
+// portrait. iOS doesn't have this problem: iPads must support all orientations
+// because the app is multitasking-capable, so only iPhones end up portrait-only.
+// Mirror that split on Android: keep the manifest lock for phones and lift it at
+// runtime on tablets (smallest width >= 600dp, the standard tablet breakpoint),
+// since requestedOrientation set in onCreate overrides the manifest value.
+// FULL_USER allows all four orientations while still respecting the user's
+// auto-rotate lock, matching iPad behavior.
+
+const ORIENTATION_OVERRIDE = `
+    if (resources.configuration.smallestScreenWidthDp >= 600) {
+      requestedOrientation = ActivityInfo.SCREEN_ORIENTATION_FULL_USER
+    }`;

title: fix(web): use themed confirmation dialogs
body:
## Summary

Rebased onto the newest `upstream/main` (`1a003e383ac6`) and addressed the review feedback. The shared themed confirmation coordinator now carries an explicit confirmation intent: destructive actions render the existing T3 destructive/red button variant, while normal confirmations keep the standard primary button.

Deletion, worktree removal, project removal, checkpoint revert, settings reset, and SIGKILL confirmations are destructive. Archive, update/install, and informational confirmations remain normal. Native macOS context menus remain unchanged.

## Verification

- `vp run --filter @t3tools/web typecheck`
- `vp run --filter @t3tools/desktop typecheck`
- targeted Oxlint on all changed confirmation files
- `vp fmt --check`
- `git diff --check`
- focused Vitest invocations retried after `vp i`; both still fail before test execution because of the repository's runner/configuration bootstrap errors (zero test bodies run)
- CI will re-run the full test job for the new head
- before/after deletion confirmation evidence is inline below
![Before: native Electron confirmation (pre-PR)](https://pub-b182a4071edc4521829926b34990540b.r2.dev/files/bc7c9799-40e7-4b62-8735-ea2e92ca91d7/pre-pr-native-electron-confirmation.png)
![After: destructive delete-thread dialog](https://pub-b182a4071edc4521829926b34990540b.r2.dev/files/ca56928d-e966-4593-bb7a-e3dcb9ba94e9/destructive-delete-confirmation.png)



## Scope

Mobile native alerts, CLI prompts, Electron message/error boxes, and native macOS context-menu behavior remain unchanged. The renderer confirmation path fails closed when no themed host is mounted.

Model/harness: gpt-5.6-luna via Codex.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how destructive actions (updates, SIGKILL, deletes via LocalApi) are confirmed; fail-closed behavior when no host is mounted could block actions in edge cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces native browser and Electron confirmation flows with a **shared in-app `AlertDialog`** so destructive prompts match the rest of the UI on web and desktop.
> 
> A new **`confirmDialog` coordinator** queues requests, handles close transitions, and exposes **`ConfirmDialogHost`** from the root route. **`LocalApi.dialogs.confirm`** now goes through `requestConfirmDialog` when a host is mounted; if none is registered it **returns `false`** instead of calling `window.confirm` or the desktop bridge.
> 
> The **Electron `confirm` IPC path** is removed (`ElectronDialog.confirm`, `CONFIRM_CHANNEL`, preload `confirm`, and `DesktopBridge.confirm` in contracts). Call sites that used **`window.confirm`** (update install, SIGKILL in diagnostics/telemetry) now **`await ensureLocalApi().dialogs.confirm`**, with **pending-state guards** to avoid double submissions.
>

Because this callback is wired directly to `onSignal` and no UI caller awaits the returned promise, the rethrown error becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than a handled failure. title: feat(mobile): one sheet for model and thread settings

title: feat(web): make sidebar artwork theme-aware
body: Custom palette themes currently inherit fixed Dev/Nightly sidebar artwork, which can clash badly with their colors. The theme editor also previews palette colors live, so artwork behavior should be previewable there too. This change makes palette themes use the environment version pill by default while preserving an explicit global `none` choice. Custom themes can opt back into sidebar artwork from the create/edit theme panel, and that preference is retained through local persistence and theme import/export files. ## Display flow First, respect the user's global environment-identification setting: - **None:** show neither artwork nor a version pill. A theme cannot override this. - **Version pill:** show the version pill. A theme cannot replace it with artwork. - **Artwork:** continue to the active-theme check below. When the global setting is **Artwork**: - **Standard T3 Code theme:** show the sidebar artwork as before. - **Palette/custom theme with “Sidebar artwork” off:** show the version pill instead, avoiding a potentially bad color contrast. - **Palette/custom theme with “Sidebar artwork” on:** show the sidebar artwork. New custom themes, duplicates, existing themes without the new preference, and imported themes without the preference all default to artwork off. The artwork toggle participates in the live theme preview, so the sidebar updates immediately while editing and returns to the saved behavior when the editor closes. ## Validation - `vp test run apps/web/src/themePalette.test.ts apps/web/src/hooks/useSettings.test.ts` - targeted `vp lint` for all changed files - targeted `vp format --check` for all changed files - `vp run typecheck` in `apps/web` Generated with GPT-5.6 Sol in the T3 Code Codex harness. > [!NOTE] > ### Make sidebar artwork display theme-aware in the web app > - Adds a `sidebarArtwork` flag to `ThemeDefinition` and `ThemeFile` types, persisted through custom theme storage, import/export, and live preview. > - The theme editor gains a toggle to opt a theme into showing sidebar artwork; the choice is previewed live and saved with the theme. > - `resolveEnvironmentIdentificationMode` now coerces `artwork` to `pill` when a palette theme is active but does not opt into sidebar artwork. > - `useEnvironmentIdentificationMode` subscribes to the active/previewed theme to dynamically apply this coercion at runtime. > - Behavioral Change: users with environment identification set to `artwork` will see `pill` instead when their active theme does not include `sidebarArtwork: true`. > > > > Macroscope summarized eecc097. > > --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > UI and theme-preference behavior only; no auth or data-path changes, with tests covering resolution and persistence. > > **Overview** > Palette/custom themes no longer always show fixed Dev/Nightly sidebar artwork when the global environment ID is set to **artwork**. Themes get an opt-in **`sidebarArtwork`** flag (default off for new, duplicate, legacy, and imported themes), stored on theme definitions and in import/export files. > > The theme editor adds a **Sidebar artwork** switch, wires it through all save/merge paths, and syncs it when merging by name. `captureFavicon` discards a successful favicon response when a duplicate `page-favicon-updated` event arrives while the first request is still in flight. 🟠 **High** `settings/ThemeSettings.tsx:474`

Each variant option uses only `getThemeCardDefinition(variant).previews[0]`, which for a dual-mode theme is always the `"light"` preview. Inside `ThemeLibraryCard`, `radialModeGroups` filters options by `preview?.mode === mode`, so a dual-mode variant never appears in the dark radial group — its dark palette cannot be selected through the variant picker.

To fix this, expand the options so each variant produces one entry per preview (one per supported mode), and carry the original theme index so `onSelectAndUse` can map the option index back to the correct `themes` entry. For example, build an `expandedOptions` array via `themes.flatMap((variant, themeIndex) => getThemeCardDefinition(variant).previews.map(preview => ({ themeIndex, label, activeModes, preview })))`, pass that as `options`, and in `onSelectAndUse` look up `expandedOptions[optionIndex].themeIndex` instead of using the option index directly as the theme index.

🟠 **High** `src/themePalette.ts:1734`

`storedThemeHasCollectionId` delegates to `parseThemeCollection`, which validates the full `ThemeCollection` shape (both `id` and `label`). If an installed entry has a valid `collection.id` but a missing or malformed `label`, `parseThemeCollection` returns `null`, so `storedThemeHasCollectionId` returns `false`. This causes two cascading failures here: at line 1734 the entry is treated as unrelated and its theme ID is added to `occupiedIds`, and at line 1751 the stale entry is kept instead of being replaced. The replacement themes then collide with `occupiedIds` and the function throws "already installed" instead of performing the update.

The fix is in `storedThemeHasCollectionId` — it should check the raw `collection.id` string directly rather than requiring the entire collection object to pass full validation.

findings.body:
🟠 **High** `src/openVsxThemes.ts:264`

When the Open VSX search endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a non-expected shape (e.g. `{}` or `{"error": ...}`), `searchOpenVsxThemes` silently returns an empty array, so the UI tells the user "No supported open-source themes found" even though the API returned a malformed or error response. The code falls back to `[]` on line 264 when `value.extensions` is absent, instead of throwing like the detail-fetch path does for unreadable responses. Consider validating that the parsed body is an object with an `extensions` array and throwing an error otherwise, so malformed search responses surface to the user instead of being indistinguishable from a legitimate empty result.

✅ Resolved in 50d3f4aaa2b87a4af0274946f77764e98bcc0045

### Paired variants keep duplicate labels **Low Severity** After `pairVsCodeThemes`, a second `resolveThemeLabelCollisions` runs without `sourceName` and only dedupes by theme id. Path-based `ovx-theme-*` ids are already unique, so leftover singles that share the paired label (for example paired `Demo` plus solo `Demo`) stay identically named in the collection carousel.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 387846dd465334d0bb97c5fb30d1b7b96a661277. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Abort wrapped as package open error **Low Severity** `signal.throwIfAborted()` runs inside the ZIP `try/catch` that only rethrows errors whose message starts with `That extension package`. An abort after `JSZip.loadAsync` therefore becomes `That Open VSX extension package could not be opened` instead of `AbortError`, breaking the cancellation contract the new abort test expects.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9ee257965359ed04bd88df7c7d1d4202ebc0b772. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

### Manifest failures abort whole search **Medium Severity** Search preflight treats a failed public `manifest` fetch or parse as a rejected candidate instead of skipping it. With `Promise.allSettled`, if every licensed result hits that path, search throws `Open VSX theme details are unavailable right now` even when detail requests succeeded. The new per-result manifest fan-out makes rate limits and file-API blips fail the whole search rather than return partial or empty results.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/openVsxThemes.ts#L217-L220`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/9ee257965359ed04bd88df7c7d1d4202ebc0b772/apps/web/src/openVsxThemes.ts#L217-L220)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9ee257965359ed04bd88df7c7d1d4202ebc0b772. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `src/openVsxThemes.ts:218`

`searchOpenVsxThemes` can return `[]` instead of throwing when every real detail/manifest fetch fails. The check at line 219 treats fulfilled `null` results (e.g. extensions filtered out for unsupported licenses) as successful completions, so when all eligible candidates fail and at least one was filtered, the function returns an empty array rather than reporting Open VSX as unavailable. This causes the UI to show "No supported open-source themes found" even though the actual problem is that the detail requests failed. The `completedDetails.length` check should only count results that returned a non-null extension, so all-null outcomes surface as an availability error.

No longer relevant as of bda97be47f673b41c5017e3ac06fabae29990d8e

findings.body:
### Failed searches look empty **Medium Severity** `searchOpenVsxThemes` hydrates up to 16 extension details in parallel and treats every failed detail fetch as a skipped result. When Open VSX rate-limits or those requests error, the function still returns an empty list, so the dialog shows “No supported open-source themes found” instead of a search failure.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/components/settings/ThemeSearchDialog.tsx#L209-L215`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/cc41220638f522470d517a170676494c9027e2eb/apps/web/src/components/settings/ThemeSearchDialog.tsx#L209-L215)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit cc41220638f522470d517a170676494c9027e2eb. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟠 **High** `src/openVsxThemes.ts:201`

`inspectZipDirectory` can reject a valid VSIX package that has a ZIP archive comment containing the byte sequence `PK\x05\x06`. The function scans backward for the End of Central Directory signature but accepts the first match it finds without checking that the EOCD's comment-length field is consistent with the actual end of the file. When the archive comment happens to contain those four bytes at an earlier offset, the scanner mistakes the comment bytes for the real EOCD and throws "invalid ZIP directory" even though the package is valid. Consider validating each candidate's comment length against the file end before selecting it.

✅ Resolved in cc41220638f522470d517a170676494c9027e2eb

🟠 **High** `src/openVsxThemes.ts:142`

`searchOpenVsxThemes` reads each of up to 16 detail responses via `detailResponse.json()` with no body-size cap. Unlike the search response (which uses `readCappedResponse` with `MAX_SEARCH_BYTES`), an oversized Open VSX detail payload is fully buffered into memory, and with up to 16 concurrent requests this can exhaust memory and crash the tab. Consider routing each detail body through `readCappedResponse` with a reasonable cap before parsing.

✅ Resolved in cc41220638f522470d517a170676494c9027e2eb

title: feat(web): fold plan mode and token-by-token output into Legacy features
body:
Plan mode and token-by-token streaming are features we want to keep available but stop advertising. Plan mode sat in Beta looking like a new feature, and token-by-token output actively hurts the experience: it is much slower than buffered output.

Now there is a collapsed **Legacy features** section at the bottom of Settings → General. You have to unfold it to see either toggle, and a settings-search jump auto-unfolds it.

title: feat: sidebar v2 is now the default sidebar
body:
The v2 sidebar has been living behind a beta toggle (plus stage-based defaults: on for nightly/dev, off for stable) long enough. It is now the sidebar, everywhere, following the same pattern as #5664.

- **Web**: `SidebarV2` is now `Sidebar`; the old sidebar lives on as `LegacySidebar` behind a new "Sidebar (legacy)" toggle in Settings → General → Legacy features.
- **Config**: `sidebarV2Enabled` + `sidebarV2ConfiguredByUser` are gone, replaced by a fresh `legacySidebarEnabled` key (default off). Like the token-streaming change, decoding drops the old keys, so prior beta opt-outs reset to the new default.
- **No more stage-based resolution**: the nightly/dev-vs-stable default logic in `branding.logic.ts` is deleted along with the configured-by-user companion bit.
- **Settings page hack removed**: the layout used to keep the v1 sidebar mounted on `/settings` because the settings nav lived inside it. `AppSidebarLayout` now renders `SettingsSidebarNav` directly on settings routes, so neither sidebar component knows about settings.
- **Settings → Beta is gone**: it only held the sidebar toggle and auto-settle. Auto-settle now lives in General (it applies to the default sidebar); the route, nav entry, and search entries are removed.
- **Mobile**: the flat thread list was already the default; the per-device `threadListV2Enabled` opt-out is replaced by a fresh `legacyThreadListEnabled` opt-in, surfaced as a "Legacy Thread List" toggle in a Legacy settings section.
