title: fix(mobile): preserve keyboard suggestions while typing
body:
## What Changed

Preserve keyboard suggestions and predictive text while typing by skipping no-op selection updates and tracking caret changes through the native editor revision flow. Prevent stale controlled values from reapplying during native edits, and ensure selection events deliver any newer text to the parent.

Also simplify changed-files layout breakpoints in the web client.

## Why

Reapplying an unchanged selection resets keyboard suggestion state on Android and iOS. Stale controlled renders could also move the caret backward or overwrite text mid-typing. The revision and event-handling changes keep native edits authoritative until the parent acknowledges them.

## UI Changes

Changed-files labels and actions now use the standard `sm` breakpoint instead of container queries.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why
- [ ] I included before/after screenshots for any UI changes
- [ ] I included a video for animation/interaction changes

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches native text-input sync and revision guards on a hot typing path; regressions could cause caret jumps, lost keystrokes, or draft restore issues, though changes are localized and well covered by unit tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes the mobile composer resetting **keyboard suggestions/autocorrect** and **yanking the caret or overwriting text** during fast typing by tightening how native selection and revision events sync with React.
> 
> **Native (iOS/Android):** Skips programmatic selection updates when the range is already correct (re-applying selection resets the keyboard context). **Caret-only moves** now bump `nativeEventCount` like text edits. iOS defers selection events during text mutations so revision counters stay paired with the right document; Android/iOS selection handlers can forward **newer text** when selection events race ahead of change events.
> 
> **React + `composerEditorRevision`:** Drops the render-sequence gate—every render resolves controlled revision from **snapshot history** (starting empty on mount so restored drafts apply). Adds **`assumeComposerControlledState`** and keeps the **latest acknowledged snapshot** when pruning so settled re-renders stay echoes instead of re-controlling the caret. Echo detection no longer treats a parent caret move as an echo of an assumed document without a stored selection.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 2e0b505e90917d6c573faec1f81cbc3804b5fcd7. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<!-- Macroscope's pull request summary starts here -->
<!-- Macroscope will only edit the content between these invisible markers, and the markers themselves will not be visible in the GitHub rendered markdown. -->
<!-- If you delete either of the start / end markers from your PR's description, Macroscope will append its summary at the bottom of the description. -->
> [!NOTE]
> ### Preserve keyboard autocorrect and predictive text suggestions while typing in the mobile composer
> - Skips no-op `selectedRange`/`setSelection` assignments in the native iOS ([T3ComposerEditorView.swift](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/6323/files#diff-bf020ce11861c51d7a3be2ccf67632f77afe80ff4ecf76a17884c5b040c21749)) and Android ([T3ComposerEditorView.kt](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/6323/files#diff-dbf8b69facaf4bfdba7369705927677e0a538325ec8355999f2a34f3b9d32e30)) views so the keyboard's suggestion context is not reset during programmatic no-op selection updates.
> - Adds `assumeComposerControlledState` in [composerEditorRevision.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/6323/files#diff-13070a989fda29d965af9c14d8b313a24fe0346688e6f55dcde290b5a37b6451) to stamp a parent-applied controlled state into snapshot history, preventing subsequent parent updates from being misclassified as ech
author: juliusmarminge

findings.body:
### Selection events drop newer text **Medium Severity** `onComposerSelectionChange` still acknowledges the native revision and can re-render, but it no longer forwards a newer `value` through `onChangeText`. On Android, `onSelectionChanged` runs during a text mutation before `afterTextChanged`, so JS can accept the post-edit text at the new `eventCount` while the parent still holds the previous draft. That render can stamp the stale value at the acknowledged revision, and `assumeComposerControlledState` can then record it as applied, overwriting in-progress typing or leaving `draftMessage` behind the editor.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/mobile/src/native/T3ComposerEditor.ios.tsx#L270-L280`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/8b7bbd1f987ea31b2fb0d32ea54c0f2f9ded4006/apps/mobile/src/native/T3ComposerEditor.ios.tsx#L270-L280)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8b7bbd1f987ea31b2fb0d32ea54c0f2f9ded4006. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `native/composerEditorRevision.ts:57`

`isComposerNativeEcho` classifies every controlled selection as an echo when the snapshot has `selection: null`, so a parent-only caret or selection update is dropped and never applied. The wildcard is needed for `resolveComposerControlledEventCount`, but echo detection must require an actual selection match (or otherwise exclude assumed snapshots) before serializing `selection: null`.

No longer relevant as of 2e0b505e90917d6c573faec1f81cbc3804b5fcd7

### Selection path can wipe drafts **High Severity** `lastDeliveredValueRef` is seeded with `props.value` even though that text never came from native, and selection events can now call `onChangeText` whenever native text differs. An early selection event from the still-empty editor (more likely now that caret moves bump `nativeEventCount` and can block the first controlled apply) publishes `""` and clears a restored draft in the parent.
Additional Locations (2) - [`apps/mobile/src/native/T3ComposerEditor.native.tsx#L110-L280`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/84465743c880508c99ab05663b62cc61016b35b1/apps/mobile/src/native/T3ComposerEditor.native.tsx#L110-L280) - [`apps/mobile/modules/t3-composer-editor/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/t3composereditor/T3ComposerEditorView.kt#L285-L290`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/84465743c880508c99ab05663b62cc61016b35b1/apps/mobile/modules/t3-composer-editor/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/t3composereditor/T3ComposerEditorView.kt#L285-L290)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 84465743c880508c99ab05663b62cc61016b35b1. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟠 **High** `native/T3ComposerEditor.ios.tsx:168`

After native state `A` is acknowledged and pruned down to its retained snapshot, a later parent-driven update from `B` back to the same `A` value/selection (with no intervening native event) matches the retained snapshot and is incorrectly classified as a native echo via `isComposerNativeEcho`. The native editor then drops the update because its current text is still `B`, so the editor stays on `B` and the parent's value `A` is silently ignored. This happens because pruning now permanently keeps the latest acknowledged snapshot, so `isComposerNativeEcho` can match a stale historical state on any render. Consider excluding snapshots that are older than the latest native event count from echo classification, or only treating a render as an echo when it matches the *current* native state rather than any retained historical snapshot.
<details>
<summary>Also found in 1 other location(s)</summary>

`apps/mobile/src/native/T3ComposerEditor.native.tsx:175`

> `isNativeEcho` is now allowed on every render, while pruning permanently retains the latest acknowledged snapshot. After native state `A` is acknowledged, if the parent controls the editor to `B` and later back to the same `A` value/selection without a new native event, this render matches the retained snapshot and is incorrectly marked as an echo. The Android native view rejects an echo whose current text differs, so the parent-driven update back to `A` is silently ignored and the editor remains on `B`.

</details>

✅ Resolved in 8b7bbd1f987ea31b2fb0d32ea54c0f2f9ded4006

title: fix(mobile): prevent OTA update restart crashes
body: ## Problem Applying an OTA update called `Updates.reloadAsync()` mid-session, seconds after the Home screen mounted — tearing down the JS runtime while native surfaces (terminal, composer editor, review diff), live WebSocket connections, and first-render hydration were still active. That teardown window is where the post-OTA crashes came from. ## Fix - After an update downloads, a native alert offers **Install Now** or **Later**. "Later" defers the restart to the next backgrounding, where nothing is rendering and the restart is invisible. - A deferred restart re-verifies it is still safe right before firing: the app must actually be backgrounded (flush latency or an iOS suspend can push the continuation into the next foreground session) and not merely paused behind an app-initiated handoff — on Android the image picker covers the activity and reports as backgrounded. Otherwise it re-arms for the next backgrounding. - Rollback directives (`eas update:rollback`) skip the prompt and apply immediately — they exist to pull a broken bundle. - Before any restart, debounced composer-draft writes and in-flight outbox writes are flushed, and both stores now write atomically (temp file + rename) so an interrupted write can never leave truncated JSON. - New foreground re-check after 15+ minutes backgrounded, so long-resident apps pick up updates published while in memory. A failed deferred restart returns the prompt to later checks instead of suppressing them for the session. - The hidden Settings 5-tap check keeps its immediate restart (`applyMode: "immediate"`). Covered by 22 unit tests over the check/prompt/defer/rollback/flush state machine plus the handoff guard; drafts and outbox suites pass unchanged. Docs: new "The Mobile App" section in `docs/user/updating.md`. Built by Claude Fable 5 via Claude Code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > [!NOTE] > ### Fix OTA update crashes by coordinating restarts with state flush and app lifecycle > - Adds a deferred install flow: downloaded updates are installed automatically when the app backgrounds, or the user is prompted after an extended foreground session. > - Introduces `flushComposerDrafts` and `flushThreadOutbox` so in-flight writes are drained before restarting; automatic installs abort and re-arm on flush failure to avoid data loss. > - Adds `isSafeToRestartInBackground` gating (checks `AppState` and foreground handoffs) so restarts never fire during image picker or other OS-covered surfaces. > - Adds a `ready` state to `AppUpdateCheckState` and surfaces an "Update ready" label in [SettingsRouteScreen](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/6324/files#diff-2f7a2e66b652454e7fd1b30226a5146d595dfe05945b34d90ffd5f3a5037cb1e) when a background-downloaded update is waiting. > - Adds `startAppUpdateForegroundRecheck` in [HomeRouteScreen](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/6324/files#diff-c2d4821e3a79b2c54784238ebdee5378f310422e4a79169b0bc6fc95081dacf5) to trigger periodic update checks after meaningful background gaps, suppressed when an install is already pending. > - Risk: restarts now flush composer drafts and the thread outbox; a flush error silently re-arms the deferred install rather than proceeding, which may delay updates indefinitely if persistence is broken. > > > > Macroscope summarized 63fe6d1. > > --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes when and ho
author: juliusmarminge

findings.body:
### Deferred re-arm busy-loops **High Severity** `defaultOnNextBackground` now calls `apply()` immediately when `AppState` is already `background`. After an unsafe or failed deferred attempt, `applyDeferredAppUpdateInstall` re-arms via that same helper while the app is still backgrounded — for example during an Android image-picker handoff — so the flush/safety check retries in a tight async loop until the app becomes active again.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L398-L407`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497/apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L398-L407)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟠 **High** `updates/app-updates.ts:406`

A failed flush or unsafe restart check causes an unbounded asynchronous retry loop while the app remains backgrounded, repeatedly performing I/O instead of waiting for a new background transition. `applyDeferredAppUpdateInstall` re-registers via `scheduleDeferredAppUpdateInstall`, but the default `onNextBackground` immediately invokes the callback when `AppState.currentState` is already `background`; re-arm this path only for a distinct future background transition (and preserve the pending install until then).

✅ Resolved in 63fe6d1eb495c4f54a77ac14f3b6ee2e24b7f618

🔴 **Critical** `updates/app-updates.ts:292`

Automatic rollback checks call `installAppUpdate`, which reloads the runtime even when `flushPendingWrites()` fails, permanently discarding unsaved drafts or outbox mutations. The “user explicitly requested” bypass in `installAppUpdate` does not apply to this rollback path; make rollback abort/re-arm on flush failure like deferred installs, or restrict this bypass to explicit installs.

✅ Resolved in 63fe6d1eb495c4f54a77ac14f3b6ee2e24b7f618

### Prompt and background reload race **High Severity** `armDeferredAppUpdateInstall` now registers the background restart before any prompt, and accepting Install Now in `promptDeferredAppUpdateInstall` calls `installAppUpdate` without canceling that listener or taking an install lock. `applyDeferredAppUpdateInstall` also never checks whether a foreground install is already running. Backgrounding during the alert or during `flushPendingWrites` after Install Now can invoke a second `reloadAsync`, which is the same teardown class this change is trying to avoid. The old prompt-first flow only armed background after a decline, so Install Now could not overlap.
Additional Locations (2) - [`apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L295-L307`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/430aa8918ca66b3166006953a6218150272ce52e/apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L295-L307) - [`apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L334-L352`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/430aa8918ca66b3166006953a6218150272ce52e/apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L334-L352)
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 430aa8918ca66b3166006953a6218150272ce52e. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟠 **High** `updates/app-updates.ts:321`

Accepting “Install Now” while `applyDeferredAppUpdateInstall` is flushing can start a second `flushPendingWrites()` and `reloadAsync()` concurrently, causing duplicate runtime teardowns. `promptDeferredAppUpdateInstall` does not claim or clear `deferral.pendingInstall` before its await, so both paths proceed; add a shared install-in-progress guard that is claimed before either restart sequence awaits.

✅ Resolved in 23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497

### Outbox flush skips queued writes **High Severity** `defaultFlushPendingWrites` only awaits `flushThreadOutboxWrites`, which tracks storage `inFlightWrites`. Outbox `enqueue` publishes to the atom first and only later runs `storage.write` on the manager `mutationQueue`, so a restart can tear down JS while a queued message is still only in memory and never reaches disk.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/mobile/src/state/thread-outbox-storage.ts#L24-L28`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/e3079761c6b85227424ecad764f523b86db879bf/apps/mobile/src/state/thread-outbox-storage.ts#L24-L28)
 
Triggered by learned rule: Mobile outbox optimistic publish: confirm before drain, rollback by reference, re-read after await Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e3079761c6b85227424ecad764f523b86db879bf. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `updates/app-updates.ts:364`

When the app is backgrounded before `import("react-native")` resolves, `defaultOnNextBackground` registers its listener too late and misses that transition, so `pendingInstall` remains set and the downloaded update is not applied until another backgrounding event. Check `AppState.currentState` after registering the listener and apply immediately when it is already `"background"`.

✅ Resolved in 23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497

🟠 **High** `lib/atomic-file.ts:10`

Concurrent writes to the same destination reuse `${file.name}.tmp`, so one call can move or overwrite the other call’s temporary contents and the other call can then fail because its temp path no longer exists. This is reachable when composer persistence runs alongside `clearComposerDraftsEnvironment`; use a unique temp name per write or serialize writes for each destination.

✅ Resolved in 23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497

### Outbox flush misses queued writes **High Severity** `flushThreadOutboxWrites` only waits on storage `inFlightWrites`, but outbox `enqueue` publishes to the atom first and starts `storage.write` only after the manager `mutationQueue`. An update restart can run flush while a queued message is still waiting on that queue, so the durable write never lands and the in-memory entry dies with the reload.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L313-L318`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/e03b521fd42752b67f9e7525672eeea7a6901634/apps/mobile/src/features/updates/app-updates.ts#L313-L318)
 
Triggered by learned rule: Mobile outbox optimistic publish: confirm before drain, rollback by reference, re-read after await Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e03b521fd42752b67f9e7525672eeea7a6901634. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

🟡 **Medium** `updates/app-updates.ts:249`

When a prompt-mode check (e.g. launch or foreground) is already in flight and the user then triggers the manual check with `applyMode: "immediate"`, the manual call ignores its own `applyMode` and follows the original prompt flow instead. The user's explicit install request can surface a confirmation prompt or defer the update to the next backgrounding. This happens because `runAppUpdateCheck` sees `appUpdateCheckInFlight` set and calls `observeAppUpdateCheck`, which awaits the already-running `performAppUpdateCheck` that captured the first caller's `applyMode`. Consider carrying the caller's `applyMode` into `observeAppUpdateCheck` so a later `"immediate"` request can escalate the in-flight operation.

✅ Resolved in 23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497

🟠 **High** `updates/app-updates.ts:277`

The deferred install path calls `installAppUpdate` on background, but the `flushPendingWrites()` await completes before `reloadAsync()` without rechecking the app's foreground/background state. If the user returns the app to the foreground while the flush is in progress, `reloadAsync()` executes with native surfaces mounted again — exactly the crash condition the background deferral was meant to avoid. Consider verifying the app is still backgrounded after the flush resolves before proceeding with the reload.

✅ Resolved in e3079761c6b85227424ecad764f523b86db879bf

🟠 **High** `state/use-composer-drafts.ts:216`

`flushComposerDrafts` suppresses all persistence errors because it delegates to `savePersistedComposerDrafts`, which catches every failure and logs a warning. As a result, when the forced write fails (e.g., storage is unavailable), `flushComposerDrafts` still resolves successfully, so the caller proceeds to tear down the JS runtime and the unsaved in-memory draft is lost. Consider catching the error in the flush path and rethrowing it so a failed flush prevents the restart.
<details>
<summary>Also found in 1 other location(s)</summary>

`docs/user/updating.md:77`

> The documentation promises that choosing **Later** is safe and that drafts and queued messages are saved before every restart. However, `installAppUpdate` treats `flushPendingWrites` as best-effort, swallows failures via `settlePromise`, and proceeds to `reloadAsync`; `defaultFlushPendingWrites` also uses `Promise.allSettled`. A persistence failure can therefore still restart the app with unsaved content, so this assurance may cause users to postpone or install an update under a false data-safety guarantee. Qualify the guarantee or make restart conditional on successful persistence.

</details>

✅ Resolved in 23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497

🟠 **High** `state/use-composer-drafts.ts:216`

`flushComposerDrafts` can return while a new debounced write is still pending, losing draft state across an OTA restart. If `persistTimer` is set (a debounce is pending) it writes the current snapshot, but a user can edit during that queued write. The edit calls `schedulePersistComposerDrafts`, setting a new `persistTimer` that is never cleared or awaited before `flushComposerDrafts` returns. Consider re-checking `persistTimer` after the awaited save and looping until no new debounce is scheduled.

✅ Resolved in 23f2cb8b3c531fab42f29ac0265124cde3524497

title: fix: avoid stale Live Activities when publishing is disabled
body:
## Problem

When agent-activity publishing is disabled on an environment (the `cloud-publish-agent-activity` opt-in was never enabled, e.g. after a plain managed `t3 connect link`), the mobile app still seeds a Live Activity with status **Connecting** when starting work from the phone. No update ever arrives to repaint or end it, so the card sits on Connecting until the relay's freshly-armed grace expires and kills it. Nothing above debug level hints at why.

## Changes

**Expose publishing state as a descriptor capability** so clients can tell whether updates will ever come, on every path the descriptor flows through (`/.well-known/t3/environment`, server config over websocket, relay environment status):

- `packages/contracts`: new optional `capabilities.agentActivityPublishing` on `ExecutionEnvironmentDescriptor`. Optional so newer clients tolerate older servers.
- `apps/server`: `readAgentActivityPublishingActive` in `cloud/config.ts` reports true only when the publish opt-in secret is enabled **and** the relay link credentials exist — mirroring the per-publish gate in `AgentAwarenessRelay`, so the descriptor never advertises publishing the publisher would skip. `ServerEnvironment.getDescriptor` computes the capability per read (the toggle flips at runtime via `t3 connect publish` / the settings toggle, so it must not be baked in at startup). The three identical `value === "true"` predicates are consolidated into one canonical helper.

**Skip the doomed seed on mobile:**

- `armAgentAwarenessLiveActivityForLocalWork` now takes the target `environmentId` and skips seeding when that environment explicitly reports `agentActivityPublishing: false`. Absent capability (older server) still arms — those servers may well be publishing, so only an explicit false skips.

## Tests

- `ServerEnvironment.test.ts`: capability defaults to false; opt-in alone is not enough without link credentials; the same service instance reflects a runtime flip without restart. The noop-filesystem failure test now stubs `makeDirectory`/`chmod` for the secret store the layer builds.
- `remoteRegistration.test.ts`: arming is skipped for explicitly non-publishing environments and preserved for publishing/pre-capability ones. The new state-module imports are mocked to keep expo-native code out of the node test graph.

## Notes

- The phone evaluates the capability from its cached server config (refreshed on reconnect). Toggling publishing off while an app holds a config can still seed one card; the relay's existing 2-minute grace ends it, same as today.

title: fix(web): align every titlebar control cluster on one shared inset
body:
Titlebar geometry polish so the sidebar trigger, the thread view's layout controls, and the pull requests page's panel toggle all read as one family. Found while dogfooding on the orchestrator branch (#2829); ported here so both lineages agree.

## What changed

- **Icon size**: the layout-control icons were hard-coded `size-3.5` while the sidebar trigger (Button `size="icon"` default) and the PR page refresh icon render `size-4` — the two ends of the titlebar sat a pixel apart on every edge. All layout-control icons now use `size-4`.
- **Trigger inset symmetry**: the right cluster carries `mr-px` (border compensation for anchoring inside the panel frame); the sidebar trigger now mirrors it with `ml-px` so both clusters sit one shared inset off their edges.
- **Sheet-mode jump**: the sheet overlays from the viewport top, but its tab bar used the compact `spacing(11)` row, re-centering the controls 4px higher than their closed-state titlebar position on every open. The sheet tab bar now keeps `--workspace-topbar-height`, and its layout-controls slot carries the `mr-px` so the horizontal inset matches too.
- **PR page toggle**: the panel toggle previously moved between an in-flow header slot (closed) and an absolute corner anchor (open). It now stays mounted at the fixed `workspace-titlebar-controls` inset in both states — the same anchor as the thread view — with a per-breakpoint footprint reserve in the list header so refresh never slides underneath it.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @t3tools/web typecheck` clean
- Web suite: 2429/2429 passing

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CSS and layout-only changes to titlebar positioning and icon sizing; no auth, data, or API behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Titlebar geometry** is unified so sidebar trigger, thread layout controls, and PR page panel toggle read as one family and stop jumping on panel open/close.
> 
> Layout-control icons move from `size-3.5` to **`size-4`** to match the sidebar trigger and PR refresh. The sidebar trigger wrapper gains **`ml-px`** to mirror the right cluster’s **`mr-px`**. In **sheet** mode, the right-panel tab bar no longer forces a shorter topbar height (removed compact `spacing(11)` override), and sheet layout controls are wrapped with **`mr-px`** so horizontal inset matches the closed titlebar. On **pull requests**, panel toggles stay on the fixed **`workspace-titlebar-controls`** anchor whenever PRs are supported (not only when the panel is open); the list header uses a footprint **spacer** instead of in-flow toggle controls when the panel is closed so refresh doesn’t slide under the fixed toggle.

### PR toggle overlaps refresh on safe-area **Medium Severity** The panel toggle is now absolutely placed with `workspace-titlebar-controls`, whose right inset includes `safe-area-inset-right`, but the closed-state header spacer and `px-3`/`px-5` padding do not. On notched or landscape devices with a non-zero safe area, that shifts the toggle left over the refresh control. The overlay is `z-50`, so refresh can stop receiving clicks. Chat’s closed header already pads with the same safe-area token, which is why the thread view does not hit this.
Additional Locations (1) - [`apps/web/src/routes/_chat.pull-requests.tsx#L1829-L1838`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/62badc9ec42a9cefdaf8a3cc77892dc719be810c/apps/web/src/routes/_chat.pull-requests.tsx#L1829-L1838)
